<style>

  :root{--navy:#0f1f3d;--bi3:#1a56db;--bi3-lt:#93c5fd;--bi3-bg:#eff6ff;--bi3-dk:#1e40af;--green:#16a34a;--amber:#d97706;--red:#dc2626;--slate:#64748b;--white:#ffffff;--py:#3b82f6;--pseudo:#8b5cf6;}
  *{box-sizing:border-box;margin:0;padding:0;}

  .lesson-hero-pills{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}

  /* PROGRESS STRIP */

  .bi3-progress-inner{display:flex!important;flex-direction:row!important;flex-wrap:nowrap!important;align-items:center!important;gap:0!important;width:max-content!important;min-width:100%!important;}
  .prog-step{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-step-link{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;text-decoration:none!important;cursor:pointer!important;}
  .prog-step-link:hover .prog-dot{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border-color:var(--bi3)!important;}

  .prog-dot.done{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border:2px solid var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-label{font-size:8px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;line-height:1.2!important;white-space:nowrap!important;}
  .prog-label.active-label{color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-arrow{flex:1 0 4px!important;height:2px!important;background:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:18px!important;min-width:4px!important;max-width:16px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}

  /* MAIN */
  .lesson-main{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;padding:40px 24px 80px;}

  .hook-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .hook-box p{font-size:15px!important;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:0!important;}

  /* LESSON SECTIONS */
  .lesson-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .lesson-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}

  .lesson-section ul,.lesson-section ol{padding-left:20px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section li{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .lesson-section code{background:#eef2ff;color:#1e3a8a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e3a8a!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}

  /* DUAL CODE PANEL */
  .code-panel-wrap{margin:20px 0;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;}
  .code-panel-tabs{display:flex;background:#1e293b;}
  .code-tab{padding:8px 16px;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;border:none;background:transparent;letter-spacing:.04em;transition:background .15s;font-family:inherit;}

  .py-fn{color:#6ee7b7!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#6ee7b7!important;}

  .py-op{color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;}
  .ps-kw{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .ps-op{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .ps-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .ps-str{color:#86efac!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#86efac!important;}
  .ps-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .ps-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* CALLOUTS */
  .callout-exam{background:#fffbeb;border:1px solid #fcd34d;border-left:4px solid var(--amber);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}

  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}

  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}

  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}

  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}

  <div class="lesson-main">

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Explain why collaboration produces better programs than working alone</span></li>
        <li><span>Describe pair programming and the driver and navigator roles</span></li>
        <li><span>List the practices of an effective collaborative team, including consensus and clear communication</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain how diverse perspectives reduce blind spots and bias in a program</span></li>
        <li><span>Give and receive constructive feedback that improves a program without discouraging a teammate</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span>Big Idea 1 (Creative Development) is 10 to 13 percent of the AP CSP exam, and collaboration questions are quick, reliable points. They also describe exactly how you will work during the Create Performance Task, so this lesson pays off twice.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>Two students are each assigned the same program. One works alone and finishes fast, but ships a bug that only shows up for left-handed users, something they never thought to consider. The other pairs up, talks through the plan out loud, and a teammate catches the blind spot in the first ten minutes. Which program is more likely to actually work for everyone, and why does talking it through help so much?</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Why Collaborate at All</h2>
      <p><strong>Collaboration</strong> is people working together to develop a program. The AP CSP framework is blunt about the payoff: collaboration that uses different perspectives, skills, and backgrounds tends to produce a <strong>better</strong> computing solution than working alone. That is not a motivational slogan, it is a claim you will be tested on. A single developer has a single point of view, and that view has gaps. More people means more ideas considered, more errors caught early, and a program that works for a wider range of users.</p>
      <p>The reason diverse teams do better is <strong>blind spots</strong>. Every developer brings assumptions about who will use the program and how. When everyone on a team shares the same background, they tend to share the same blind spots, so nobody notices what is missing. A team with varied experiences is far more likely to have someone ask the question no one else thought of, which is how you avoid shipping a program that quietly fails for some group of users.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>When a question asks why a program benefits from collaboration, the strongest answer is almost always about <strong>diverse perspectives catching problems a single person would miss</strong>, not simply "the work gets done faster." Speed is a possible side effect; better quality and fewer blind spots is the point.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Pair Programming: Driver and Navigator</h2>
      <p><strong>Pair programming</strong> is a specific collaboration technique in which two programmers share one computer and one program. It is not two people typing on two machines. The roles are defined:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>The <strong>driver</strong> controls the keyboard and writes the code, focusing on the line right in front of them.</li>
        <li>The <strong>navigator</strong> watches, thinks ahead, spots errors, and keeps the bigger goal in view.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>The pair <strong>switches roles regularly</strong> so both people stay engaged and both understand the whole program. The value is continuous review: the navigator catches a mistake as it is typed instead of hours later during testing. Two sets of eyes on the same code, in real time, is why pairs often produce fewer bugs even though only one person is typing.</p>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">During pair programming, a teammate is watching the code being typed, thinking about the next step, and pointing out a likely error. Which role are they playing?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-collab-1-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-collab-1','A','B','mc-collab-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> Driver</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-collab-1','B','B','mc-collab-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> Navigator</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-collab-1','C','B','mc-collab-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> Manager</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-collab-1','D','B','mc-collab-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> Tester</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-collab-1-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What Effective Teams Actually Do</h2>
      <p>Collaboration only helps if the team collaborates well. The framework and the exam expect you to recognize the habits of an effective team:</p>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Practice</th>
<th>What it means</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Clear communication</strong></td>
<td>Explaining ideas so teammates understand, and listening to make sure you understood them.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Consensus building</strong></td>
<td>Working toward a decision the whole team can support, rather than one person overriding everyone.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Conflict resolution</strong></td>
<td>Handling disagreement about the code or the plan without it becoming personal.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Constructive feedback</strong></td>
<td>Critiquing the work, not the person, and offering a specific improvement.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Inclusion of perspectives</strong></td>
<td>Actively inviting every teammate's input, especially the quiet or dissenting voice.</td>
</tr>
      </table>
      <p>Notice the pattern: every one of these is about the <strong>process of working together</strong>, not about who is the best coder. A team of strong programmers who will not listen to each other usually loses to an average team that communicates and reaches consensus.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>"Collaboration means splitting the work so everyone codes a separate piece alone and you staple it together at the end." That is division of labor, and it can be part of a project, but it is not what the exam means by effective collaboration. The tested idea is people <strong>exchanging perspectives and reviewing each other's work</strong>, not silently working in parallel and merging at the deadline.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Feedback That Helps</h2>
      <p>Getting and using feedback is part of collaboration. Good feedback is <strong>specific</strong> and <strong>about the work</strong>. "This is bad" helps no one; "the loop repeats one time too many, so the last item gets skipped" tells the teammate exactly what to fix. When you receive feedback, the collaborative move is to treat it as information about the program, not an attack on you, and to test whether the suggestion actually improves the result.</p>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A teammate says your function works but is hard to read, and suggests renaming the variables and adding a comment. The most collaborative response is to:</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-collab-2-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-collab-2','A','C','mc-collab-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> Reject it, since the function already works</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-collab-2','B','C','mc-collab-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> Take offense and defend the original code</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-collab-2','C','C','mc-collab-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> Consider the suggestion and apply the changes that make the program clearer</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-collab-2','D','C','mc-collab-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> Rewrite the whole program from scratch alone</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-collab-2-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How This Shows Up on the Create Performance Task</h2>
      <p>The Create Performance Task is completed <strong>individually</strong> under current AP rules, so you submit your own program and written responses. Collaboration still matters in two ways the exam cares about. First, you are allowed to <strong>discuss ideas and get feedback</strong> from classmates and your teacher while you build, as long as the program and the writing are your own. Using a navigator-style partner to talk through your plan and catch bugs early is exactly the kind of collaboration that improves a program. Second, the multiple-choice section tests collaboration concepts directly, so the vocabulary here (pair programming, driver and navigator, consensus, diverse perspectives) is worth points even though the Create Task itself is solo.</p>
    </div>

      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q1">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 1 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Concept</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Predict the best answer before reading the options.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A software team is deciding how to build a new app. Which situation best illustrates the specific benefit that collaboration is expected to provide, according to the AP CSP framework?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q1-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','A','A','q1-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Team members with different backgrounds each raise a user need the others had not considered, and the design changes to include it</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','B','A','q1-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> The fastest programmer writes all the code so the app is finished sooner</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','C','A','q1-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Each member writes one function alone and the pieces are combined the night before the deadline</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','D','A','q1-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> The team lead makes every decision so there is never any disagreement</button>
</div>
<div id="q1-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. The tested benefit of collaboration is that diverse perspectives surface needs and problems a single developer would miss, producing a better solution.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Speed from one strong coder is not the framework's point, and a single perspective is exactly the blind-spot risk collaboration is meant to reduce.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Working alone in parallel and merging at the deadline is division of labor, not the perspective-sharing that the framework credits.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Removing all disagreement by having one person decide throws away the diverse input that makes collaboration valuable.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q2">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 2 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Roles</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Name the driver's job before you look.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>Two students are pair programming. Which statement about their roles is correct?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q2-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','A','B','q2-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Both students type on separate keyboards and merge their code at the end</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','B','B','q2-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> The driver writes the code while the navigator reviews it and thinks ahead, and they switch roles regularly</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','C','B','q2-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> The navigator writes the code while the driver waits for instructions</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','D','B','q2-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> The driver plans the whole program first, then the navigator implements it without discussion</button>
</div>
<div id="q2-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Pair programming uses one computer and one program, not two separate keyboards.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. The driver types, the navigator reviews and looks ahead, and the pair switches roles so both stay engaged and informed.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The roles are reversed here. The driver writes the code; the navigator reviews and thinks ahead.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Pair programming is continuous shared work with discussion, not a silent hand-off between planner and implementer.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q3">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 3 of 6<span class="diff-tag">I and II only style</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Decide which statements are true before matching to an option.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>Consider these claims about effective collaborative teams:</p></div>
        <ul class="mcq-roman">
          <li>
<strong>I.</strong> Reaching consensus means the team works toward a decision everyone can support.</li>
          <li>
<strong>II.</strong> Constructive feedback focuses on improving the work rather than criticizing the person.</li>
          <li>
<strong>III.</strong> The most effective teams avoid all disagreement by letting the strongest coder decide.</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q3-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','A','C','q3-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> I only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','B','C','q3-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> II and III only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','C','C','q3-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> I and II only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','D','C','q3-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> I, II, and III</button>
</div>
<div id="q3-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement II is also true; constructive feedback is a core practice of effective teams.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement III is false, and statement I is true, so this pairing cannot be right.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. I and II describe effective collaboration. III is false: silencing disagreement discards the diverse input that makes teams effective.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement III is false, so not all three can be correct.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q4">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 4 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Spot the problem</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Find the weak point in the team's process first.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A team of four has one member who quietly disagrees with the design but is never asked for input, so the team proceeds without hearing the objection. Which collaboration practice is the team failing to apply?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q4-options">
          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','A','D','q4-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Version control</button>
          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','B','D','q4-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> Syntax checking</button>
          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','C','D','q4-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Writing faster code</button>
          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','D','D','q4-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> Inclusion of all team members' perspectives</button>
        </div>
        <div id="q4-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Version control is a tool for managing code changes, not the practice being described here.</div>
        <div id="q4-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Syntax checking is about code correctness, not about how the team includes its members.</div>
        <div id="q4-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Speed of coding is unrelated to the failure, which is about not hearing a team member.</div>
        <div id="q4-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Effective teams actively invite every member's perspective, especially a dissenting one. Ignoring the quiet member fails inclusion.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q5">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 5 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Best choice</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Predict the most collaborative action first.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>During development, two teammates disagree about which of two working approaches to use. Which action best reflects effective collaboration?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q5-options">
          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','A','A','q5-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> The teammates discuss the trade-offs, weigh them against the program's goal, and reach a decision together</button>
          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','B','A','q5-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> Whichever teammate is louder gets their way so the team can move on</button>
          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','C','A','q5-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> They split the program and each secretly builds their own version to avoid the conflict</button>
          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','D','A','q5-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> They abandon both approaches and ask the teacher to decide everything</button>
        </div>
        <div id="q5-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Discussing trade-offs against the program's goal and deciding together is exactly consensus building and conflict resolution.</div>
        <div id="q5-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Deciding by who is loudest ignores the trade-offs and undermines consensus.</div>
        <div id="q5-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Secretly building rival versions avoids collaboration rather than practicing it.</div>
        <div id="q5-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Offloading every decision to the teacher skips the team's responsibility to resolve the disagreement.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q6">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 6 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Application</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Predict what a diverse team changes about the outcome.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A team building a voice assistant is made up entirely of people who speak the same dialect and grew up in the same region. After release, users with other accents report the assistant often fails to understand them. How does this outcome most directly illustrate a collaboration concept from the framework?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q6-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','A','B','q6-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> It shows the program needed faster hardware</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','B','B','q6-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> It shows a lack of diverse perspectives on the team led to a blind spot that harmed some users</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','C','B','q6-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> It shows pair programming was not used during coding</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','D','B','q6-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> It shows the team should have written more comments in the code</button>
</div>
<div id="q6-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The failure is about whose needs were considered, not about hardware speed.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. A team sharing one background shared one blind spot. Diverse perspectives would more likely have surfaced the accent issue before release.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Pair programming is a technique, but the root cause here is the team's lack of diverse perspectives, not the coding method.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Comments improve readability for developers but would not have caught a missing user need.</div>
      </div>

    shuffle(opts);
    el.opts.innerHTML="";
    var letters=["A","B","C","D"];
    opts.forEach(function(p,pos){
      var b=document.createElement('button');
      b.className="tr-opt"; b.type="button";
      b.innerHTML='<span class="ltr">'+letters[pos]+'</span><span>'+esc(p.o.t)+'</span>';
      b.onclick=function(){ choose(b, p.o, r); };
      el.opts.appendChild(b);
    });
  }

  function esc(s){ return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g,function(c){return {'&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"'}[c];}); }

  function choose(btn, opt, r){
    if(answered) return;
    answered=true;
    var buttons=el.opts.querySelectorAll('.tr-opt');
    buttons.forEach(function(b){ b.disabled=true; });
    if(opt.ok){
      btn.classList.add('correct');
      var gain=10 + streak*2;
      score+=gain; streak++;
      el.fb.className="tr-fb good show";
      el.fb.innerHTML='<b>+'+gain+' points.</b> '+esc(r.good);
    } else {
      btn.classList.add('wrong');
      streak=0;
      buttons.forEach(function(b){
        var txt=b.querySelector('span:last-child').textContent;
        var match=r.opts.filter(function(o){return o.ok;})[0];
        if(txt===match.t) b.classList.add('correct');
      });
      el.fb.className="tr-fb bad show";
      el.fb.innerHTML='<b>Not the best move.</b> '+esc(r.bad);
    }
    el.score.textContent=score;
    el.streak.textContent=streak;
    el.progbar.style.width=Math.round(((idx+1)/TOTAL)*100)+"%";
    el.nextwrap.classList.remove('tr-hidden');
  }

  el.next.onclick=function(){
    if(!answered) return;
    idx++;
    if(idx>=TOTAL) end();
    else render();
  };

  function end(){
    el.play.classList.add('tr-hidden');
    el.endcard.classList.remove('tr-hidden');
    el.final.textContent=score;
    var maxBase=TOTAL*10;
    var pct=score/maxBase;
    var title, msg;
    if(pct>=1.0){ title="Dream team!"; msg="Perfect run. You picked the strongest collaborative move every round. Collaboration like this consistently produces better programs than working alone."; }
    else if(pct>=0.75){ title="Great teammate"; msg="Strong collaboration instincts. Keep pairing, swapping roles, and inviting diverse perspectives to make every program better."; }
    else if(pct>=0.4){ title="Getting in sync"; msg="Solid start. Remember: pair programming, constructive feedback, consensus, and diverse voices are what make teamwork beat solo work."; }
    else { title="Team huddle"; msg="Collaboration is a skill. Focus on communicating clearly, sharing roles, and welcoming feedback, and your programs will improve fast."; }
    el.endtitle.textContent=title;
    el.endmsg.textContent=msg;
    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsGameScore',{detail:{value:score}}));
  }

  el.again.onclick=start;

  start();
})();
</script>

  /* CALLOUTS */

  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */

  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}

  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}

  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}

  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}

  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}

  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}

  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .vt-line{display:block;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;white-space:pre;}

  .vt-question{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-options{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-btn{padding:12px;border-radius:9px;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);cursor:pointer;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;font-family:monospace;transition:all .15s;}

  .vt-btn.w{border-color:#f87171;background:rgba(248,113,113,.15);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .vt-btn.rv{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.08);}
  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}
  .vt-fb.w{background:rgba(248,113,113,.1);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;display:block;}
  .vt-next{display:none;width:100%;padding:12px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>

        <li><span>Distinguish logic, syntax, run-time, and overflow errors by how each one shows up</span></li>

        <li><span>Design test cases that include typical, boundary, and invalid inputs to expose errors</span></li>
        <li><span>Apply debugging strategies such as hand-tracing, adding display statements, and isolating sections of code</span></li>

    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span>Big Idea 1 (Creative Development) is 10 to 13 percent of the AP CSP exam, and error-and-testing questions are among the most frequent. </div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>A program that calculates the average of a class quiz runs with no red error messages, prints a clean number, and looks finished. But when a student scores a perfect 100 on every quiz, the program reports an average of 91. Nothing crashed, nothing was underlined in red, and yet the answer is wrong. What kind of error is this, and what single test case would have caught it before the program shipped?</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Four Kinds of Errors</h2>
      <p>An <strong>error</strong> is any flaw that keeps a program from doing what it should. The AP CSP framework names four types, and the exam expects you to tell them apart by <strong>how they show up</strong>, not just by their definitions. The single most useful question to ask is: <em>does the program still run?</em></p>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Error type</th>
<th>Does it run?</th>
<th>Example</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Syntax error</strong></td>
<td>No. It violates the rules of the language, so the program will not run at all.</td>
<td>A missing quotation mark or an unmatched parenthesis, such as <code>DISPLAY("hi)</code>
</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Logic error</strong></td>
<td>Yes. It runs, but produces incorrect or unintended output.</td>
<td>Using <code>+</code> where you meant <code>*</code>, so the total is wrong but no error is shown</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Run-time error</strong></td>
<td>It starts, then fails while running.</td>
<td>Dividing by zero, or reading a list value that does not exist</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Overflow error</strong></td>
<td>It runs, then breaks or wraps.</td>
<td>A number grows too large to fit in the space allotted to represent it</td>
</tr>
      </table>
      <p>Read that table carefully. A <strong>syntax error</strong> is caught before the program even starts because the language cannot understand it. A <strong>logic error</strong> is the sneakiest because everything looks fine, the program runs to completion, and only the <em>answer</em> is wrong. A <strong>run-time error</strong> happens partway through, often because of a specific input like a zero or a missing value. An <strong>overflow error</strong> is a special case where a value is simply too big for the number of bits allotted to store it.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>If a program <strong>runs and finishes but the output is wrong</strong>, the answer is almost always a <strong>logic error</strong>. If the program <strong>will not run at all</strong>, it is a <strong>syntax error</strong>. If it <strong>runs for a while and then stops</strong>, look for a <strong>run-time error</strong> tied to a specific input. Anchor your choice to whether and when the program runs.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A program to find the largest of three numbers runs completely and prints a result every time, but when the largest value is the last one entered, it prints the wrong number. What type of error is this?</div>

        </div>

      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Testing: Trying to Break Your Own Program</h2>
      <p><strong>Testing</strong> is running a program with a variety of inputs to find errors and check that it behaves correctly. The goal is not to confirm that the program works on the one input you already tried; it is to actively hunt for the input that makes it fail. Good testing covers three kinds of input:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Typical inputs</strong>, the ordinary values a user is expected to enter, to confirm normal behavior.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Boundary (edge) cases</strong>, the extremes and just-past-extremes such as zero, an empty list, a maximum value, or the very first and very last items. Most bugs hide here.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Invalid inputs</strong>, values the program should reject, such as a letter where a number is expected or a negative age, to check that the program handles bad data gracefully.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>The quiz-average program from the hook is a perfect example: it passed on a mix of scores but failed on the boundary case of all perfect scores. A single well-chosen <strong>edge case</strong> would have exposed the logic error immediately.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>"The program worked when I ran it, so it is correct." Running a program once with one friendly input is not testing. A program can pass every typical case and still fail on an empty list, a zero, or the last element of a range. If a question offers "test it with one normal input" versus "test it with typical, boundary, and invalid inputs," the thorough option is the right one.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Debugging: Finding and Fixing the Problem</h2>
      <p><strong>Debugging</strong> is the process of finding and correcting errors. Testing tells you <em>that</em> something is wrong; debugging is how you locate <em>where</em> and fix it. The framework expects you to know several concrete strategies, not just the word "debug":</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Hand-tracing</strong> (tracing code by hand): stepping through the program line by line on paper, tracking each variable's value, to see where reality diverges from what you expected.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Adding display or print statements</strong> to reveal intermediate values while the program runs, so you can watch a variable change and spot the moment it goes wrong.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Testing sections in isolation</strong>: running one procedure or block by itself, apart from the rest, to confirm that piece works before trusting the whole.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Commenting out code</strong> to temporarily remove a suspect section and see whether the problem disappears, which narrows down where the bug lives.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Studying the error message</strong>: a run-time or syntax error usually reports a line number and a description that points you straight at the trouble.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>Consider a loop that is supposed to add up a list but reports a total that is always one item short:</p>
      <pre>total <- 0
FOR EACH n IN [3, 5, 8]
{
  total <- n
}
DISPLAY(total)</pre>
      <p>Hand-tracing exposes the bug at once: each pass <strong>replaces</strong> <code>total</code> instead of adding to it, so the program prints 8 rather than 16. The fix is <code>total <- total + n</code>. This is a classic <strong>logic error</strong>, invisible until you trace the values, and a display statement inside the loop would have made it obvious.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>Documentation and collaboration are debugging aids, not just nice-to-haves. Clear <strong>comments</strong> and a teammate reviewing your code (a navigator, from Topic 1.1) make errors easier to find because a second reader with fresh eyes catches assumptions the author cannot see. Expect the exam to credit "add a comment / get a second reader" as a legitimate error-reduction strategy.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">You suspect a specific loop is producing wrong values, but the program runs without crashing. Which debugging strategy most directly lets you watch the loop's variable change on each pass?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-error-2-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-error-2','A','B','mc-error-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> Rewrite the entire program from scratch</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-error-2','B','B','mc-error-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> Add a display statement inside the loop to print the variable each pass</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-error-2','C','B','mc-error-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> Increase the size of the input list</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-error-2','D','B','mc-error-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> Delete the loop and ignore the feature</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-error-2-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How This Shows Up on the Create Performance Task</h2>
      <p>The Create Performance Task is completed <strong>individually</strong> under current AP rules, so the program and the written responses must be your own. Topic 1.4 is central to it. Your program must include a <strong>call to a student-developed procedure</strong>, and the written responses ask you to describe how that procedure works and how you know your program behaves correctly. That is a testing-and-debugging story.</p>
      <p>Specifically, you should <strong>test your program with a variety of inputs</strong> (including edge cases such as empty input, the smallest and largest values, and invalid entries) and be ready to explain in writing how you identified and corrected errors, or how the program handles unexpected behavior. Reviewers reward responses that show you traced or tested the program rather than just claiming it works. When you describe your procedure and the two calls that produce different results, you are demonstrating exactly the testing thinking this lesson teaches. Keep clear comments in your code so your written explanation matches what the program actually does.</p>

        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A programmer writes a line of code but forgets to close a set of parentheses. When they try to run the program, it will not start at all and no output is produced. Which type of error is this?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q1-options">
          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','A','C','q1-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Logic error</button>

          <button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','C','C','q1-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Syntax error</button>

</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Trace the loop by hand and predict what prints before reading the choices.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>The procedure below is intended to return the sum of the numbers in the list. Study it, then choose the best description of the error.</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-code"><pre>PROCEDURE sumList(nums)
{
  total <- 0
  FOR EACH n IN nums
  {
    total <- n
  }
  RETURN total
}</pre></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q2-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','A','D','q2-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> A syntax error that stops the procedure from running</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','B','D','q2-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> A run-time error that occurs only when the list is empty</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','C','D','q2-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> An overflow error caused by adding numbers that are too large</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','D','D','q2-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> A logic error: the loop replaces total each pass instead of accumulating, so it returns the last value, not the sum</button>
</div>
<div id="q2-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The pseudocode is valid and would run; nothing here violates the language rules.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The procedure runs fine on a non-empty list; it simply returns the wrong number. It does not crash.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Nothing here concerns a value too large for its space; the flaw is in how total is updated.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Writing total <- n overwrites the running total each pass, so the procedure returns the final element instead of the sum. The fix is total <- total + n. The program runs but is wrong, which is a logic error.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q3">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 3 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Testing</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Predict which single input is most likely to expose a hidden bug.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A student wrote a program that computes the average score of a list of quiz grades and only tested it once, with the list [80, 90, 100], getting a reasonable result. Which additional test case is most likely to reveal a hidden error in the program?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q3-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','A','D','q3-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Another typical list such as [70, 85, 95]</button>

</div>
<div id="q3-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Another ordinary list mostly repeats a case that already passed and is unlikely to expose a boundary bug.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Re-running the identical input gives no new information about the program's behavior.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Reordering the same values usually yields the same average and does not probe a boundary condition.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. An empty list is a boundary case that can trigger a division by zero or other failure the typical inputs never reach. Edge cases expose the most bugs.</div>

        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 4 of 6<span class="diff-tag">I and II only style</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Judge each statement true or false before matching to an option.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>Consider these statements about errors in a program:</p></div>
        <ul class="mcq-roman">
          <li>
<strong>I.</strong> A syntax error prevents a program from running at all.</li>
          <li>
<strong>II.</strong> A logic error can be present in a program that runs to completion and produces output.</li>
          <li>
<strong>III.</strong> A run-time error is always detected before the program begins executing.</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q4-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','A','A','q4-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> I and II only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','B','A','q4-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> I only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','C','A','q4-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> II and III only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','D','A','q4-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> I and III only</button>
</div>
<div id="q4-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. I and II are true. III is false: a run-time error, by definition, occurs while the program is running, not before it starts.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement II is also true; a running program can still contain a logic error.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement III is false, so any option that includes III cannot be correct.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement III is false. A run-time error surfaces during execution, not before it begins.</div>

<div id="q5-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The same input on unchanged code produces the same wrong result and reveals nothing new.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Commenting out sections and printing intermediate values narrows down exactly where a correct value turns into a wrong one, isolating the faulty section.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Adding features increases complexity and makes the existing bug harder, not easier, to find.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Blaming the language is almost never the cause and abandons the systematic debugging that would locate the real error.</div>

        <div class="predict-note">Predict which error type matches a value that is too big to store.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A program repeatedly doubles a whole number stored in a fixed amount of memory. After many doublings the value suddenly becomes negative or wildly incorrect, even though the code and inputs are valid. Which type of error best explains this behavior?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q6-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','A','C','q6-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Syntax error, because the doubling operation is written incorrectly</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','B','C','q6-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> Logic error, because doubling a number is the wrong operation to use</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','C','C','q6-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Overflow error, because the number grew too large for the space allotted to represent it</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','D','C','q6-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> Run-time error, because the program stopped executing at the moment it happened</button>
</div>
<div id="q6-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The code runs correctly for many steps, so it is valid syntax; the problem appears only after the value grows large.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The doubling itself is intended; the failure is about representing the resulting value, not about choosing the wrong operation.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. When a number exceeds the fixed space allotted to store it, the representation breaks and can wrap to a wrong or negative value. That is an overflow error.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The program keeps running and produces a value; it just produces a corrupted one. Nothing here reports a crash.</div>

<div class="bs-game" id="bs-game">
  <div class="bs-card">
    <div class="bs-hero">
      <h1 class="bs-title">🐛 Bug Squasher</h1>
      <p class="bs-sub">AP CSP 1.4 • Identify and correct errors: syntax, logic, runtime, and overflow.</p>
      <p class="bs-how">How to play: read the buggy code, first CLASSIFY the error type, then pick the FIX. Beat the timer and build a streak!</p>
    </div>
    <div class="bs-bar">
      <div class="bs-stat">
<div class="k">Round</div>
<div class="v" id="bs-round">1/10</div>
</div>
      <div class="bs-stat">
<div class="k">Score</div>
<div class="v" id="bs-score">0</div>
</div>
      <div class="bs-stat strk">
<div class="k">Streak</div>
<div class="v" id="bs-streak">0</div>
</div>
