<script>
(function(){
  var ERR = {
    SYN:{tag:'Syntax',   desc:'Breaks the rules of the language'},
    LOG:{tag:'Logic',    desc:'Runs, but the wrong result'},
    RUN:{tag:'Runtime',  desc:'Crashes while running'},
    OVR:{tag:'Overflow', desc:'Value exceeds its allowed range'}
  };
  var ORDER = ['SYN','LOG','RUN','OVR'];

  // Each round: code lines (bug line flagged), correct type, fix options.
  var ROUNDS = [
    {
      code:[['if score > 90',true],['    grade = "A"',false]],
      type:'SYN',
      why:'Missing colon after the condition breaks the language rules, so it never runs.',
      fixes:[
        {t:'Add a colon: <span class="bs-mono">if score > 90:</span>',ok:true},
        {t:'Change to <span class="bs-mono">if score = 90</span>',ok:false},
        {t:'Indent the if statement',ok:false}
      ]
    },
    {
      code:[['count = 0',false],['while count < 5',true],['    count = count + 1',false]],
      type:'SYN',
      why:'The while header needs a colon. A missing colon is a syntax error caught before the code runs.',
      fixes:[
        {t:'Write <span class="bs-mono">while count < 5:</span>',ok:true},
        {t:'Start count at 1',ok:false},
        {t:'Use <span class="bs-mono">count == 5</span>',ok:false}
      ]
    },
    {
      code:[['if password == "open" and admin == "yes"',false],['    unlock()',true]],
      type:'SYN',
      why:'The call to unlock is fine, but print below is missing a paren. Unbalanced parentheses are a syntax error.',
      alt:'print( "Access granted"',
      code2:[['if ok:',false],['    print( "Access granted"',true]],
      fixes:[
        {t:'Close the paren: <span class="bs-mono">print("Access granted")</span>',ok:true},
        {t:'Remove the quotes',ok:false},
        {t:'Use <span class="bs-mono">and</span> instead of <span class="bs-mono">or</span>',ok:false}
      ]
    },
    {
      code:[['// user must be 18 or older',false],['if age > 18:',true],['    allowVote()',false]],
      type:'LOG',
      why:'It runs fine but 18 is wrongly rejected. A wrong comparison operator is a logic error.',
      fixes:[
        {t:'Use <span class="bs-mono">age >= 18</span>',ok:true},
        {t:'Add a colon after 18',ok:false},
        {t:'Use <span class="bs-mono">age < 18</span>',ok:false}
      ]
    },
    {
      code:[['sum = 0',false],['for i in range(1, 5):',true],['    sum = sum + nums[i]',false]],
      type:'LOG',
      why:'range(1,5) skips index 0 and stops at 4, an off-by-one logic error. It runs but sums the wrong items.',
      fixes:[
        {t:'Use <span class="bs-mono">range(0, 5)</span>',ok:true},
        {t:'Change sum to 1',ok:false},
        {t:'Add a colon',ok:false}
      ]
    },
    {
      code:[['// pass only if BOTH tests pass',false],['if test1 or test2:',true],['    pass_student()',false]],
      type:'LOG',
      why:'Using or instead of and lets one passing test through. A boolean operator mixup is a logic error.',
      fixes:[
        {t:'Use <span class="bs-mono">test1 and test2</span>',ok:true},
        {t:'Use <span class="bs-mono">not test1</span>',ok:false},
        {t:'Add parentheses around test1',ok:false}
      ]
    },
    {
      code:[['total = 100',false],['people = 0',false],['share = total / people',true]],
      type:'RUN',
      why:'Dividing by zero crashes the program as it runs. That is a runtime error, not caught until execution.',
      fixes:[
        {t:'Guard: only divide when <span class="bs-mono">people > 0</span>',ok:true},
        {t:'Add a colon after share',ok:false},
        {t:'Change <span class="bs-mono">/</span> to <span class="bs-mono">and</span>',ok:false}
      ]
    },
    {
      code:[['list = [10, 20, 30]',false],['print(list[3])',true]],
      type:'RUN',
      why:'Valid indexes are 0 to 2, so index 3 is out of range and crashes at runtime.',
      fixes:[
        {t:'Access <span class="bs-mono">list[2]</span> (last valid index)',ok:true},
        {t:'Add another comma',ok:false},
        {t:'Use <span class="bs-mono">list = 3</span>',ok:false}
      ]
    },
    {
      code:[['// counter stored in 8 bits (max 255)',false],['counter = 255',false],['counter = counter + 1',true]],
      type:'OVR',
      why:'An 8-bit value maxes at 255, so adding 1 exceeds the range. That is overflow.',
      fixes:[
        {t:'Use more bits or cap the value at 255',ok:true},
        {t:'Add a colon after counter',ok:false},
        {t:'Start counter at 1',ok:false}
      ]
    },
    {
      code:[['// price is a signed 8-bit int (-128..127)',false],['price = 120',false],['price = price + 50',true]],
      type:'OVR',
      why:'127 is the max for a signed 8-bit int, so 170 overflows past the range and wraps around.',
      fixes:[
        {t:'Store price in a larger integer type',ok:true},
        {t:'Change <span class="bs-mono">+</span> to <span class="bs-mono">==</span>',ok:false},
        {t:'Add a colon after price',ok:false}
      ]
    }
  ];

  var TOTAL = ROUNDS.length;
  var TIME = 16; // seconds per round
  var body = document.getElementById('bs-body');
  var elRound = document.getElementById('bs-round');
  var elScore = document.getElementById('bs-score');
  var elStreak = document.getElementById('bs-streak');

  var idx, score, streak, phase, timeLeft, timer, classifyOk, finalScore;

  function reset(){
    idx = 0; score = 0; streak = 0; finalScore = 0;
    updateBar();
    renderRound();
  }

  function updateBar(){
    elRound.textContent = Math.min(idx+1, TOTAL) + '/' + TOTAL;
    elScore.textContent = score;
    elStreak.textContent = streak;
  }

  function stopTimer(){ if(timer){ clearInterval(timer); timer = null; } }

  function startTimer(){
    timeLeft = TIME * 10; // tenths
    stopTimer();
    timer = setInterval(function(){
      timeLeft--;
      var bar = document.getElementById('bs-tim');
      if(bar){
        var pct = Math.max(0, timeLeft) / (TIME*10) * 100;
        bar.style.width = pct + '%';
        bar.className = 'bs-tim' + (pct < 25 ? ' crit' : (pct < 55 ? ' warn' : ''));
      }
      if(timeLeft <= 0){ stopTimer(); onTimeout(); }
    }, 100);
  }

  function codeHtml(lines){
    return lines.map(function(l,i){
      var num = '<span class="ln">' + (i+1) + '  </span>';
      return num + (l[1] ? '<span class="bug">' + l[0] + '</span>' : l[0]);
    }).join('\n');
  }

  function renderRound(){
    phase = 'classify';
    classifyOk = false;
    updateBar();
    var r = ROUNDS[idx];
    var lines = r.code2 || r.code;
    var html = '';
    html += '<div class="bs-timwrap"><div class="bs-tim" id="bs-tim"></div></div>';
    html += '<p class="bs-prompt">Step 1 • What kind of error is on the red line?</p>';
    html += '<div class="bs-code">' + codeHtml(lines) + '</div>';
    html += '<div class="bs-grid" id="bs-opts">';
    ORDER.forEach(function(k){
      html += '<button class="bs-opt" data-k="'+k+'"><span class="tag">'+ERR[k].tag+'</span>'+
              '<span class="desc">'+ERR[k].desc+'</span></button>';
    });
    html += '</div>';
    html += '<div class="bs-fb" id="bs-fb"></div>';
    html += '<button class="bs-next" id="bs-next">Continue →</button>';
    body.innerHTML = html;

    Array.prototype.forEach.call(body.querySelectorAll('#bs-opts .bs-opt'), function(b){
      b.onclick = function(){ pickClassify(b.getAttribute('data-k')); };
    });
    startTimer();
  }

  function pickClassify(k){
    if(phase !== 'classify') return;
    stopTimer();
    var r = ROUNDS[idx];
    var correct = r.type;
    var opts = body.querySelectorAll('#bs-opts .bs-opt');
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(opts, function(b){
      var bk = b.getAttribute('data-k');
      b.disabled = true;
      if(bk === correct) b.classList.add('ok');
      else if(bk === k) b.classList.add('no');
      else b.classList.add('dim');
    });
    var fb = document.getElementById('bs-fb');
    if(k === correct){
      classifyOk = true;
      var bonus = Math.round(timeLeft/10) * 3;
      score += 40 + bonus;
      fb.className = 'bs-fb show good';
      fb.innerHTML = '✅ Correct type: <b>'+ERR[correct].tag+'</b>. +'+(40+bonus)+' (time bonus '+bonus+'). Now pick the fix.';
    } else {
      classifyOk = false;
      fb.className = 'bs-fb show bad';
      fb.innerHTML = '❌ That is a <b>'+ERR[correct].tag.toLowerCase()+'</b> error. '+r.why+' Now pick the fix.';
    }
    updateBar();
    setTimeout(renderFix, 650);
  }

  function renderFix(){
    phase = 'fix';
    var r = ROUNDS[idx];
    var lines = r.code2 || r.code;
    var html = '';
    html += '<p class="bs-prompt">Step 2 • Which change fixes the bug?</p>';
    html += '<div class="bs-code">' + codeHtml(lines) + '</div>';
    html += '<div class="bs-grid" id="bs-opts" style="grid-template-columns:1fr;">';
    // shuffle fixes
    var order = r.fixes.map(function(_,i){return i;});
    for(var i=order.length-1;i>0;i--){ var j=Math.floor(Math.random()*(i+1)); var t=order[i];order[i]=order[j];order[j]=t; }
    order.forEach(function(fi){
      var f = r.fixes[fi];
      html += '<button class="bs-opt" data-ok="'+(f.ok?1:0)+'">'+f.t+'</button>';
    });
    html += '</div>';
    html += '<div class="bs-fb" id="bs-fb"></div>';
    html += '<button class="bs-next" id="bs-next">Continue →</button>';
    body.innerHTML = html;
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(body.querySelectorAll('#bs-opts .bs-opt'), function(b){
      b.onclick = function(){ pickFix(b.getAttribute('data-ok')==='1', b); };
    });
  }

  function pickFix(isOk, btn){
    if(phase !== 'fix') return;
    phase = 'done';
    var r = ROUNDS[idx];
    var opts = body.querySelectorAll('#bs-opts .bs-opt');
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(opts, function(b){
      b.disabled = true;
      if(b.getAttribute('data-ok')==='1') b.classList.add('ok');
      else if(b===btn) b.classList.add('no');
      else b.classList.add('dim');
    });
    var fb = document.getElementById('bs-fb');
    if(isOk){
      score += 60;
      if(classifyOk){ streak++; score += (streak-1)*10; }
      fb.className = 'bs-fb show good';
      fb.innerHTML = '🐛 Squashed! +60. '+r.why+ (streak>1 ? ' Streak x'+streak+'!' : '');
    } else {
      streak = 0;
      fb.className = 'bs-fb show bad';
      fb.innerHTML = '❌ Not quite. '+r.why+' Streak reset.';
    }
    updateBar();
    var nb = document.getElementById('bs-next');
    nb.classList.add('show');
    nb.textContent = (idx+1 >= TOTAL) ? 'See results →' : 'Next round →';
    nb.onclick = advance;
  }

  function onTimeout(){
    // ran out during classify
    if(phase !== 'classify') return;
    phase = 'done';
    streak = 0;
    var r = ROUNDS[idx];
    var opts = body.querySelectorAll('#bs-opts .bs-opt');
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(opts, function(b){
      b.disabled = true;
      if(b.getAttribute('data-k')===r.type) b.classList.add('ok'); else b.classList.add('dim');
    });
    var fb = document.getElementById('bs-fb');
    fb.className = 'bs-fb show bad';
    fb.innerHTML = '⏳ Out of time! It was a <b>'+ERR[r.type].tag.toLowerCase()+'</b> error. '+r.why+' Streak reset.';
    updateBar();
    var nb = document.getElementById('bs-next');
    nb.classList.add('show');
    nb.textContent = (idx+1 >= TOTAL) ? 'See results →' : 'Next round →';
    nb.onclick = advance;
  }

  function advance(){
    idx++;
    if(idx >= TOTAL){ endGame(); } else { renderRound(); }
  }

  function endGame(){
    stopTimer();
    finalScore = score;
    var msg, max = TOTAL * 100 + TOTAL*10;
    if(score >= max*0.8) msg = 'Ace debugger! You classify and fix errors fast.';
    else if(score >= max*0.5) msg = 'Solid work. You know your error categories.';
    else msg = 'Good start. Keep practicing spotting each error type.';
    body.innerHTML =
      '<div class="bs-end">'+
        '<h2>🐛 Bugs Squashed!</h2>'+
        '<div class="big">'+score+'</div>'+
        '<p><b>'+msg+'</b></p>'+
        '<p>Remember: syntax errors break the rules and stop the code, logic errors run but give wrong answers, '+
        'runtime errors crash mid-run, and overflow means a value passed its allowed range. '+
        'Testing is how you surface every one of them.</p>'+
        '<div class="rank" id="bs-rank"></div>'+
        '<button class="bs-again" id="bs-again">▶ Play again</button>'+
      '</div>';
    document.getElementById('bs-again').onclick = reset;
    updateBar();
    try{ document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsGameScore',{detail:{value:finalScore}})); }catch(e){}
  }

  reset();
})();
</script>

      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between a syntax error and a logic error?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A syntax error breaks the rules of the language, so the program will not run at all. A logic error lets the program run to completion but produces incorrect or unintended output. The quick test: if it will not run, suspect syntax; if it runs but the answer is wrong, suspect logic.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What exactly is a run-time error?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A run-time error occurs while the program is executing, after it has started. Common causes are dividing by zero or trying to use a value that does not exist, such as an item beyond the end of a list. The program begins normally and then fails at the moment it hits the bad operation.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why do edge cases matter so much in testing?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Because most bugs hide at the boundaries. A program often works for typical inputs but breaks on an empty list, a zero, a maximum value, or the first and last elements of a range. Testing typical, boundary, and invalid inputs together is far more likely to expose errors than running one friendly input.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What are the main debugging strategies the exam expects?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Hand-tracing the code line by line, adding display or print statements to inspect intermediate values, testing sections of the program in isolation, commenting out code to narrow down the problem, using varied test cases, and reading error messages. Documentation and a second reviewer also make errors easier to find.</div>
      </div>

        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How does this topic connect to the Create Performance Task?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>

The task is completed individually.</div>

  <div class="lesson-main">

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Explain why program design begins by investigating and reflecting on a need or problem</span></li>
        <li><span>Describe the development process as iterative and non-linear, cycling through investigating, designing, prototyping, and testing</span></li>
        <li><span>Define program requirements and identify how a design can be represented as requirements, a diagram or flowchart, or a prototype</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain how design decisions involve tradeoffs and sometimes require input from users or others</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain the purpose of program documentation and comments, and why documentation is added throughout development and used during maintenance</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span>Big Idea 1 (Creative Development) is 10 to 13 percent of the AP CSP exam, and design and development questions are steady, predictable points. The iterative process and documentation ideas here are also exactly what the Create Performance Task written response asks you to describe, so this lesson pays off twice.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>A student sits down to build an app, opens the editor, and starts typing code immediately with no plan. Halfway through they realize they never asked who the app is for or what it actually needs to do, and now large parts have to be thrown out and rebuilt. A second student spends the first hour investigating the need, sketching a design, and building a rough prototype to test one idea. Which student is following the process the AP CSP framework describes, and why does starting with the code so often cost you time later?</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Design Starts With a Need, Not With Code</h2>
      <p>Good program design does not begin at the keyboard. It begins by <strong>investigating and reflecting on a need or a problem</strong>. Before writing anything, a developer studies the situation, often <strong>consulting or using multiple sources</strong>, and works to understand the <strong>needs of the intended users</strong>. The whole point of a program is to serve those users, so figuring out who they are and what they actually need is the first real step of development.</p>
      <p>This is why "just start coding" is the wrong instinct. A program built without understanding the need often solves the wrong problem, or solves it in a way that does not fit how real users work. Investigating first, and reflecting on what you find, is what keeps the rest of the process pointed at something worth building.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>When a question asks what a developer should do <strong>first</strong>, the credited answer is almost always about <strong>investigating the problem and understanding the users' needs</strong>, not about choosing a programming language or writing code. Understanding the need comes before implementation.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>The Development Process Is Iterative and Non-Linear</h2>
      <p>The framework describes development as a cycle of four kinds of activity:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Investigating and reflecting</strong> on the need, the users, and what you have learned so far.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Designing</strong> a plan for how the program will work.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Prototyping</strong> an early version to try out an idea.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Testing</strong> to see whether it works and meets the need.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>The key word is <strong>iterative</strong>. These steps are <strong>not a straight line</strong> that you walk through once. The process is <strong>non-linear</strong>: you repeat steps and revisit earlier ones. Testing a prototype might send you back to redesign; a design choice might raise a new question that sends you back to investigate. You cycle through the activities as many times as the program needs, refining a little more each pass.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>"Development is a fixed sequence: you finish investigating, then finish designing, then finish coding, then test once, and you are done." That waterfall picture is exactly what the framework says development is <strong>not</strong>. The tested idea is that development is iterative and non-linear, so you loop back to earlier steps whenever what you learn tells you to.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">While testing a prototype, a developer discovers that users are confused by the main screen, so they return to redesign that part before continuing. What does this best illustrate about the development process?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-design-1-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-design-1','A','C','mc-design-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> That testing should only happen after the program is completely finished</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-design-1','B','C','mc-design-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> That designing must always be fully completed before any testing begins</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-design-1','C','C','mc-design-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> That the process is iterative, so testing can send you back to an earlier step like designing</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-design-1','D','C','mc-design-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> That the developer made an error by not planning the screen correctly the first time</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-design-1-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Requirements and Ways to Represent a Design</h2>
      <p><strong>Program requirements</strong> describe how a program functions, and they may include the needs and expectations of the users. Requirements are the agreed-upon description of what the program has to do, so they give the team a shared target to build toward and to test against later.</p>
      <p>A design can be <strong>represented</strong> in more than one form, and the framework names three:</p>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Representation</th>
<th>What it is</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Requirements</strong></td>
<td>A written description of what the program must do and how it should function, often including user needs and expectations.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Diagram or flowchart</strong></td>
<td>A visual representation of the program's structure or the flow of steps, showing how parts connect before any code is written.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Prototype</strong></td>
<td>An early, incomplete version of the program built to test an idea and get feedback.</td>
</tr>
      </table>
      <p>All three describe the <strong>design</strong>, not the finished program. A <strong>prototype</strong> in particular is an early version used to try out ideas: it is meant to be rough, and it exists so you can learn something before committing to the full build.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>Know that a design can be shown as <strong>requirements, a diagram or flowchart, or a prototype</strong>. If a question describes a rough early version made to test whether an idea works, that is a <strong>prototype</strong>, and its purpose is to test ideas, not to be the final product.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Design Decisions and Tradeoffs</h2>
      <p>Building a program is a stream of <strong>design decisions</strong>: which feature to include, how a screen should behave, what to leave out. These decisions are <strong>sometimes made collaboratively</strong>, and they sometimes <strong>require input from the users or from other people</strong> who understand the need. A developer working alone still benefits from asking users what they expect.</p>
      <p>Almost every design decision involves <strong>tradeoffs</strong>. Adding a feature might make the program more capable but harder to use; making it faster might make it more complex to build. There is rarely a choice that is better in every way, so developers weigh the options against the program's goal and the users' needs and pick the one that fits best.</p>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A developer is unsure whether users would prefer a simpler menu or one with more options. What is the most appropriate way to make this design decision?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-design-2-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-design-2','A','B','mc-design-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> Pick whichever option is faster to code and never revisit it</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-design-2','B','B','mc-design-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> Get input from intended users and weigh the tradeoffs against the program's goal</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-design-2','C','B','mc-design-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> Include every possible option so no decision has to be made</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-design-2','D','B','mc-design-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> Wait until the program is finished and then ask whether it was right</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-design-2-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Program Documentation and Comments</h2>
      <p><strong>Program documentation</strong> is a written description of what a program or a segment of a program does, how it behaves, and how it was developed. It is written for people: the developer who will come back to the code later, and anyone else who has to read, use, or modify it.</p>
      <p><strong>Comments</strong> are documentation placed <strong>inside the code</strong> itself. In text-based languages a comment is ignored by the computer when the program runs, so it exists purely to explain the code to a human reader. Comments are one form of documentation, but documentation also includes descriptions kept outside the code.</p>
      <p>Two facts the exam cares about:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>Documentation is useful <strong>during</strong> development, helping the team track how the program works and why decisions were made, and it is useful later for <strong>maintenance</strong>, when someone needs to fix or update the program.</li>
        <li>Documentation should be added <strong>throughout</strong> development, not saved for the very end. Writing it as you go keeps it accurate and useful while you are still building.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>"Documentation is a final step you do after the program is finished." That is the wrong picture. The framework says documentation should be added <strong>throughout</strong> development and helps <strong>during</strong> the build as well as later during maintenance. Waiting until the end usually means the documentation is rushed, incomplete, or already out of date.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How This Shows Up on the Create Performance Task</h2>
      <p>The Create Performance Task is completed <strong>individually</strong> under current AP rules, so your program and your written responses must be your own. Topic 1.3 is the process you are expected to live out while you build. You do not write a program in one straight shot; you follow the <strong>iterative development process</strong>, cycling through designing, prototyping, and testing, and returning to earlier steps as you learn what works.</p>
      <p>The written response asks you to describe <strong>how you developed the program</strong>. You will point to a part of the program you <strong>developed independently</strong> and explain the <strong>process of testing and refining</strong> it: what you tried, what a test revealed, what you changed in response, and how the program improved. That is the iterative process in miniature, so getting comfortable with investigate, design, prototype, test, and repeat here makes that written response far easier to write later. Documenting your process as you go, rather than reconstructing it at the end, is what makes the description accurate.</p>
    </div>

        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 1 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Concept</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Predict what a developer does first before reading the options.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A developer is beginning work on a new program. According to the AP CSP development process, which activity should come at the very start?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q1-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','A','D','q1-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Choosing the programming language and writing the first lines of code</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','B','D','q1-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> Writing the program documentation that will ship with the finished product</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','C','D','q1-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Deciding exactly how many features the final program will contain</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','D','D','q1-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> Investigating and reflecting on the need or problem and the intended users' needs</button>
</div>
<div id="q1-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Picking a language and coding comes after understanding the problem. Starting at the keyboard risks solving the wrong problem.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Documentation is added throughout development, but the process starts by investigating the need, not by writing the final documentation first.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Locking the exact feature count before investigating the need puts a decision ahead of the understanding that should inform it.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Design begins by investigating and reflecting on the need or problem and understanding the intended users' needs, often using multiple sources.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q2">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 2 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Best choice</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Decide what the iterative process really means before you look.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>Which statement best describes the development process as presented in the AP CSP framework?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q2-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','A','A','q2-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> It is iterative and non-linear, so developers repeat activities and return to earlier steps as needed</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','B','A','q2-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> It is a one-way sequence completed exactly once from start to finish</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','C','A','q2-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> It requires all testing to be saved until every other step is fully complete</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','D','A','q2-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> It forbids changing the design once prototyping has begun</button>
</div>
<div id="q2-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. The process is iterative and non-linear: developers cycle through investigating, designing, prototyping, and testing and revisit earlier steps.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. A single one-way pass is the waterfall picture the framework explicitly rejects.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Testing is part of the cycle and happens repeatedly, including on prototypes, not only at the very end.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Returning to redesign after prototyping is exactly the kind of iteration the process encourages.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q3">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 3 of 6<span class="diff-tag">II and III only style</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Decide which statements are true before matching to an option.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>Consider these claims about program documentation:</p></div>
        <ul class="mcq-roman">
          <li>
<strong>I.</strong> Documentation should only be written after the program is completely finished.</li>
          <li>
<strong>II.</strong> Comments are a form of documentation placed inside the code to explain it to human readers.</li>
          <li>
<strong>III.</strong> Documentation is useful both during development and later during maintenance.</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q3-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','A','B','q3-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> I only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','B','B','q3-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> II and III only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','C','B','q3-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> I and II only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','D','B','q3-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> I, II, and III</button>
</div>
<div id="q3-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement I is false and statements II and III are both true, so this cannot be right.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Statements II and III are true. Statement I is false because documentation should be added throughout development, not saved for the end.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement I is false: documentation should be added throughout development, not only at the end.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement I is false, so not all three can be correct.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q4">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 4 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Spot the problem</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Find the weak point in the team's process first.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A team writes code for weeks, adds no comments and keeps no written descriptions, and plans to document everything the night before submission. Which specific problem with their process does the framework most directly warn against?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q4-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','A','C','q4-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> They should not use comments at all because the computer ignores them when the program runs</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','B','C','q4-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> Documentation is only for other people, so a solo submission never needs any</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','C','C','q4-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Documentation should be added throughout development, not left entirely until the very end</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','D','C','q4-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> Writing documentation before the program is finished always introduces errors into the code</button>
</div>
<div id="q4-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Comments being ignored at run time is exactly why they are useful to human readers. The problem is the timing, not using comments.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Documentation also helps the developer, including later during maintenance, so a solo project still benefits from it.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. The framework says documentation should be added throughout development, so saving all of it for the end is the flawed practice here.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Documentation such as comments does not run, so it cannot introduce errors into the program's behavior.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q5">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 5 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Application</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Predict which term the scenario is describing before reading options.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>Before building a full scheduling app, a developer creates a rough, incomplete version of just the calendar screen and shows it to a few intended users to see whether the layout makes sense.         <div class="mcq-options" id="q5-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','A','C','q5-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> A requirement, whose purpose is to list everything the finished program must do</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','B','C','q5-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> A flowchart, whose purpose is to show the exact order of every line of code</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','C','C','q5-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> A prototype, whose purpose is to test an idea and gather feedback before the full build</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','D','C','q5-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> The final program, whose purpose is to be delivered to users as the finished product</button>
</div>
<div id="q5-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. A requirement is a written description of what the program must do, not a rough working version of a screen.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. A flowchart is a diagram of steps or structure, not a rough working version that users interact with.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. A prototype is an early, incomplete version built to test ideas and gather feedback, which is exactly what the developer is doing.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. A rough, incomplete version made to test an idea is a prototype, not the finished program meant for delivery.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q6">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 6 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Concept</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Predict what a design decision involves before you look.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A developer must choose between adding a powerful feature that makes the program harder to learn and keeping the program simple but less capable. Which idea from the framework does this choice most directly illustrate?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q6-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','A','D','q6-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> That program requirements can never change once they are written down</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','B','D','q6-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> That documentation must be completed before any design decision is made</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','C','D','q6-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> That the fastest option to implement is always the correct design choice</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','D','D','q6-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> That design decisions involve tradeoffs and may require input from users</button>
</div>
<div id="q6-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Requirements can be revised as development iterates; that is not what this choice is about.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Documentation is written throughout development and is not a prerequisite for making a design decision.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Choosing purely by implementation speed ignores the tradeoffs and the users' needs that a design decision should weigh.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. There is no option that is better in every way, so the developer weighs tradeoffs and may seek user input, which is exactly how design decisions work.</div>
      </div>

<script>
(function(){
  var stage = document.getElementById('ds-stage');
  var elRound = document.getElementById('ds-round');
  var elScore = document.getElementById('ds-score');
  var elStreak = document.getElementById('ds-streak');
  var RA = '→';

  // Canonical iterative development order.
  var STEPS = [
    'Investigate and define the problem',
    'Design the solution',
    'Build a prototype',
    'Test the program',
    'Reflect and refine'
  ];

  function orderRound(prompt){
    return { type:'order', prompt:prompt, answer:[0,1,2,3,4] };
  }
  function decideRound(ctx, q, opts, correct, ok, no){
    return { type:'decide', ctx:ctx, q:q, opts:opts, correct:correct, ok:ok, no:no };
  }

  // 8 rounds, mixed, escalating.
  var ROUNDS = [
    orderRound('Drag the development steps into a sensible order, from the very start of a project.'),
    decideRound(
      'Your teammates keep arguing about what the app should even do.',
      'What should happen before anyone writes code?',
      [
        'Investigate and clearly define the problem and requirements',
        'Start coding the fastest feature so there is something to show',
        'Buy a faster computer to speed up development',
        'Pick the programming language everyone likes best'
      ], 0,
      'Good design comes before coding. You investigate and define the problem first so the whole team builds the right thing.',
      'Jumping into code before defining the problem wastes effort. Program design starts by investigating and defining what is actually needed.'
    ),
    decideRound(
      'Early testers say your menu is confusing and they cannot find the settings.',
      'What is the best next move?',
      [
        'Gather that feedback and revise the design',
        'Ignore it, the menu makes sense to you',
        'Add more features on top of the menu',
        'Ship it and tell users to read a manual'
      ], 0,
      'Development is iterative and driven by user feedback. Confusing results send you back to refine the design.',
      'User feedback is a signal to loop back and improve the design, not something to ignore. Iteration is the whole point.'
    ),
    orderRound('A new sprint is starting. Put the iterative steps back in order for this build.'),
    decideRound(
      'A feature gives the right answer but runs very slowly on large inputs.',
      'What should you do?',
      [
        'Test to find the slow part, then refine that code',
        'Delete the feature since it technically works',
        'Assume users will not notice and move on',
        'Rewrite the entire program from scratch'
      ], 0,
      'Testing pinpoints the problem, then you refine. Iteration means improving what works, not scrapping it.',
      'Correct output is not the finish line. You test to locate the bottleneck and refine, rather than discarding working code.'
    ),
    decideRound(
      'Your prototype passes every test you wrote, but you only tested normal inputs.',
      'Which choice best reflects good development?',
      [
        'Test edge cases and unexpected input, then refine',
        'Declare it finished since your tests pass',
        'Remove tests so the code looks cleaner',
        'Publish it and wait for users to report crashes'
      ], 0,
      'Thorough testing includes edge cases. Iterative development keeps testing and refining before you call it done.',
      'Passing a few normal tests is not enough. Good developers test edge cases and keep iterating before shipping.'
    ),
    decideRound(
      'After launch, real users request a feature that changes how the program should work.',
      'What does an iterative process do here?',
      [
        'Loop back: redefine, redesign, and refine with the new needs',
        'Refuse changes because the project is already finished',
        'Add the feature without any design or testing',
        'Start a brand new unrelated project instead'
      ], 0,
      'Development never truly ends. New needs send you back through the cycle: define, design, build, test, refine.',
      'Iterative means you loop back. New requirements restart the cycle of defining, designing, testing, and refining.'
    ),
    orderRound('Final round. Show you know the cycle: order the steps of the iterative process one more time.')
  ];

  var idx = 0, score = 0, streak = 0, answered = false;

  function shuffle(a){
    a = a.slice();
    for(var i=a.length-1;i>0;i--){ var j=Math.floor(Math.random()*(i+1)); var t=a[i]; a[i]=a[j]; a[j]=t; }
    return a;
  }
  function updateBar(){
    elRound.textContent = (idx+1) + ' / ' + ROUNDS.length;
    elScore.textContent = score;
    elStreak.textContent = streak;
  }

  function render(){
    answered = false;
    updateBar();
    var r = ROUNDS[idx];
    if(r.type==='order') renderOrder(r); else renderDecide(r);
  }

  // ---- Order round ----
  function renderOrder(r){
    var order = shuffle([0,1,2,3,4]);
    // Avoid an already-correct shuffle.
    var isSorted = order.every(function(v,i){ return v===i; });
    if(isSorted){ var t=order[0]; order[0]=order[4]; order[4]=t; }

    var html = '<div class="ds-tag order">Order the process</div>';
    html += '<p class="ds-q">' + r.prompt + '</p>';
    html += '<ul class="ds-list" id="ds-list"></ul>';
    html += '<div id="ds-fb"></div>';
    html += '<button class="ds-btn" id="ds-check">Check order</button>';
    stage.innerHTML = html;

    var list = document.getElementById('ds-list');
    var dragEl = null;

    function paint(){
      list.innerHTML = '';
      order.forEach(function(stepId, pos){
        var li = document.createElement('li');
        li.className = 'ds-item';
        li.setAttribute('draggable','true');
        li.dataset.pos = pos;
        li.innerHTML = '<span class="num">'+(pos+1)+'</span>'+
          '<span class="lbl">'+STEPS[stepId]+'</span>'+
          '<span class="ds-arrows"><button class="up" '+(pos===0?'disabled':'')+' aria-label="Move up">▲</button>'+
          '<button class="dn" '+(pos===order.length-1?'disabled':'')+' aria-label="Move down">▼</button></span>'+
          '<span class="grip">⋮</span>';

        li.querySelector('.up').onclick = function(e){ e.stopPropagation(); if(answered) return; swap(pos,pos-1); };
        li.querySelector('.dn').onclick = function(e){ e.stopPropagation(); if(answered) return; swap(pos,pos+1); };

        li.addEventListener('dragstart', function(){ if(answered) return; dragEl=li; li.classList.add('drag'); });
        li.addEventListener('dragend', function(){ li.classList.remove('drag'); dragEl=null; Array.prototype.forEach.call(list.children,function(c){c.classList.remove('over');}); });
        li.addEventListener('dragover', function(e){ e.preventDefault(); if(li!==dragEl) li.classList.add('over'); });
        li.addEventListener('dragleave', function(){ li.classList.remove('over'); });
        li.addEventListener('drop', function(e){ e.preventDefault(); if(answered||!dragEl) return; swap(parseInt(dragEl.dataset.pos,10), parseInt(li.dataset.pos,10)); });

        list.appendChild(li);
      });
    }
    function swap(a,b){
      if(a<0||b<0||a>=order.length||b>=order.length) return;
      var t=order[a]; order[a]=order[b]; order[b]=t; paint();
    }
    paint();

    document.getElementById('ds-check').onclick = function(){
      if(answered) return;
      answered = true;
      var correct = order.every(function(v,i){ return v===i; });
      var items = list.querySelectorAll('.ds-item');
      Array.prototype.forEach.call(items, function(li){
        li.setAttribute('draggable','false');
        li.querySelector('.up').disabled = true;
        li.querySelector('.dn').disabled = true;
      });
      var fb = document.getElementById('ds-fb');
      if(correct){
        score += 15; streak += 1; if(streak>=2) score += 5;
        fb.innerHTML = '<div class="ds-fb ok"><b>Correct order!</b> Investigate '+RA+' Design '+RA+' Prototype '+RA+' Test '+RA+' Refine. And it loops: refining sends you back to redesign and retest. Development is iterative.</div>';
      } else {
        streak = 0;
        fb.innerHTML = '<div class="ds-fb no"><b>Not quite.</b> The sensible flow is Investigate '+RA+' Design '+RA+' Prototype '+RA+' Test '+RA+' Refine. Design before building, and loop back after testing. That looping is what makes it iterative.</div>';
      }
      updateBar();
      showNext();
    };
  }

  // ---- Decide round ----
  function renderDecide(r){
    var order = shuffle(r.opts.map(function(_,i){ return i; }));
    var html = '<div class="ds-tag decide">Best next move</div>';
    html += '<p class="ds-q">' + r.q + '<span class="ctx">Situation: ' + r.ctx + '</span></p>';
    html += '<div class="ds-opts" id="ds-opts"></div>';
    html += '<div id="ds-fb"></div>';
    stage.innerHTML = html;

    var wrap = document.getElementById('ds-opts');
    order.forEach(function(optId){
      var b = document.createElement('button');
      b.className = 'ds-opt';
      b.type = 'button';
      b.textContent = r.opts[optId];
      b.onclick = function(){ choose(optId, b); };
      wrap.appendChild(b);
    });

    function choose(optId, btn){
      if(answered) return;
      answered = true;
      var btns = wrap.querySelectorAll('.ds-opt');
      var i = 0;
      Array.prototype.forEach.call(btns, function(bb){ bb.disabled = true; });
      // mark
      Array.prototype.forEach.call(order, function(oid, pos){
        var bb = btns[pos];
        if(oid===r.correct) bb.classList.add('correct');
      });
      var fb = document.getElementById('ds-fb');
      if(optId===r.correct){
        btn.classList.add('correct');
        score += 12; streak += 1; if(streak>=2) score += 5;
        fb.innerHTML = '<div class="ds-fb ok"><b>Smart move.</b> '+r.ok+'</div>';
      } else {
        btn.classList.add('wrong');
        streak = 0;
        fb.innerHTML = '<div class="ds-fb no"><b>Better to iterate.</b> '+r.no+'</div>';
      }
      updateBar();
      showNext();
    }
  }

  function showNext(){
    var btn = document.createElement('button');
    btn.className = 'ds-btn';
    btn.style.marginTop = '4px';
    btn.textContent = (idx < ROUNDS.length-1) ? 'Next round' : 'See results';
    btn.onclick = function(){
      idx++;
      if(idx < ROUNDS.length) render(); else renderEnd();
    };
    stage.appendChild(btn);
  }

  function renderEnd(){
    updateBar();
    var maxable = 0; // rough max for message tiers
    var msg;
    if(score >= 110) msg = 'You have the iterative mindset down. You design before coding, and you let testing and user feedback drive every revision.';
    else if(score >= 70) msg = 'Solid work. Remember: development loops. Testing and user feedback always send you back to refine the design.';
    else msg = 'Keep practicing the cycle: Investigate, Design, Prototype, Test, Refine, then loop back. Good design comes before coding, and feedback drives the rest.';

    stage.innerHTML =
      '<div class="ds-end">'+
        '<p class="big">🏁 Sprint complete!</p>'+
        '<p class="score">You scored '+score+' points</p>'+
        '<p class="msg">'+msg+'</p>'+
        '<button class="ds-btn" id="ds-again">▶ Play again</button>'+
      '</div>';
    document.getElementById('ds-again').onclick = reset;

    // Dispatch final score for the leaderboard.
    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsGameScore',{detail:{value:score}}));
  }

  function reset(){
    idx = 0; score = 0; streak = 0; answered = false;
    render();
  }

  render();
})();
</script>

This scenario shows testing happening on a prototype and feeding back into design.", "B": "No. The point is the opposite: designing does not have to be fully complete before testing.   .lesson-num-badge{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:44px;height:44px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;font-size:14px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;flex-shrink:0;}
  .lesson-eyebrow{font-size:12px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;}
  .lesson-hero h1{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:clamp(26px,4vw,40px)!important;line-height:1.2!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;}
  .lesson-hero-pills{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-pill{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.08);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);padding:5px 12px;border-radius:100px;font-size:12px;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .ced-tag{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;background:rgba(26,86,219,.25);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.3);padding:4px 10px;border-radius:100px;font-size:11px;font-weight:600;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;letter-spacing:.04em;}

  /* PROGRESS STRIP */
  .bi3-progress{background:#fff!important;border-bottom:1px solid #e2e8f0!important;padding:14px 20px!important;overflow-x:auto!important;-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch!important;}
  .bi3-progress-inner{display:flex!important;flex-direction:row!important;flex-wrap:nowrap!important;align-items:center!important;gap:0!important;width:max-content!important;min-width:100%!important;}
  .prog-step{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-step-link{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;text-decoration:none!important;cursor:pointer!important;}
  .prog-step-link:hover .prog-dot{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-dot{width:26px!important;height:26px!important;border-radius:50%!important;display:flex!important;align-items:center!important;justify-content:center!important;font-size:9px!important;font-weight:700!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-dot.active{background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;}
  .prog-dot.upcoming{background:#f1f5f9!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;}
  .prog-dot.done{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border:2px solid var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-label{font-size:8px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;line-height:1.2!important;white-space:nowrap!important;}
  .prog-label.active-label{color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-arrow{flex:1 0 4px!important;height:2px!important;background:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:18px!important;min-width:4px!important;max-width:16px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}

  /* MAIN */
  .lesson-main{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;padding:40px 24px 80px;}
  .lesson-objectives{background:var(--bi3-bg);border-left:4px solid var(--bi3);border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin-bottom:28px;}
  .lesson-objectives h2{font-size:14px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;text-transform:uppercase!important;letter-spacing:.06em!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .lesson-objectives ul{list-style:none;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-objectives li{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#1e3a8a;line-height:1.5;}
  .lesson-objectives li::before{content:"\2713";color:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:1px;}
  .score-impact{background:#f0fdf4;border:1px solid #bbf7d0;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 18px;margin-bottom:28px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#14532d;}
  .score-impact strong{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}

  /* HOOK */
  .hook-box{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:32px;}
  .hook-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .hook-box p{font-size:15px!important;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:0!important;}

  /* LESSON SECTIONS */
  .lesson-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .lesson-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .lesson-section h3{font-size:17px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-top:24px!important;margin-bottom:10px!important;}
  .lesson-section p{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section ul,.lesson-section ol{padding-left:20px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section li{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .lesson-section code{background:#eef2ff;color:#1e3a8a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e3a8a!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}

  /* DUAL CODE PANEL */
  .code-panel-wrap{margin:20px 0;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;}
  .code-panel-tabs{display:flex;background:#1e293b;}
  .code-tab{padding:8px 16px;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;border:none;background:transparent;letter-spacing:.04em;transition:background .15s;font-family:inherit;}
  .code-tab.py{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.pseudo{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.active{background:rgba(255,255,255,.15)!important;}
  .code-tab-label{font-size:10px;opacity:.6;margin-left:4px;font-weight:400;}
  .code-pane{background:#0f172a;padding:18px 20px;overflow-x:auto;height:0;overflow:hidden;padding:0;}
  .code-pane.active{height:auto;overflow-x:auto;padding:18px 20px;}
  .code-pane pre{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:0;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;max-width:100%;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-kw{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .py-fn{color:#6ee7b7!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#6ee7b7!important;}
  .py-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .py-str{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .py-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .py-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-op{color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;}
  .ps-kw{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .ps-op{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .ps-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .ps-str{color:#86efac!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#86efac!important;}
  .ps-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .ps-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* CALLOUTS */
  .callout-exam{background:#fffbeb;border:1px solid #fcd34d;border-left:4px solid var(--amber);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-exam-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--amber)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--amber)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-exam p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}
  .callout-trap{background:#fef2f2;border:1px solid #fca5a5;border-left:4px solid var(--red);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-opt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;padding:10px 14px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;font-family:monospace;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;background:#f8fafc;text-align:left;width:100%;transition:border-color .15s;}
  .mini-opt:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mini-opt.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
