  <div class="lesson-main">

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Define a program as a collection of statements that performs a specific task when run</span></li>
        <li><span>Distinguish a program's function (what it does) from its purpose (the need it meets and why)</span></li>
        <li><span>Identify the inputs a program receives and the outputs it produces, across text, visual, audible, tactile, and movement forms</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain program behavior as how a program responds to a given input or set of inputs</span></li>
        <li><span>Recognize event-driven code that runs only when a triggering event, such as a click or key press, occurs</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span>Big Idea 1 (Creative Development) is 10 to 13 percent of the AP CSP exam, and describing a program's function and purpose is a skill you use twice: on the multiple-choice section and in the written responses of the Create Performance Task. Getting the function versus purpose distinction right is nearly free points, and it is the exact language your Create Task writeup must use.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>A weather app on a phone quietly checks the barometer sensor every few minutes, and when the pressure drops sharply it buzzes and shows a storm warning. Ask two people what the app is, and one says "it reads a sensor and shows a message," while the other says "it helps people stay safe when bad weather is coming." Both are right, but they are answering two different questions. Which one is describing the function, and which one is describing the purpose?</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What a Program Actually Is</h2>
      <p>A <strong>program</strong> is a collection of statements that performs a specific task when it is run. That definition is small but exact, and the exam holds you to it. The statements are the instructions; running them is what produces a result. Nothing happens until the program runs, and when it does, it carries out the task it was written to do.</p>
      <p>To <strong>describe</strong> a program you answer two separate questions: what does it do, and why does it exist? Those map to two vocabulary terms you must not mix up: <strong>function</strong> and <strong>purpose</strong>. Almost every 1.2 question is really testing whether you can tell those two apart, so it is worth getting clear before anything else.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>When a question asks you to describe a program, decide first whether it wants the <strong>function</strong> (the observable behavior) or the <strong>purpose</strong> (the need it addresses). Answering the wrong one is the single most common way students lose these points even when they understand the program.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Function versus Purpose</h2>
      <p>The <strong>function</strong> of a program is <strong>what it does</strong>: its observable behavior, described concretely. "It takes a list of numbers and displays the largest one" is a function. You could watch the program run and confirm it.</p>
      <p>The <strong>purpose</strong> of a program is <strong>why it was created</strong>: the problem it addresses, the need it meets, who it is for, and the value it provides. "It helps a coach quickly find the top score so practice runs faster" is a purpose. You cannot see the purpose by watching the screen; it lives in the reason someone built the program. A program can also reflect the <strong>creativity, values, and interests</strong> of the person who made it, which is part of why two programmers solving the same need may build very different programs.</p>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Term</th>
<th>Question it answers</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Function</strong></td>
<td>What does the program do? (its observable behavior)</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Purpose</strong></td>
<td>Why does it exist? (the need it meets, who it is for, the value it gives)</td>
</tr>
      </table>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">An app scans a photo of a meal and shows an estimated calorie count. A user says, "This exists to help people who are tracking their diet make quicker food choices." That sentence is describing the app's:</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-purpose-1-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-purpose-1','A','B','mc-purpose-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> Function</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-purpose-1','B','B','mc-purpose-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> Purpose</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-purpose-1','C','B','mc-purpose-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> Input</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-purpose-1','D','B','mc-purpose-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> Output</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-purpose-1-fb"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>Do not assume purpose is just a fancier restatement of function. "It sorts the scores" (function) and "it helps a teacher find who needs help" (purpose) are different answers to different questions. A response that only lists what the code does has <strong>not</strong> described the purpose, and vice versa.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Inputs and Outputs</h2>
      <p><strong>Input</strong> is how a program receives data. Input does not have to come from a person typing. It can come from a <strong>user</strong>, from <strong>another program</strong>, from an <strong>input device</strong> such as a keyboard or mouse, from a <strong>sensor</strong> such as a thermometer or accelerometer, or from a <strong>file</strong>. Input can be <strong>tactile</strong> (a touch or button press), <strong>audible</strong> (a spoken command), <strong>visual</strong> (a scanned image), or <strong>text</strong>.</p>
      <p><strong>Output</strong> is any observable behavior a program produces. Like input, it comes in several forms: <strong>visual</strong> (something on the screen), <strong>audible</strong> (a sound), <strong>tactile</strong> (a vibration), <strong>movement</strong> (a robot arm turning), or <strong>text</strong>. If you can observe it happening, it is a candidate for being an output.</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Input examples:</strong> a tapped button, a voice command, a temperature reading from a sensor, a saved file the program opens.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Output examples:</strong> a message on the screen, a beep, a phone buzz, a drawn shape, a motor spinning.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>Identifying input and output precisely matters because the Create Task written responses ask you to name at least one input to your program and one output your program produces. Vague answers like "the program" are not inputs; a specific piece of data the program receives is.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Behavior and Events</h2>
      <p><strong>Program behavior</strong> is how a program responds to a given input or set of inputs. Same program, different input, and the behavior can change: type a valid password and you are let in; type the wrong one and you get an error. Describing behavior means connecting an input to the response it produces.</p>
      <p>Some programs are <strong>event-driven</strong>. In an event-driven program, certain code runs <strong>only when a specific event occurs</strong>. The event is the <strong>trigger</strong>: a mouse click, a key press, a sensor crossing a threshold, a screen tap. Until that event happens, that block of code simply waits. A button that does nothing until you click it, then plays a sound, is event-driven: the click is the event, and playing the sound is the response.</p>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">In a drawing app, a block of code runs only at the moment the user presses the space bar, at which point the canvas clears. What is the event that triggers this code?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-purpose-2-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-purpose-2','A','C','mc-purpose-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> Clearing the canvas</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-purpose-2','B','C','mc-purpose-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> The drawing already on the canvas</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-purpose-2','C','C','mc-purpose-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> The space bar being pressed</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-purpose-2','D','C','mc-purpose-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> The app being a drawing app</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-purpose-2-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-visual">
      <p class="lv-kicker">💡 See it in action</p>
    <div class="wgt" role="group" aria-label="Interactive input output program behavior demo">
      <div class="wgt-h">Input, Program, Output</div>
      <div class="wgt-sub">A thermostat program. Its function: turn the heater on when the room is below 68 degrees.</div>
      <div class="iom-flow">
        <div class="iom-box">
<div class="l">Input</div>
<div class="iom-temp" id="iomTemp">70°</div>
</div>
        <div class="iom-ar" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
        <div class="iom-box prog">
<div class="l">Program</div>
<div class="v">if temp < 68:<br>heater on</div>
</div>
        <div class="iom-ar" aria-hidden="true">→</div>
        <div class="iom-box out">
<div class="l">Output</div>
<div class="v" id="iomOut">Heater OFF</div>
</div>
      </div>
      <div class="ptl-ctl" style="margin-top:16px">
<label for="iomR">Room temperature</label><input type="range" id="iomR" min="60" max="78" value="70">
</div>
      <div class="wgt-note" id="iomNote">Change the input and the output changes. Same input always gives the same output: that is the program's behavior.</div>
    </div>
    <script>(function(){
      var r=document.getElementById('iomR'),t=document.getElementById('iomTemp'),o=document.getElementById('iomOut'),note=document.getElementById('iomNote');
      function upd(){var v=parseInt(r.value,10);t.innerHTML=v+'°';var on=v<68;o.textContent='Heater '+(on?'ON':'OFF');o.parentElement.className='iom-box out';
        note.textContent=on?('Input '+v+' is below 68, so the program outputs Heater ON.'):('Input '+v+' is at or above 68, so the program outputs Heater OFF.');note.className='wgt-note';}
      r.addEventListener('input',upd);upd();
    })();</script>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How This Shows Up on the Create Performance Task</h2>
      <p>The Create Performance Task is completed <strong>individually</strong> under current AP rules, so the program and every written response must be your own. Topic 1.2 is the backbone of the written responses. You are asked to <strong>describe the overall function and purpose</strong> of your program: state clearly what your program does (its function) and why you made it or what need it addresses (its purpose). Do not settle for one; a strong response names both. You are also asked to <strong>identify the input and the output</strong> of your program: point to a specific piece of data your program receives, whether from a user, a file, or a device, and a specific observable result it produces. Using the exact vocabulary from this lesson, function, purpose, input, output, and behavior, is what makes these responses earn their points.</p>
    </div>

        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A student describes a program by saying, "It exists so that visually impaired users can hear the text on a web page instead of reading it." Which aspect of the program is the student describing?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q1-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','A','B','q1-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> The function, because it names the observable behavior the program produces</button>

<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','D','B','q1-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> The behavior, because it names how the program responds to one input</button>
</div>
<div id="q1-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The observable behavior would be something like "it reads the page text aloud." This sentence gives the reason the program exists.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Naming the need (accessibility for visually impaired users) and who it serves describes the program's purpose, not what it observably does.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The input would be the text on the page. This sentence explains why the program was built.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Behavior connects a specific input to a response. This sentence gives the underlying reason the program exists.</div>

      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q2">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 2 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Spot the problem</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Decide what is missing from the description before you look.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>For the Create Task, a student writes: "My program takes a number the user types and prints whether it is even or odd." A teacher says the description is incomplete for the purpose requirement. What is the most accurate reason?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q2-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','A','C','q2-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> It never states which programming language was used to build the program</button>

<script>
(function(){

  // Each round: {kind, tag, q, io:[[in,out],...], ioHead:[inLabel,outLabel], opts:[...], answer:idx, fb:'rule'}
  var ROUNDS = [

      tag:'What is the purpose?',

    {
      // reversed style: given purpose, pick correct output
      tag:'Predict the output',
      q:'A program converts Celsius to Fahrenheit using F = C * 9/5 + 32. For the input C = 20, which output is correct?',
      ioHead:['Input','Output'],
      io:[['0','32'],['100','212']],

      answer:1,
      fb:'F = 20 * 9/5 + 32 = 36 + 32 = 68. The examples (0\u219232, 100\u2192212) confirm the same rule.'

      tag:'What is the purpose?',
      q:'A program takes two numbers and returns one number. What is its purpose?',

      q:'A program takes a string and returns a string. What is its purpose?',

  var round = 0, score = 0, streak = 0, answered = false;

  function updateBar(){

    streakEl.textContent = streak;
    progEl.style.width = ((round)/TOTAL*100) + '%';
  }

  function render(){
    updateBar();
    if(round >= TOTAL){ return renderEnd(); }
    answered = false;
    var r = ROUNDS[round];
    var rowsHtml = r.io.map(function(p){
      return '<div class="gp-ior"><span>'+esc(p[0])+'</span><span>'+esc(p[1])+'</span></div>';

    playEl.innerHTML =

      '</div>';

        <div class="faq-a">The function is what the program does, its observable behavior, such as "it displays the largest number in a list."   .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-opt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;padding:10px 14px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;font-family:monospace;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;background:#f8fafc;text-align:left;width:100%;transition:border-color .15s;}
  .mini-opt:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mini-opt.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .game-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .vt-stat{text-align:center;}
  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .vt-line{display:block;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;white-space:pre;}
  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .vt-question{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-options{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-btn{padding:12px;border-radius:9px;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);cursor:pointer;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;font-family:monospace;transition:all .15s;}
  .vt-btn:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:rgba(26,86,219,.2);}
  .vt-btn.c{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.15);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;}
  .vt-btn.w{border-color:#f87171;background:rgba(248,113,113,.15);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .vt-btn.rv{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.08);}
  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}
  .vt-fb.w{background:rgba(248,113,113,.1);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;display:block;}
  .vt-next{display:none;width:100%;padding:12px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .vt-next.show{display:block;}
  .vt-results{display:none;text-align:center;padding:20px;}
  .vt-results.show{display:block;}
  .vt-res-score{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:52px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-res-lbl{font-size:14px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .vt-res-msg{font-size:14px;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;margin-bottom:20px;line-height:1.6;}
  .vt-restart{background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;padding:11px 24px;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

  /* CODE EDITOR (Pyodide live) */
  .code-editor-section{background:#0f172a;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .code-editor-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .code-editor-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:22px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .code-editor-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .code-problem{background:rgba(255,255,255,.04);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08);border-radius:10px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .scaffold-badge{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:3px 10px;border-radius:100px;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .code-problem-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .code-problem-prompt{font-size:14px!important;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}

  .code-textarea{width:100%;min-height:120px;background:#020617;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0!important;resize:vertical;outline:none;line-height:1.8;}
  .code-textarea:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .code-btn-row{display:flex;gap:8px;margin-top:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;}
  .code-run-btn{padding:9px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:7px!important;font-size:13px!important;font-weight:700!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}

  .code-hint-btn,.code-sol-btn{padding:9px 16px!important;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06)!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.12)!important;border-radius:7px!important;font-size:13px!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .code-output{margin-top:10px;background:#020617;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;min-height:44px;display:none;line-height:1.7;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  .code-output.err{color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .code-hint{margin-top:8px;background:rgba(147,197,253,.06);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.2);border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;display:none;line-height:1.6;}

  .code-solution{margin-top:8px;background:rgba(74,222,128,.06);border:1px solid rgba(74,222,128,.2);border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#bbf7d0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bbf7d0!important;display:none;white-space:pre;line-height:1.8;overflow-x:auto;}
  .code-solution.show{display:block;}

  /* FAQ */
  .faq-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .faq-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .faq-item{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:10px;margin-bottom:10px;overflow:hidden;}
  .faq-q{width:100%;text-align:left;padding:16px 20px;background:none;border:none;cursor:pointer;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;font-family:inherit!important;line-height:1.4!important;}

      <p>A single light switch can be off or on, which is exactly two states. String eight of those switches together and you can spell any letter, store a number up to 255, or set the shade of one pixel. Computers do not understand the number 42, a photo, or the word cat directly, yet all three end up as nothing but 0s and 1s. How can two symbols possibly be enough to represent everything a computer stores?</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Bits, Bytes, and Why Two Symbols Are Enough</h2>
      <p>A <strong>bit</strong> is a binary digit: a single value that is either <code>0</code> or <code>1</code>. It is the smallest unit of data a computer stores. A <strong>byte</strong> is a group of <strong>8 bits</strong>. Computers represent <strong>all</strong> data — numbers, text, images, and sound — as sequences of bits. A photo, a song, and this sentence are all, underneath, just long strings of 0s and 1s. The meaning comes from how a program agrees to interpret those bits, not from the bits themselves.</p>
      <p>Two symbols are enough because you combine them in a <strong>place-value system</strong>, the same idea you already use in base ten. In decimal you have ten digits and each place is worth ten times the one to its right. <strong>Binary is base 2</strong>: only two digits, and each place is worth twice the one to its right. Add more bits and you can count higher, exactly the way adding another decimal digit lets you count past 9.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>Know the vocabulary cold: a <strong>bit</strong> is one 0 or 1, a <strong>byte</strong> is 8 bits, and <strong>every</strong> kind of data is stored as bits. A question that says a computer stores text or images "as binary" or "as sequences of bits" is stating a fact you are expected to already accept.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Binary Place Values and Converting to Decimal</h2>
      <p>Because binary is base 2, the place values are the <strong>powers of 2</strong>. Reading right to left they are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, and so on, each one double the last. To convert a binary number to decimal, write the place values above the bits and <strong>add up the place values wherever a 1 appears</strong>.</p>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Place value</th>
<th>128</th>
<th>64</th>
<th>32</th>
<th>16</th>
<th>8</th>
<th>4</th>
<th>2</th>
<th>1</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Binary digit</strong></td>
<td>0</td>
<td>0</td>
<td>0</td>
<td>0</td>
<td>1</td>
<td>0</td>
<td>1</td>
<td>1</td>
</tr>
      </table>
      <p>In the row above, 1s sit in the 8, 2, and 1 columns, so the value is <code>8 + 2 + 1 = 11</code>. That is how you read the binary number <code>1011</code> as decimal 11. The reverse direction, decimal to binary, is covered next.</p>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">Convert the binary number <code>1011</code> to decimal.</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-binary-1-opts">

        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-binary-1-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Converting Decimal to Binary</h2>
      <p>Two reliable methods give the same answer. Pick whichever you trust under time pressure.</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Subtract the largest power of 2.</strong> Find the biggest power of 2 that fits, put a 1 there, subtract it, and repeat with what is left. For 37: 32 fits, leaving 5; 4 fits, leaving 1; 1 fits, leaving 0. Ones go in the 32, 4, and 1 columns, giving <code>100101</code>.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Repeated division by 2.</strong> Divide by 2 and record each remainder. The remainders, read from <strong>bottom to top</strong>, are the binary digits. Dividing 37 gives remainders 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1 from last to first, which reads as <code>100101</code>.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>Check your work by converting back: <code>32 + 4 + 1 = 37</code>. If the place values you marked do not add to the original decimal number, one of the bits is wrong.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>With the division method, students read the remainders in the order they wrote them and get the number backwards. The correct order is <strong>bottom to top</strong> (last remainder first). Always sanity-check by adding the place values back to the original decimal.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How Many Values Can n Bits Hold?</h2>
      <p>With <code>n</code> bits you can represent <strong>2 to the n</strong> distinct values. Each bit doubles the count, because every existing pattern can now end in either a 0 or a 1. So 1 bit gives 2 values, 2 bits give 4, 3 bits give 8, and 8 bits (one byte) give <code>2^8 = 256</code> values. When those 256 values are used for whole numbers starting at zero, the range is <strong>0 to 255</strong>, not 1 to 256.</p>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Number of bits</th>
<th>Distinct values (2 to the n)</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td>1</td>
<td>2</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td>2</td>
<td>4</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td>4</td>
<td>16</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td>8 (one byte)</td>
<td>256</td>
</tr>
      </table>
      <p>This rule is the backbone of many exam questions. Adding a single bit does not add one more value, it <strong>doubles</strong> the number of values you can store.</p>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">Using 3 bits, how many distinct values can you represent?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-binary-2-opts">

        </div>

      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Analog vs Digital</h2>
      <p><strong>Analog</strong> data changes smoothly and continuously, with infinitely many possible values between any two points — think of a dimmer knob sliding, a real sound wave, or a shadow lengthening through the afternoon. <strong>Digital</strong> data uses <strong>discrete</strong> values: a finite set of separate steps, stored as bits. To put analog information into a computer you take <strong>samples</strong>, measuring the signal at many moments and recording each measurement as a number.</p>
      <p>A digital version is an <strong>approximation</strong> of the analog original, like a staircase tracing a ramp. The more samples you take and the more bits you use per sample, the closer the digital copy gets to the smooth original — but with a finite number of bits it can never be a perfect match.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>Match the keyword to the concept: <strong>continuous</strong> means analog, <strong>discrete</strong> or <strong>sampled</strong> means digital. Expect a question where more samples and more bits per sample yield a <strong>closer</strong> approximation of an analog signal, never an exact one.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Limits of Fixed Bit-Width: Overflow and Roundoff</h2>
      <p>Because a computer sets aside a fixed number of bits for a value, some numbers simply do not fit, and the framework names two specific errors that result.</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Overflow error:</strong> a value is <strong>too large</strong> to represent in the available bits. With 8 bits the largest whole number is 255; try to store 256 and there is no room, so the result is wrong.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Roundoff error:</strong> a value <strong>cannot be stored exactly</strong> and must be approximated or rounded. Many real numbers, such as the result of <code>1 / 3</code>, would need infinitely many digits, so a fixed number of bits can only hold a rounded version.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>The clean split: overflow is about a number being <strong>too big to fit at all</strong>; roundoff is about a number being <strong>impossible to store precisely</strong>, so it is stored close-but-not-exact. Both come from the same root cause, a finite number of bits.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>Do not swap the two. If a program adds 1 to the largest value a variable can hold and gets a nonsense result, that is <strong>overflow</strong>. If a program stores 0.1 or 1/3 and later the arithmetic is slightly off, that is <strong>roundoff</strong>. "Too large to represent" is overflow; "cannot be represented exactly" is roundoff.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Many Representations, Real Tradeoffs</h2>
      <p>The same information can be represented in more than one way, and the choice has consequences. The number eleven can be written as decimal <code>11</code> or binary <code>1011</code>; both mean the same quantity. Using more bits per value widens the range you can store and reduces overflow and roundoff, but it also uses more memory and storage. Representations are chosen by weighing these <strong>tradeoffs</strong>, which is a theme you will see again in data compression.</p>
    </div>

      <h2>How Binary Is Tested on the Exam</h2>
      <p>Binary number representation is <strong>multiple-choice material</strong>, not a skill you demonstrate on the Create Performance Task. You will not hand-convert numbers inside your Create Task program; instead the end-of-course multiple-choice exam asks you to convert between binary and decimal, apply the <strong>2 to the n</strong> rule, and tell overflow apart from roundoff. Treat this as fast, high-confidence points.</p>
      <p>Quick strategy for the exam room:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Write the place values first.</strong> Jot 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1 across the top and line the bits up underneath. For binary to decimal, add the place values under each 1.</li>
        <li>
<strong>For decimal to binary, subtract the largest power of 2</strong> that fits, mark a 1, and repeat with the remainder.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Always check by converting back.</strong> Add your marked place values; they must equal the original decimal number.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Sort the error type by keyword.</strong> "Too large to store" is overflow; "cannot be stored exactly" is roundoff.</li>
      </ul>

<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','A','C','q6-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> It is an exact copy of the analog wave, because every point of the wave is stored</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','B','C','q6-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> It is analog data, because sound is continuous by nature</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','C','C','q6-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> It is an approximation of the analog wave, and taking more samples with more bits each makes it closer to the original</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','D','C','q6-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> It is digital only if the wave never changes, since digital data cannot represent change</button>
</div>
<div id="q6-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. A finite set of samples cannot capture every point of a continuous wave, so it is an approximation, not an exact copy.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Storing measurements as numbers makes the recording digital and discrete, even though the source was analog.</div>

<div id="q6-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Digital data represents change fine by storing many samples over time; that is exactly how the recording works.</div>

<script>
(function () {
  var PLACES = [128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1];
  var GAME_SECONDS = 60;

  var state = {
    time: GAME_SECONDS,
    score: 0,
    streak: 0,
    bestStreak: 0,
    correct: 0,
    rounds: 0,
    mode: 'build',      // 'build' or 'read'
    target: 0,          // build: decimal to make ; read: decimal answer
    bits: [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0], // build mode player toggles ; read mode fixed pattern
    locked: false,
    timerId: null
  };

  var el = {};
  ['time','score','streak-val','best','timerfill','start','play','end','flash',
   'rtype','prompt','target','places','bitrow','sumline','answerrow','input',
   'checkbtn','feedback','startbtn','againbtn','endscore','endbest','endright',
   'endmsg','endtitle'].forEach(function (id) {
    el[id] = document.getElementById('bcr-' + id);
  });

  // Build the static place-value header once.
  PLACES.forEach(function (p) {
    var d = document.createElement('div');
    d.className = 'bcr-place';
    d.textContent = String(p);
    el.places.appendChild(d);
  });

  // Build the 8 bit cells once; behavior depends on mode.
  var bitCells = [];
  for (var i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
    (function (idx) {
      var b = document.createElement('button');
      b.className = 'bcr-bit';
      b.type = 'button';
      b.textContent = '0';
      b.addEventListener('click', function () {
        if (state.mode !== 'build' || state.locked) return;
        state.bits[idx] = state.bits[idx] ? 0 : 1;
        renderBits();
        renderSum();
      });
      bitCells.push(b);
      el.bitrow.appendChild(b);
    })(i);
  }

  function bitsValue(bits) {
    var s = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < 8; i++) if (bits[i]) s += PLACES[i];
    return s;
  }

  function bitsString(bits) {
    return bits.join('');
  }

  function renderBits() {
    for (var i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
      var on = !!state.bits[i];
      bitCells[i].textContent = on ? '1' : '0';
      bitCells[i].className = 'bcr-bit' + (on ? ' bcr-on' : '') +
        (state.mode === 'read' ? ' bcr-ro' : '');
    }
  }

  function renderSum() {
    if (state.mode === 'build') {
      var parts = [];
      for (var i = 0; i < 8; i++) if (state.bits[i]) parts.push(PLACES[i]);
      var sum = bitsValue(state.bits);
      if (parts.length === 0) {
        el.sumline.innerHTML = 'Current value: <b>0</b>';
      } else {
        el.sumline.innerHTML = 'Current value: ' + parts.join(' + ') + ' = <b>' + sum + '</b>';
      }
    } else {
      el.sumline.innerHTML = 'Pattern: <b>' + bitsString(state.bits) + '</b>  -  add the lit place values.';
    }
  }

  function randInt(max) { return Math.floor(Math.random() * (max + 1)); } // 0..max

  // Difficulty ramps by rounds played.
  function targetForRound(r) {
    if (r < 3) return randInt(15) + 1;          // 1..16 -> small, 4 low bits area
    if (r < 6) return randInt(31);              // 0..31
    if (r < 10) return randInt(63);             // 0..63
    return randInt(255);                        // full range 0..255
  }

  function nextRound() {
    state.locked = false;
    el.feedback.textContent = '';
    el.feedback.className = 'bcr-feedback';
    el.input.value = '';

    // Alternate modes each round.
    state.mode = (state.rounds % 2 === 0) ? 'build' : 'read';
    var val = targetForRound(state.rounds);
    state.target = val;

    if (state.mode === 'build') {
      state.bits = [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0];
      el.rtype.textContent = 'Build the number';
      el.prompt.textContent = 'Toggle bits so the binary equals this decimal:';
      el.target.textContent = String(val);
      el.target.classList.remove('bcr-hidden');
      el.answerrow.classList.add('bcr-hidden');
      el.checkbtn.textContent = 'Check';
    } else {
      // Read the bits: display fixed pattern of the target value.
      var bits = [];
      for (var i = 0; i < 8; i++) bits.push((val & PLACES[i]) ? 1 : 0);
      state.bits = bits;
      el.rtype.textContent = 'Read the bits';
      el.prompt.textContent = 'What decimal value does this 8-bit pattern equal?';
      el.target.classList.add('bcr-hidden');
      el.answerrow.classList.remove('bcr-hidden');
      el.checkbtn.textContent = 'Check';
      setTimeout(function () { try { el.input.focus(); } catch (e) {} }, 30);
    }

    renderBits();
    renderSum();
    updateStats();
  }

  function flash(good) {
    el.flash.className = 'bcr-flash ' + (good ? 'bcr-good' : 'bcr-bad');
    // force reflow to restart animation
    void el.flash.offsetWidth;
  }

  function explainWrong() {
    if (state.mode === 'build') {
      var got = bitsValue(state.bits);
      var want = state.target;
      var parts = [];
      for (var i = 0; i < 8; i++) if (state.bits[i]) parts.push(PLACES[i]);
      var gotExpr = parts.length ? parts.join(' + ') + ' = ' + got : '0';
      return bitsString(state.bits) + ' is ' + gotExpr + ', not ' + want + '. Check the place values.';
    } else {
      var parts2 = [];
      for (var j = 0; j < 8; j++) if (state.bits[j]) parts2.push(PLACES[j]);
      var expr = parts2.length ? parts2.join(' + ') + ' = ' + state.target : '0';
      return bitsString(state.bits) + ' is ' + expr + '. Add every lit place value.';
    }
  }

  function check() {
    if (state.locked || el.play.classList.contains('bcr-hidden')) return;

    var isCorrect;
    if (state.mode === 'build') {
      isCorrect = (bitsValue(state.bits) === state.target);
    } else {
      var raw = (el.input.value || '').trim();
      if (raw === '' || !/^\d+$/.test(raw)) {
        el.feedback.className = 'bcr-feedback bcr-no';
        el.feedback.textContent = 'Enter a whole number 0-255.';
        return;
      }
      isCorrect = (parseInt(raw, 10) === state.target);
    }

    state.rounds++;

    if (isCorrect) {
      state.streak++;
      if (state.streak > state.bestStreak) state.bestStreak = state.streak;
      state.correct++;
      var base = 10;
      var bonus = Math.min(state.streak - 1, 5) * 5; // up to +25 streak bonus
      var gained = base + bonus;
      state.score += gained;
      flash(true);
      el.feedback.className = 'bcr-feedback bcr-ok';
      var comboTxt = state.streak >= 2
        ? ' <span class="bcr-combo">' + state.streak + 'x combo! +' + gained + '</span>'
        : ' +' + gained;
      el.feedback.innerHTML = 'Correct!' + comboTxt;
      updateStats();
      state.locked = true;
      setTimeout(function () { if (state.time > 0) nextRound(); }, 520);
    } else {
      state.streak = 0;
      flash(false);
      el.feedback.className = 'bcr-feedback bcr-no';
      el.feedback.textContent = explainWrong();
      updateStats();
      // allow retry on same round (no auto-advance)
    }
  }

  function updateStats() {
    el.time.textContent = String(state.time);
    el.score.textContent = String(state.score);
    el['streak-val'].textContent = String(state.streak);
    el.best.textContent = String(state.bestStreak);
    if (state.time <= 10) el.time.classList.add('bcr-low'); else el.time.classList.remove('bcr-low');
    if (state.streak >= 3) el['streak-val'].classList.add('bcr-hot'); else el['streak-val'].classList.remove('bcr-hot');
    var pct = Math.max(0, (state.time / GAME_SECONDS) * 100);
    el.timerfill.style.width = pct + '%';
  }

  function tick() {
    state.time--;
    if (state.time <= 0) {
      state.time = 0;
      updateStats();
      endGame();
      return;
    }
    updateStats();
  }

  function startGame() {
    state.time = GAME_SECONDS;
    state.score = 0;
    state.streak = 0;
    state.bestStreak = 0;
    state.correct = 0;
    state.rounds = 0;
    state.locked = false;

    el.start.classList.add('bcr-hidden');
    el.end.classList.add('bcr-hidden');
    el.play.classList.remove('bcr-hidden');

    updateStats();
    nextRound();

    if (state.timerId) clearInterval(state.timerId);
    state.timerId = setInterval(tick, 1000);
  }

  function endGame() {
    if (state.timerId) { clearInterval(state.timerId); state.timerId = null; }
    state.locked = true;
    el.play.classList.add('bcr-hidden');
    el.end.classList.remove('bcr-hidden');

    el.endscore.textContent = String(state.score);
    el.endbest.textContent = String(state.bestStreak);
    el.endright.textContent = String(state.correct);

    var msg;
    if (state.score >= 200) msg = 'Binary master! You can read place values in your sleep.';
    else if (state.score >= 120) msg = 'Great pace! Place value 128-64-32-16-8-4-2-1 is clicking.';
    else if (state.score >= 60) msg = 'Solid run. Keep chaining streaks for the bonus points.';
    else msg = 'Good start! Remember: each bit is worth double the one to its right.';
    el.endmsg.textContent = msg;

    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsGameScore', { detail: { value: state.score } }));
  }

  el.startbtn.addEventListener('click', startGame);
  el.againbtn.addEventListener('click', startGame);
  el.checkbtn.addEventListener('click', check);
  el.input.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
    if (e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); check(); }
  });
})();
</script>

        <div class="faq-a">A bit is a single binary digit, either 0 or 1, and is the smallest unit of data. A byte is a group of 8 bits. Computers represent all data, including numbers, text, images, and sound, as sequences of bits.</div>

        <div class="faq-a">Write the place values 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1 above the bits, then add up the place values everywhere a 1 appears. For example, 1011 has 1s in the 8, 2, and 1 columns, so it equals 8 + 2 + 1 = 11.</div>

      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why can 8 bits store only 256 different values?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">With n bits you can represent 2 to the n distinct values, because each bit doubles the number of patterns. Eight bits give 2 to the 8 = 256 values. When used for whole numbers starting at 0, that range is 0 to 255.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between overflow and roundoff errors?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Overflow happens when a value is too large to represent in the available bits, such as going past the maximum a variable can hold. Roundoff happens when a value cannot be stored exactly, like many real numbers, so it is approximated. Overflow is too big to fit; roundoff is impossible to store precisely.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What does analog versus digital mean on the exam?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Analog data changes smoothly and continuously with infinitely many possible values. Digital data uses discrete, separate values stored as bits. Analog signals are turned into digital data by sampling, and more samples with more bits per sample give a closer approximation of the original.</div>

  /* CALLOUTS */

  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .mini-opt:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:var(--bi3-bg);}

  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}

  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}

  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}

  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}

  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}

  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .game-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .vt-stat{text-align:center;}
  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .vt-line{display:block;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;white-space:pre;}
  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .vt-question{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-options{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-btn{padding:12px;border-radius:9px;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);cursor:pointer;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;font-family:monospace;transition:all .15s;}
  .vt-btn:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:rgba(26,86,219,.2);}
  .vt-btn.c{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.15);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;}
  .vt-btn.w{border-color:#f87171;background:rgba(248,113,113,.15);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .vt-btn.rv{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.08);}
  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}
  .vt-fb.w{background:rgba(248,113,113,.1);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;display:block;}
  .vt-next{display:none;width:100%;padding:12px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
