  .lesson-hero-inner{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;}
  .lesson-hero-meta{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .lesson-num-badge{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:44px;height:44px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;font-size:14px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;flex-shrink:0;}
  .lesson-eyebrow{font-size:12px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;}
  .lesson-hero h1{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:clamp(26px,4vw,40px)!important;line-height:1.2!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;}
  .lesson-hero-pills{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-pill{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.08);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);padding:5px 12px;border-radius:100px;font-size:12px;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .ced-tag{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;background:rgba(26,86,219,.25);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.3);padding:4px 10px;border-radius:100px;font-size:11px;font-weight:600;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;letter-spacing:.04em;}

  /* PROGRESS STRIP */
  .bi3-progress{background:#fff!important;border-bottom:1px solid #e2e8f0!important;padding:14px 20px!important;overflow-x:auto!important;-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch!important;}
  .bi3-progress-inner{display:flex!important;flex-direction:row!important;flex-wrap:nowrap!important;align-items:center!important;gap:0!important;width:max-content!important;min-width:100%!important;}
  .prog-step{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-step-link{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;text-decoration:none!important;cursor:pointer!important;}
  .prog-step-link:hover .prog-dot{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-dot{width:26px!important;height:26px!important;border-radius:50%!important;display:flex!important;align-items:center!important;justify-content:center!important;font-size:9px!important;font-weight:700!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-dot.active{background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;}
  .prog-dot.upcoming{background:#f1f5f9!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;}
  .prog-dot.done{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border:2px solid var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-label{font-size:8px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;line-height:1.2!important;white-space:nowrap!important;}
  .prog-label.active-label{color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-arrow{flex:1 0 4px!important;height:2px!important;background:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:18px!important;min-width:4px!important;max-width:16px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}

  /* MAIN */
  .lesson-main{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;padding:40px 24px 80px;}
  .lesson-objectives{background:var(--bi3-bg);border-left:4px solid var(--bi3);border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin-bottom:28px;}
  .lesson-objectives h2{font-size:14px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;text-transform:uppercase!important;letter-spacing:.06em!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .lesson-objectives ul{list-style:none;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-objectives li{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#1e3a8a;line-height:1.5;}
  .lesson-objectives li::before{content:"\2713";color:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:1px;}
  .score-impact{background:#f0fdf4;border:1px solid #bbf7d0;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 18px;margin-bottom:28px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#14532d;}
  .score-impact strong{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}

  /* HOOK */
  .hook-box{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:32px;}
  .hook-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .hook-box p{font-size:15px!important;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:0!important;}

  /* LESSON SECTIONS */
  .lesson-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .lesson-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .lesson-section h3{font-size:17px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-top:24px!important;margin-bottom:10px!important;}
  .lesson-section p{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section ul,.lesson-section ol{padding-left:20px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section li{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .lesson-section code{background:#eef2ff;color:#1e3a8a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e3a8a!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}

  /* DUAL CODE PANEL */
  .code-panel-wrap{margin:20px 0;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;}
  .code-panel-tabs{display:flex;background:#1e293b;}
  .code-tab{padding:8px 16px;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;border:none;background:transparent;letter-spacing:.04em;transition:background .15s;font-family:inherit;}
  .code-tab.py{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.pseudo{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.active{background:rgba(255,255,255,.15)!important;}
  .code-tab-label{font-size:10px;opacity:.6;margin-left:4px;font-weight:400;}
  .code-pane{background:#0f172a;padding:18px 20px;overflow-x:auto;height:0;overflow:hidden;padding:0;}
  .code-pane.active{height:auto;overflow-x:auto;padding:18px 20px;}
  .code-pane pre{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:0;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;max-width:100%;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-kw{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .py-fn{color:#6ee7b7!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#6ee7b7!important;}
  .py-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .py-str{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .py-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .py-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-op{color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;}
  .ps-kw{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .ps-op{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .ps-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .ps-str{color:#86efac!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#86efac!important;}
  .ps-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .ps-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* CALLOUTS */
  .callout-exam{background:#fffbeb;border:1px solid #fcd34d;border-left:4px solid var(--amber);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-exam-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--amber)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--amber)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-exam p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}
  .callout-trap{background:#fef2f2;border:1px solid #fca5a5;border-left:4px solid var(--red);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-opt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;padding:10px 14px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;font-family:monospace;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;background:#f8fafc;text-align:left;width:100%;transition:border-color .15s;}
  .mini-opt:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mini-opt.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>Suppose a program checks every pair of students in a class to find matching birthdays. With 10 students that is about 100 checks. Double the class to 20 and it is not 200 checks, it is about 400. The work grew four times as fast as the class. Now imagine a program that tries every possible combination of choices: at 10 items it is about a thousand steps, but at 60 items it is more steps than a fast computer could finish in a lifetime. This lesson is about predicting how fast an algorithm's work grows, and why some algorithms are usable while others are hopeless.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Efficiency Means Counting Steps, Not Seconds</h2>
      <p><strong>Algorithmic efficiency</strong> is about how the amount of work an algorithm does grows as the size of its input grows. The size of the input is usually called <code>n</code>: the number of items in a list, the number of users, the number of pixels. The key question is not "how many seconds does it take" but "how many steps does it take, and how does that step count change when <code>n</code> gets bigger."</p>
      <p>We deliberately count steps instead of timing with a clock. A stopwatch measures the computer, the network, and what else the machine happens to be doing. Counting steps measures the <strong>algorithm itself</strong>, so the answer is the same on a fast laptop or a slow phone. To make this concrete, every example below uses a <code>count</code> variable that goes up by one each time the algorithm does a unit of work, and then prints the total.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-1')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-1')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-1-py"><pre><span class="py-comment"># ONE loop over n items: about n steps (linear)</span>
<span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">0</span>
<span class="py-kw">for</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">i</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">in</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">range</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">1</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-1-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">0</span>
<span class="ps-kw">REPEAT</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">TIMES</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>A single loop that runs <code>n</code> times does about <code>n</code> steps. We call this <strong>linear</strong> growth: double the input and you roughly double the work. If <code>n</code> is 5 the count is 5; if <code>n</code> is 500 the count is 500. Simple and predictable.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>The CED (AAP-4.A) asks you to compare algorithms by the number of steps they take relative to the input size. On the exam you will not compute exact runtimes. You will reason about how the step count <em>grows</em>: linear, then squared, then explosively.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Nested Loops Multiply</h2>
      <p>Put one loop inside another and the work explodes. For every single pass of the outer loop, the inner loop runs all the way through. So an inner loop of <code>n</code> steps running inside an outer loop of <code>n</code> steps does about <code>n</code> times <code>n</code> steps. This is <strong>quadratic</strong> growth, often written <code>n</code> squared.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-2')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-2')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-2-py"><pre><span class="py-comment"># NESTED loop: about n times n steps (quadratic)</span>
<span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">0</span>
<span class="py-kw">for</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">i</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">in</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">range</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">for</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">j</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">in</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">range</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">1</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-2-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">0</span>
<span class="ps-kw">REPEAT</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">TIMES</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">REPEAT</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">TIMES</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>

      <p>The single most common mistake is thinking nested loops <em>add</em>. They do not. Two loops side by side add (that is <code>n</code> plus <code>n</code>, which is <code>2n</code>). Two loops nested multiply (that is <code>n</code> times <code>n</code>). Compare the nested version above with two separate loops below, which only reach <code>2n</code>.</p>

<span class="py-kw">for</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">i</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">in</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">range</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">1</span>
<span class="py-kw">for</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">j</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">in</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">range</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">1</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>

        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ The multiply-vs-add trap</div>
        <p>Nested loops multiply; separate loops add. And because quadratic grows so fast, <strong>doubling</strong> the input roughly <strong>quadruples</strong> the work. If <code>n</code> going from 10 to 20 turns 100 steps into 400 steps, you are looking at <code>n</code> squared. A favorite MCQ hands you a nested loop and offers <code>2n</code> as a tempting wrong answer.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Reasonable Time vs Unreasonable Time</h2>
      <p>The CED draws one big line. An algorithm runs in <strong>reasonable time</strong> when its step count grows like a <strong>polynomial</strong> in <code>n</code>: <code>n</code>, or <code>n</code> squared, or <code>n</code> cubed. These grow, but at a pace we can plan around. An algorithm runs in <strong>unreasonable time</strong> when its step count grows like an <strong>exponential</strong>, such as <code>2</code> to the <code>n</code>. Exponential growth starts small and then detonates.</p>
      <p>Look at the numbers. For <code>2</code> to the <code>n</code>: at <code>n</code> = 10 it is about a thousand, at <code>n</code> = 20 about a million, at <code>n</code> = 40 about a trillion, at <code>n</code> = 60 it is more steps than a fast computer could finish in a lifetime. An exponential-time solution becomes <strong>infeasible</strong> almost immediately as the input grows, even though it may look harmless for tiny inputs. That is why "it works on my small test" is not proof that an algorithm is efficient.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Faster-growing eventually loses</div>
        <p>An algorithm that grows faster can still be quicker on tiny inputs and yet lose badly as <code>n</code> grows. Suppose one algorithm takes <code>n</code> squared steps and another takes <code>500</code> times <code>n</code> steps. For small <code>n</code> the first is faster, but once <code>n</code> passes 500 the <code>n</code> squared one takes far more steps. Efficiency is about the trend as <code>n</code> grows, not the score on one small case.</p>
      </div>

      <h2>When Exact Is Too Slow: Heuristics</h2>
      <p>Some problems have no known efficient (reasonable-time) exact solution. Finding the truly shortest route that visits many cities is a classic example: checking every possible order is exponential and hopeless past a few dozen cities. When an exact answer is out of reach, we use a <strong>heuristic</strong>: a rule of thumb that produces a <strong>good-enough</strong> answer quickly, without guaranteeing the best possible answer.</p>
      <p>A delivery app that always drives to the nearest unvisited stop next is using a heuristic. The route it builds is usually close to optimal and it is computed in reasonable time, which is a trade every real system makes: give up a guarantee of perfection to get an answer you can actually use. On the exam, remember the definition: a heuristic gives an approximate, good-enough solution faster than an exact method, and it is what you reach for when an efficient exact algorithm is not known.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 Trace it like a machine</div>
        <p>To answer a counting-steps question: find the loops, decide whether they are separate (add) or nested (multiply), and count how many times the innermost work runs. One loop over <code>n</code> is <code>n</code>. A loop inside a loop is <code>n</code> times <code>n</code>. Then classify: polynomial is reasonable, exponential is unreasonable.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="cpt-connection">
      <div class="cpt-connection-label">📋 Create Performance Task • Reasoning about your algorithm</div>
      <p>The Create Task written response asks you to describe an algorithm in your program that includes selection and iteration. Understanding efficiency helps you describe that algorithm precisely and choose a structure that actually runs in reasonable time.</p>
      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>Suppose your program compares every item to every other item, for example to find duplicate entries. That is a nested loop, and you should be able to state how much work it does:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">count <- 0
REPEAT n TIMES
{
    REPEAT n TIMES
    {
        count <- count + 1
    }
}
DISPLAY(count)</div>
      <p>In your written response, describe the algorithm and its iteration honestly:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"The outer loop runs once for each of the <code>n</code> items, and for each pass the inner loop also runs <code>n</code> times."</li>
        <li>"So the algorithm does about <code>n</code> times <code>n</code> steps, which grows quadratically as the list gets larger."</li>
        <li>"This is polynomial growth, so the program still runs in reasonable time for the input sizes it is designed to handle."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The trap to avoid</h3>
      <p>Do not claim two nested loops do <code>2n</code> steps. Nested loops multiply, so it is <code>n</code> times <code>n</code>. If a single loop would solve the problem, prefer it: choosing a linear structure over a needless quadratic one is exactly the kind of design decision that shows real understanding. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What does algorithmic efficiency actually measure?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Efficiency measures how the number of steps an algorithm takes grows as the input size n grows. We count steps rather than timing with a clock, because a clock also measures the hardware and other running programs. Counting steps describes the algorithm itself, so the answer is the same on any machine.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why do nested loops multiply instead of add?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Because the inner loop runs all the way through for every single pass of the outer loop. If the outer loop runs n times and the inner loop runs n times, the inner work happens n times n times. Two loops that are side by side rather than nested each run once, so their steps add to about 2n.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between reasonable and unreasonable time?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Reasonable time means the step count grows like a polynomial, such as n, n squared, or n cubed. Unreasonable time means it grows like an exponential, such as 2 to the n. Exponential growth starts small but explodes, so an unreasonable-time solution becomes infeasible almost immediately as the input grows.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">If an algorithm is faster on small inputs, is it more efficient?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Not necessarily. Efficiency is about the trend as n grows, not one small case. An algorithm that grows faster can win on tiny inputs and still lose badly for large n. For example n squared beats 500 times n while n is under 500, but past that point the quadratic one takes far more steps.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is a heuristic and when do you use one?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A heuristic is a rule of thumb that produces a good-enough, approximate answer quickly, without guaranteeing the best possible answer. You use one when no efficient exact solution is known, such as finding the shortest route through many cities. It trades a guarantee of perfection for an answer you can compute in reasonable time.</div>
      </div>

  var code=document.getElementById('ce-'+n).value;var res=execUser(py,code);
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);
  if(res.err){out.className='code-output show err';out.textContent='\u2717 Error:\n'+res.err;}
  else{var got=(res.output||'').replace(/\s+$/,'');var exp=CE_EXPECTED[n];
    var shown=res.output&&res.output.length?res.output.replace(/\n$/,''):'(no output)';
    if(exp!==undefined&&got===exp){out.className='code-output show ok';out.textContent='\u2713 Correct! Output:\n'+shown;if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}

    else{out.className='code-output show';out.textContent='Output:\n'+shown;}
    if(typeof exp!=='undefined')_activity({activity:'exercise-1',item:'ce-'+n,correct:(got===exp)});}
  if(btn)btn.disabled=false;}
function showHint(n){var box=document.getElementById('ce-hint-'+n);
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]===undefined)CE_HINT_IDX[n]=0;var hints=CE_HINTS[n]||[];
  if(hints.length===0)return;

  var shown=CE_HINT_IDX[n]+1;var text='';

  LESSON_USAGE.hints[n]=shown;LESSON_USAGE.totalHints=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.hints);updateUsage();
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]<hints.length-1)CE_HINT_IDX[n]++;
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}

function vtRender(){if(vtQ>=VT_QS.length){vtShowResults();return;}vtAnswered=false;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  document.getElementById('vt-qn').textContent=(vtQ+1)+'/'+VT_QS.length;

  var btns=document.querySelectorAll('.vt-btn');btns.forEach(function(b){b.onclick=null;});

  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}

  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}

  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}

  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .game-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .vt-stat{text-align:center;}
  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .vt-line{display:block;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;white-space:pre;}
  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .vt-question{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-options{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-btn{padding:12px;border-radius:9px;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);cursor:pointer;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;font-family:monospace;transition:all .15s;}
  .vt-btn:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:rgba(26,86,219,.2);}
  .vt-btn.c{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.15);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;}
  .vt-btn.w{border-color:#f87171;background:rgba(248,113,113,.15);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .vt-btn.rv{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.08);}
  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}
  .vt-fb.w{background:rgba(248,113,113,.1);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;display:block;}
  .vt-next{display:none;width:100%;padding:12px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

  .vt-results{display:none;text-align:center;padding:20px;}
  .vt-results.show{display:block;}
  .vt-res-score{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:52px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}

  .code-editor-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .code-problem-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}

  /* FAQ */

  .related-links-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(200px,1fr));gap:8px;}

    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>Think about finding a word in a physical dictionary. You do not start at page one and read every entry. You open to the middle, see whether your word comes before or after, and instantly ignore half the book. Repeat a few times and you are there. That is binary search. It is dramatically faster than checking every page, but it only works because a dictionary is already sorted.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What Binary Search Is</h2>
      <p><strong>Binary search</strong> is a fast way to find a value in a list. Instead of checking items one at a time, it repeatedly looks at the <strong>middle</strong> element and throws away half of the remaining items with a single comparison. Because it can discard half the data on every step, it reaches an answer in far fewer checks than looking at each item in turn.</p>
      <p>There is one hard requirement: <strong>the data must already be sorted</strong>. Binary search only works because comparing the target to the middle element tells you which half the target must be in. If the list is not in order, that comparison tells you nothing, and the search can skip right past the value it is looking for.</p>

Since 12 < 23, everything from index 3 and below is eliminated and the search continues in the upper half. The next middle is index 5 (value 23), a match. Binary search found the value in just two checks, while looking one by one could have taken six.</p>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Linear Search vs Binary Search</h2>
      <p><strong>Linear search</strong> checks each element from the start until it finds the target or runs off the end. It is simple and it works on <strong>any</strong> list, sorted or not, but for a list of n items it may need up to n comparisons.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">

<span class="ps-var">}</span>

      <p>Binary search trades that flexibility for speed. It demands a sorted list, but in return it finds a value (or reports it is missing) in about <strong>log2(n)</strong> steps because each step halves the remaining items. The difference grows fast: a list of 1000 items takes up to 1000 checks with linear search but only about 10 with binary search, since 2 to the 10th power is 1024. Double the list to 2000 items and binary search needs just one more step.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 The number-of-steps shortcut</div>
        <p>To estimate binary search steps, ask how many times you can halve n before reaching 1. That is log2(n). Handy anchors: 8 items take about 3 steps, 16 take about 4, 1000 take about 10, and 1,000,000 take about 20. Linear search on those same lists could take 8, 16, 1000, and 1,000,000 checks.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How the Halving Works: low, high, and mid</h2>
      <p>Binary search keeps track of the region of the list still worth searching using two markers: <code>low</code> (the first index of that region) and <code>high</code> (the last index). Each step it computes the middle index as <code>mid = (low + high) // 2</code> and compares <code>data[mid]</code> to the target. That one comparison decides which half survives:</p>
      <ul class="rules">
        <li>if <code>data[mid]</code> equals the target: found it, stop</li>
        <li>if <code>data[mid] < target</code>: the target must be to the right, so set <code>low = mid + 1</code>
</li>
        <li>if <code>data[mid] > target</code>: the target must be to the left, so set <code>high = mid - 1</code>
</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-3')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-3')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-3-py"><pre><span class="py-var">data</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">4</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">9</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">15</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">22</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">30</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">41</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">55</span><span class="py-var">]</span>
<span class="py-var">target</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">41</span>
<span class="py-var">low</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">0</span>
<span class="py-var">high</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">6</span>
<span class="py-var">mid</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">low</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">high</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment">// 2</span>
<span class="py-kw">if</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">data</span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-var">mid</span><span class="py-var">]</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"><</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">target</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">low</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">mid</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">1</span>
<span class="py-kw">else</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">high</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">mid</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">-</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">1</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-3-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">low</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>
<span class="ps-var">high</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">7</span>
<span class="ps-var">mid</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">low</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">high</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">/</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span>
<span class="ps-kw">IF</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">data</span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-var">mid</span><span class="ps-var">]</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">target</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">low</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">mid</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">ELSE</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">high</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">mid</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Here the middle value 22 is less than the target 41, so the entire lower half (indices 0 through 3, including the middle) is eliminated and <code>low</code> jumps to 4. Notice you move past <code>mid</code> with <code>mid + 1</code> or <code>mid - 1</code>, never leaving it in the region. The loop ends when <code>low</code> passes <code>high</code>, which means the region is empty and the value is not present.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Two classic traps</div>
        <p>First, binary search on <strong>unsorted</strong> data is simply wrong; it can report "not found" for a value that is actually in the list. Second, watch the off-by-one: writing <code>low = mid</code> instead of <code>low = mid + 1</code> can leave <code>low</code> and <code>high</code> stuck on the same spot forever, an infinite loop. Always step past <code>mid</code>.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="mini-ex">

      <h2>Tracing Binary Search by Hand</h2>
      <p>Use one disciplined procedure and these traces become mechanical:</p>
      <ol>
        <li>Write the current <strong>low</strong> and <strong>high</strong>. Start with low at the first index and high at the last.</li>
        <li>Compute <code>mid = (low + high) // 2</code> using integer division (drop any fraction).</li>
        <li>Compare <code>data[mid]</code> to the target. If equal, you are done.</li>
        <li>If <code>data[mid]</code> is too small, set <code>low = mid + 1</code>. If it is too big, set <code>high = mid - 1</code>.</li>
        <li>Repeat until you find the target or <code>low</code> becomes greater than <code>high</code>, which means not found.</li>
      </ol>
      <p>Counting the number of times you compute a new <code>mid</code> gives the number of steps, which is what step-counting questions ask for. Computing <code>mid</code> correctly is the single most common place students slip, so practice it directly below.</p>

      <div class="cpt-connection-label">📋 Create Performance Task • Binary search as an algorithm you can explain</div>
      <p>Binary search is a strong choice for the algorithm your Create Task program develops, because it combines <strong>iteration</strong> (the loop that keeps narrowing the region) with <strong>selection</strong> (the comparison that decides which half to keep). That combination is exactly what the rubric asks you to identify and explain in your written responses.</p>
      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>Suppose your program searches a sorted list of scores for a target value:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">low <- 1
high <- LENGTH(scores)
REPEAT UNTIL (low > high)
{
    mid <- (low + high) / 2
    IF (scores[mid] = target)
    {
        DISPLAY(mid)
    }
    ELSE
    {
        IF (scores[mid] < target)
        {
            low <- mid + 1
        }
        ELSE
        {
            high <- mid - 1
        }
    }
}</div>
      <p>In your written response, name the algorithm and explain how the loop and the comparison work together:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"My algorithm uses binary search, which requires the list to be sorted first."</li>
        <li>"Each iteration computes the middle index and compares <code>scores[mid]</code> to the target, then updates <code>low</code> or <code>high</code> to keep only the half that could contain the target."</li>
        <li>"Because it eliminates half the remaining items each time, it finds the value in about log2(n) steps instead of up to n."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The trap to avoid</h3>
      <p>Do not claim binary search on a list you never sorted. If your data is not in order, the algorithm is incorrect and your explanation loses credibility. Sort first, or describe a linear search instead. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why does binary search require sorted data?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Binary search decides which half of the list to keep by comparing the target to the middle element. That comparison is only meaningful if the elements are in order. On an unsorted list, a smaller middle value does not guarantee the target is to the right, so the search can eliminate the half that actually contains the value and report it as not found.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How many steps does binary search take?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">About <code>log2(n)</code> steps for a list of n items, because each step eliminates half of what remains. A list of 1000 items takes at most about 10 checks, and 1,000,000 items takes about 20. Linear search on those same lists could take up to 1000 and 1,000,000 checks.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How is mid calculated?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">The middle index is <code>mid = (low + high) // 2</code> using integer division, which drops any fraction. For example, with low 0 and high 6, mid is 3. Computing mid is the single most common place students make an error, so it is worth practicing directly.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between binary search and linear search?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Linear search checks each element one at a time and works on any list, sorted or not, but may need up to n comparisons. Binary search is much faster at about log2(n) steps, but it only works when the data is already sorted. Choose linear search for small or unsorted data and binary search for large sorted data.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">When does binary search report not found?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">When the region being searched empties out, meaning <code>low</code> becomes greater than <code>high</code>, the value is not in the list. A common way to handle this is to store the found index in a variable that starts at -1 and, after the loop, print the index if it changed or print not found otherwise.</div>
      </div>

function execUser(py,code){var output='',err=null;
  try{py.runPython('import sys, io\n__old_out = sys.stdout\nsys.stdout = io.StringIO()\nsys.stderr = sys.stdout');
    try{var ns=py.globals.get('dict')();py.runPython(code,{globals:ns});ns.destroy();}
    catch(e){err=cleanErr(e.message);}
    output=py.runPython('sys.stdout.getvalue()');}
  catch(e2){err=cleanErr((e2&&e2.message)||String(e2));}
  finally{try{py.runPython('sys.stdout = __old_out\nsys.stderr = __old_out');}catch(e3){}}
  return {output:output,err:err};}
