  .prog-dot{width:26px!important;height:26px!important;border-radius:50%!important;display:flex!important;align-items:center!important;justify-content:center!important;font-size:9px!important;font-weight:700!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-dot.active{background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;}
  .prog-dot.upcoming{background:#f1f5f9!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;}
  .prog-dot.done{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border:2px solid var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-label{font-size:8px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;line-height:1.2!important;white-space:nowrap!important;}
  .prog-label.active-label{color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-arrow{flex:1 0 4px!important;height:2px!important;background:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:18px!important;min-width:4px!important;max-width:16px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}

  /* MAIN */
  .lesson-main{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;padding:40px 24px 80px;}
  .lesson-objectives{background:var(--bi3-bg);border-left:4px solid var(--bi3);border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin-bottom:28px;}
  .lesson-objectives h2{font-size:14px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;text-transform:uppercase!important;letter-spacing:.06em!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .lesson-objectives ul{list-style:none;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-objectives li{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#1e3a8a;line-height:1.5;}
  .lesson-objectives li::before{content:"\2713";color:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:1px;}
  .score-impact{background:#f0fdf4;border:1px solid #bbf7d0;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 18px;margin-bottom:28px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#14532d;}
  .score-impact strong{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}

  /* HOOK */
  .hook-box{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:32px;}
  .hook-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .hook-box p{font-size:15px!important;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:0!important;}

  /* LESSON SECTIONS */
  .lesson-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .lesson-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .lesson-section h3{font-size:17px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-top:24px!important;margin-bottom:10px!important;}
  .lesson-section p{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section ul,.lesson-section ol{padding-left:20px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section li{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .lesson-section code{background:#eef2ff;color:#1e3a8a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e3a8a!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}

  /* DUAL CODE PANEL */
  .code-panel-wrap{margin:20px 0;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;}
  .code-panel-tabs{display:flex;background:#1e293b;}
  .code-tab{padding:8px 16px;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;border:none;background:transparent;letter-spacing:.04em;transition:background .15s;font-family:inherit;}
  .code-tab.py{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.pseudo{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.active{background:rgba(255,255,255,.15)!important;}
  .code-tab-label{font-size:10px;opacity:.6;margin-left:4px;font-weight:400;}
  .code-pane{background:#0f172a;padding:18px 20px;overflow-x:auto;height:0;overflow:hidden;padding:0;}
  .code-pane.active{height:auto;overflow-x:auto;padding:18px 20px;}
  .code-pane pre{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:0;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;max-width:100%;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-kw{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .py-fn{color:#6ee7b7!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#6ee7b7!important;}
  .py-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .py-str{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .py-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .py-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-op{color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;}
  .ps-kw{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .ps-op{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .ps-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .ps-str{color:#86efac!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#86efac!important;}
  .ps-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .ps-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* CALLOUTS */
  .callout-exam{background:#fffbeb;border:1px solid #fcd34d;border-left:4px solid var(--amber);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-exam-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--amber)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--amber)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-exam p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}
  .callout-trap{background:#fef2f2;border:1px solid #fca5a5;border-left:4px solid var(--red);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-opt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;padding:10px 14px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;font-family:monospace;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;background:#f8fafc;text-align:left;width:100%;transition:border-color .15s;}
  .mini-opt:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mini-opt.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .game-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .vt-stat{text-align:center;}
  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .vt-line{display:block;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;white-space:pre;}
  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}

    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>Every decision a program makes comes down to one question with only two possible answers: True or False. Is the score high enough? Is the user logged in? Is the input empty? Before a program can choose a path, it must reduce a messy real-world question to a single Boolean value. This lesson is about building and evaluating those expressions with total confidence, one comparison and one operator at a time.</p>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What a Boolean Expression Is</h2>
      <p>A <strong>Boolean expression</strong> is any expression that evaluates to exactly one of two values: <code>True</code> or <code>False</code>. That is the entire universe of answers a Boolean can have. The simplest way to produce one is a <strong>relational operator</strong>, which compares two values and reports whether the comparison holds. The comparison itself is not a question the computer leaves open; it collapses immediately to a single Boolean value.</p>
      <p>This idea that a comparison <em>is a value</em> trips up many students. When you write <code>x > 5</code>, Python does not store the words "x greater than 5." It computes a result, <code>True</code> or <code>False</code>, and that result can be printed, stored, or combined just like a number. The AP reference sheet lists six relational operators, shown here next to their Python spellings.</p>

With x holding 7: <code>x > 5</code> is <code>True</code>, <code>x <= 7</code> is <code>True</code> (7 is equal, which counts), <code>x == 5</code> is <code>False</code>, and <code>x != 5</code> is <code>True</code>. Notice that Python prints these with a capital letter: <code>True</code> and <code>False</code>, never lowercase.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ == is not =</div>
        <p>In Python a single <code>=</code> means "assign this value," while a double <code>==</code> means "compare for equality." Writing <code>x = 5</code> where you meant <code>x == 5</code> does not compare anything, and inside <code>print(x = 5)</code> it is a hard error. In AP pseudocode a single <code>=</code> is the comparison, so the exam deliberately tests whether you can switch between the two notations.</p>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>The Three Logical Operators: NOT, AND, OR</h2>
      <p>Relational operators give you one Boolean at a time. <strong>Logical operators</strong> let you combine or flip Booleans to build richer tests. There are exactly three, and each has a simple rule you can memorize.</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>NOT</strong> (<code>not</code>) reverses a Boolean: <code>not True</code> is <code>False</code>, and <code>not False</code> is <code>True</code>.</li>
        <li>
<strong>AND</strong> (<code>and</code>) is <code>True</code> only when <strong>both</strong> sides are <code>True</code>. If either side is <code>False</code>, the whole thing is <code>False</code>.</li>
        <li>
<strong>OR</strong> (<code>or</code>) is <code>True</code> when <strong>at least one</strong> side is <code>True</code>. It is <code>False</code> only when both sides are <code>False</code>.</li>
      </ul>

<span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">False</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-kw">not</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">and</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">or</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>

<span class="ps-var">b</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">FALSE</span>

<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">OR</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">b</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>With a as <code>True</code> and b as <code>False</code>: <code>not a</code> is <code>False</code>, <code>a and b</code> is <code>False</code> (b breaks the "both" requirement), and <code>a or b</code> is <code>True</code> (a alone satisfies "at least one"). The single most useful intuition to carry into the exam: <strong>OR is far easier to satisfy than AND.</strong> AND demands everything; OR is happy with anything.</p>

        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>The CED (AAP-2.F) expects you to evaluate expressions using NOT, AND, and OR and to know their truth tables cold. A favorite trap swaps AND for OR: an expression that looks like it demands two things but really only needs one, or the reverse. Always ask: does this test require both, or just one?</p>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Evaluating Compound Expressions Step by Step</h2>
      <p>When an expression mixes operators, order matters. Evaluate in this fixed order, exactly like arithmetic precedence:</p>
      <ol>
        <li>Resolve every <strong>relational</strong> comparison into a Boolean first.</li>
        <li>Apply <strong>NOT</strong> next (it binds tightest of the three logical operators).</li>
        <li>Apply <strong>AND</strong>.</li>
        <li>Apply <strong>OR</strong> last (it binds loosest).</li>
      </ol>
      <p>Take <code>True or False and False</code>. AND goes before OR, so first <code>False and False</code> becomes <code>False</code>, leaving <code>True or False</code>, which is <code>True</code>. If you had wrongly worked left to right you would have gotten <code>False</code>. Parentheses override this order, and using them generously is a smart habit.</p>

<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">x</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">></span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">5</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">OR</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">y</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">></span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">5</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>

For the second line, <code>True or False</code> is <code>True</code>. Same two comparisons, different combiner, opposite result. That contrast is the heart of AND versus OR.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">

Students sometimes imagine NOT reaching across an AND or OR; it does not. It flips only the single Boolean immediately to its right unless parentheses say otherwise.</p>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>De Morgan: Flipping AND and OR</h2>
      <p>One equivalence appears again and again on the exam. When you push a NOT inside a parenthesized AND or OR, the operator flips and each piece gets its own NOT. This is <strong>De Morgan's law</strong>:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<code>not (a and b)</code> is the same as <code>(not a) or (not b)</code>
</li>
        <li>
<code>not (a or b)</code> is the same as <code>(not a) and (not b)</code>
</li>
      </ul>
      <p>The intuition: "it is not the case that both are true" means "at least one is false," which is an OR of the negations. Distributing the NOT turns AND into OR and OR into AND. Test it against every combination and the two sides always agree.</p>

<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-kw">NOT</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">OR</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-kw">NOT</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">b</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>With a as <code>True</code> and b as <code>False</code>: the left side <code>not (a and b)</code> is <code>not (False)</code>, which is <code>True</code>. The right side <code>(not a) or (not b)</code> is <code>False or True</code>, which is <code>True</code>. They match, and they would match for all four combinations of a and b. Recognizing this pair lets you rewrite an awkward condition into a cleaner one.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="cpt-connection">
      <div class="cpt-connection-label">📋 Create Performance Task • Boolean expressions drive your logic</div>
      <p>Every meaningful decision your Create Task program makes rests on a Boolean expression. The rubric wants selection and iteration that respond to input, and the condition inside them is always a Boolean. Writing that condition precisely, and being able to explain it, is exactly what earns the point.</p>
      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>Suppose your program decides whether a player has cleared a level. The rule is: they clear it when their score is at least 100 and they did not run out of lives. That single rule is one Boolean expression:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">cleared <- (score >= 100) AND (NOT out_of_lives)</div>
      <p>In your written response, name the expression and explain what makes it True or False:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"The Boolean expression <code>score >= 100 AND NOT out_of_lives</code> evaluates to True only when both parts hold."</li>
        <li>"Because it uses AND, a player who scores 100 but has run out of lives still evaluates to False."</li>
        <li>"The comparison <code>score >= 100</code> and the negation <code>NOT out_of_lives</code> each produce a Boolean, and AND combines them into the single decision value."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The trap to avoid</h3>
      <p>Do not swap AND for OR. With OR, a player who scored zero would still clear the level as long as they had lives left, which is not your rule. Say out loud whether your rule needs both parts or just one, then pick the matching operator. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is a Boolean expression?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A Boolean expression is any expression that evaluates to exactly one of two values, True or False. A comparison such as <code>x > 5</code> is a Boolean expression because the computer resolves it immediately to True or False.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between = and == in Python?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A single <code>=</code> assigns a value to a variable, while a double <code>==</code> compares two values for equality and produces a Boolean. In AP pseudocode a single <code>=</code> is the comparison, so you switch notations between the two.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">When is AND true versus when is OR true?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">
<code>and</code> is True only when both sides are True. <code>or</code> is True when at least one side is True, and False only when both sides are False. OR is much easier to satisfy than AND.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">In what order are NOT, AND, and OR evaluated?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Comparisons resolve first, then NOT, then AND, then OR. So <code>True or False and False</code> evaluates the AND first (giving False) and then the OR, resulting in True. Parentheses override this order.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is De Morgan's law?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">De Morgan's law says <code>not (a and b)</code> equals <code>(not a) or (not b)</code>, and <code>not (a or b)</code> equals <code>(not a) and (not b)</code>. Pushing a NOT inside parentheses flips AND to OR and negates each part.</div>
      </div>

function cleanErr(msg){if(!msg)return 'error';var lines=String(msg).trim().split('\n');return lines.slice(-3).join('\n');}
function execUser(py,code){var output='',err=null;
  try{py.runPython('import sys, io\n__old_out = sys.stdout\nsys.stdout = io.StringIO()\nsys.stderr = sys.stdout');
    try{var ns=py.globals.get('dict')();py.runPython(code,{globals:ns});ns.destroy();}
    catch(e){err=cleanErr(e.message);}
    output=py.runPython('sys.stdout.getvalue()');}
  catch(e2){err=cleanErr((e2&&e2.message)||String(e2));}
  finally{try{py.runPython('sys.stdout = __old_out\nsys.stderr = __old_out');}catch(e3){}}
  return {output:output,err:err};}

    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span><strong>Exam weight:</strong> Calling procedures appears throughout Big Idea 3 tracing and spot-the-bug items, and calling a student-developed procedure is directly rewarded on the Create Task. Swapped arguments and discarded return values are favorite traps.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>You use procedures you did not write every day. When you call a photo filter, you hand it an image and a strength, and it hands back an edited picture. You do not need to know how it works inside, only what to pass in and what comes back. That is calling a procedure: give it the right values in the right order, and use what it returns. This lesson is about getting both of those right.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What Calling a Procedure Does</h2>
      <p>A <strong>procedure</strong> (also called a function or a method) is a named group of programming instructions. Writing the procedure is one job; <strong>calling</strong> it is another. When you call a procedure, the program pauses where it is, jumps to the procedure, runs the statements inside it, and then <strong>returns control</strong> to the exact spot where the call happened. Execution continues from there. This topic is about <em>using</em> procedures that already exist. Writing your own is the next topic.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-1')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-1')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-1-py"><pre><span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">greet</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">name</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-str">"Hi "</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">name</span><span class="py-var">)</span>

<span class="py-var">greet</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-str">"Sam"</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-str">"done"</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-1-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-kw">PROCEDURE</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">greet</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">name</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"Hi "</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">name</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-var">greet</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"Sam"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"done"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Reading top to bottom: the <code>def</code> block only defines <code>greet</code>; nothing runs yet. The first line that actually executes is <code>greet("Sam")</code>, which jumps into the procedure, displays <code>Hi Sam</code>, and then hands control back so that <code>print("done")</code> runs next. Two lines are displayed, in order, because control always returns to the caller.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>The CED (AAP-3.A) says a procedure is "a named group of programming instructions." On the exam, Python uses <code>def</code> and AP pseudocode uses <code>PROCEDURE name(parameters)</code>. Both mean the same thing. A call runs the instructions and then resumes after the call.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">✍ Mini Exercise 1 • Predict the output</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">The procedure returns a value that is then printed. What does this display?</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-code"><pre style="margin:0;white-space:pre;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0;"><span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">f</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">return</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">-</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">f</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">10</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">4</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>

          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me1','A','A','me1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> 6</button>

    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Arguments and Parameters: Matched by Order</h2>
      <p>When you call a procedure you may pass it values. Those values are the <strong>arguments</strong>. The names inside the procedure that receive them are the <strong>parameters</strong>. The connection between them is <strong>position</strong>: the first argument is copied into the first parameter, the second argument into the second parameter, and so on. The names do not have to match; only the order matters.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-2')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-2')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-2-py"><pre><span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">power</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">base</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">exp</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">return</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">base</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">exp</span>

<span class="py-var">x</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">power</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">3</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">x</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-2-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-kw">PROCEDURE</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">power</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">base</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">exp</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">RETURN</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">base</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">^</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">exp</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-var">x</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">power</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">3</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">x</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>In <code>power(2, 3)</code> the argument <code>2</code> lands in the parameter <code>base</code> and <code>3</code> lands in <code>exp</code>, so the procedure returns <code>2 ** 3</code>, which is 8. If you called <code>power(3, 2)</code> instead, you would get <code>3 ** 2</code>, which is 9. Same procedure, different argument order, different result. This is a favorite exam trap.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Swapped arguments</div>
        <p>Passing the right values in the wrong order is a silent bug: the code still runs, it just computes the wrong thing. Below, the procedure is fine but the call reverses the two arguments, so a subtraction meant to be 10 minus 3 becomes 3 minus 10.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-3')">🐛 Python (buggy call)</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-3')">📋 Pseudocode (fixed call)</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-3-py"><pre><span class="py-comment"># wanted 10 - 3, but the call is swapped</span>
<span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">minus</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">return</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">-</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span>

<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">minus</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">3</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">10</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment"># prints -7, wrong</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-3-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-kw">PROCEDURE</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">minus</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">b</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">RETURN</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">b</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">minus</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">10</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">3</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>The procedure never changed. Only the call did. When you trace a call, always line up each argument with the parameter in the <strong>same position</strong> before you compute anything.</p>

      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">✍ Mini Exercise 2 • Spot the flaw</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">The procedure computes <code>a - b</code>. Why does this display <code>-6</code>?</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-code"><pre style="margin:0;white-space:pre;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0;"><span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">diff</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">return</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">-</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">diff</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">4</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">10</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="me2-opts">

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Return a Value or Perform an Action</h2>
      <p>Procedures come in two flavors. Some <strong>return a value</strong> that the caller can store or use in a larger expression. Others just <strong>perform an action</strong>, such as displaying text, and hand back no useful value. Knowing which kind you are calling tells you whether you need to capture the result.</p>
      <p>The critical habit: if a procedure returns a value, you must <strong>use</strong> that value by storing it in a variable or placing the call inside another expression such as <code>print(...)</code>. A call like <code>double(5)</code> on a line by itself computes 10 and then throws it away, because nothing catches the return value. Nothing is displayed. Compare the two calls below.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-4')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-4')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-4-py"><pre><span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">double</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">return</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">2</span>

<span class="py-var">double</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">5</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment"># return value discarded</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">double</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">5</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment"># return value used, prints 10</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-4-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-kw">PROCEDURE</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">double</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">RETURN</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">*</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-var">double</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">5</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">double</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">5</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>The first call, <code>double(5)</code>, runs and returns 10, but the 10 is discarded because it is not stored or printed. The second call, <code>print(double(5))</code>, uses the return value, so 10 appears. A returned value is only useful if the caller does something with it.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 Return vs display</div>
        <p>Do not confuse <code>return</code> with <code>print</code>. <code>return</code> hands a value back to the caller; it does not put anything on the screen by itself. <code>print</code> (or <code>DISPLAY</code>) shows text but hands back no useful value. A procedure that only prints cannot have its result stored and reused.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Tracing Programs That Call Procedures</h2>
      <p>Calls can happen many times, and each one runs the whole procedure again from the top. Use one disciplined routine and these traces become mechanical:</p>
      <ol>
        <li>Find the call. Match each argument to the parameter in the <strong>same position</strong>.</li>
        <li>Run the procedure's statements with those values. Note whether it returns a value or just acts.</li>
        <li>When it finishes, send any returned value back to the call, then continue right after the call.</li>
        <li>If a call is inside a loop, the procedure runs <strong>once per iteration</strong>, so count the iterations.</li>
        <li>Only a used return value affects the output. A discarded one changes nothing you can see.</li>
      </ol>
      <p>For example, if <code>add(a, b)</code> returns <code>a + b</code> and you write a loop that calls <code>t = add(t, k)</code> for <code>k</code> in <code>range(3)</code> starting from <code>t = 0</code>, the procedure runs three times: <code>t</code> becomes 0, then 1, then 3. The final <code>print(t)</code> displays 3. Each call returned a value that the caller stored back into <code>t</code>, so the results accumulated.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="cpt-connection">
      <div class="cpt-connection-label">📋 Create Performance Task • Calling a procedure and using its result</div>
      <p>Procedural abstraction is central to the Create Task. Once you have defined a procedure, <strong>calling</strong> it and using its return value is how your program stays organized and handles varied input. The rubric rewards a program that calls a student-developed procedure and does something meaningful with what it returns.</p>
      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>Imagine your program prices an order by calling a procedure that returns a total:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">PROCEDURE calcTotal(price, qty)
{
    RETURN(price * qty)
}
subtotal <- calcTotal(4, 3)
DISPLAY(subtotal)</div>
      <p>In your written response, name the call, explain the arguments, and describe how the returned value is used:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"The program calls <code>calcTotal</code> with the arguments <code>4</code> and <code>3</code>, which are received by the parameters <code>price</code> and <code>qty</code> in that order."</li>
        <li>"The procedure returns <code>price * qty</code>, and the program stores that returned value in <code>subtotal</code> so it can be displayed to the user."</li>
        <li>"Calling the procedure instead of repeating its steps lets the program reuse one tested calculation, which manages complexity."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The trap to avoid</h3>
      <p>Two mistakes cost the point: passing arguments in the wrong order so the parameters receive the wrong values, and calling a procedure that returns a value without storing or displaying it, so the result is discarded. Line up arguments with parameters by position, and always capture a return value you need. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What does it mean to call a procedure?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Calling a procedure runs the instructions inside it. The program jumps to the procedure, executes its statements, and then returns control to the exact place where the call was made, continuing from there.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between an argument and a parameter?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">An <strong>argument</strong> is a value you pass in when you call the procedure. A <strong>parameter</strong> is the name inside the procedure that receives that value. Arguments are matched to parameters by position: the first argument goes to the first parameter, and so on.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why does swapping the arguments change the result?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Because arguments are matched to parameters by order, not by name. If a procedure computes <code>a - b</code> and you call it with the values reversed, the wrong value lands in each parameter, so the subtraction runs in the wrong direction. The code still runs; it just computes the wrong answer.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between returning a value and displaying one?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">
<code>return</code> hands a value back to the caller so it can be stored or used in an expression, but it does not show anything on the screen. <code>print</code> (or <code>DISPLAY</code>) shows text but hands back no useful value. If a procedure returns a value, you must store or print it, or the value is discarded.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How does calling procedures help my Create Task?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Calling a procedure lets your program reuse one tested calculation instead of repeating its steps, which manages complexity. In your written response you name the call, explain how the arguments fill the parameters, and describe how the returned value is used in the program.</div>
      </div>

    if(w){ d.course=w.getAttribute('data-course'); d.unit=w.getAttribute('data-unit'); d.lesson=w.getAttribute('data-lesson'); }
    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsActivity',{detail:d}));
  }catch(e){}
}
function miniMCQ(id, chosen, correct, fbId){
  var opts=document.querySelectorAll('#'+id+'-opts .mini-opt');
  opts.forEach(function(b){b.onclick=null;b.style.cursor='default';});
  var letters=['A','B','C','D'];
  opts[letters.indexOf(chosen)].classList.add(chosen===correct?'correct':'incorrect');
  if(chosen!==correct)opts[letters.indexOf(correct)].classList.add('reveal');
  var fb=document.getElementById(fbId);
  if(MINI_MSGS[id]){fb.textContent=MINI_MSGS[id][chosen]||'';fb.className='mini-fb '+(chosen===correct?'c':'w');}
}
function miniFIB(id, fbId){
  var inp=document.getElementById(id+'-inp'),fb=document.getElementById(fbId);
  var val=inp.value.trim().toLowerCase();var d=MINI_FIB[id];
  var ok=(val===String(d.correct).toLowerCase());
  inp.classList.add(ok?'correct':'incorrect');
  fb.textContent=ok?d.c:d.w; fb.className='mini-fb '+(ok?'c':'w'); inp.disabled=true;
}
function checkMCQ(qid, chosen, correct, fbId){
  var opts=document.querySelectorAll('#'+qid+'-options .mcq-option');
  opts.forEach(function(b){b.disabled=true;b.onclick=null;});
  var letters=['A','B','C','D'];
  opts[letters.indexOf(chosen)].classList.add(chosen===correct?'correct':'incorrect');
  if(chosen!==correct)opts[letters.indexOf(correct)].classList.add('revealed-correct');
  document.getElementById(fbId).classList.add('show');
  _activity({activity:'quiz',item:qid,choice:chosen});
}
function toggleFAQ(btn){
  var item=btn.parentElement,wasOpen=item.classList.contains('open');
  document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(function(el){el.classList.remove('open');});
  if(!wasOpen)item.classList.add('open');

function handleCapture(){
  var email=document.getElementById('capture-email').value.trim();
  if(!email||!email.includes('@')){document.getElementById('capture-email').focus();return;}
  document.getElementById('capture-form').style.display='none';
  document.getElementById('capture-success').style.display='block';
  if(typeof window._learnq!=='undefined'){window._learnq.push(['identify',{'$email':email}]);}
}
var PY_URL='https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.26.2/full/';
var CE_HINT_IDX={};
/* Hint/solution usage tracking. window.LESSON_USAGE is read by the gradebook reporter
   (separate task) and mirrored in a visible on-page tally so teachers can factor it in. */
var LESSON_USAGE={hints:{},solutions:{},totalHints:0,totalSolutions:0};
window.LESSON_USAGE=LESSON_USAGE;
function _sumv(o){var t=0;for(var k in o){t+=o[k];}return t;}
function updateUsage(){
  var el=document.getElementById('code-usage');
  if(el){el.innerHTML='Hints used: <strong>'+LESSON_USAGE.totalHints+'</strong> • Solutions viewed: <strong>'+LESSON_USAGE.totalSolutions+'</strong>';}
  try{document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('lessonUsage',{detail:LESSON_USAGE}));}catch(e){}
}
function loadScriptOnce(src){return new Promise(function(res,rej){
  if(document.querySelector('script[data-pyodide]')){res();return;}
  var s=document.createElement('script');s.src=src;s.setAttribute('data-pyodide','1');
  s.onload=function(){res();};s.onerror=function(){rej(new Error('script load failed'));};
  document.head.appendChild(s);});}
function ensurePy(){if(window.__pyPromise)return window.__pyPromise;
  window.__pyPromise=(async function(){await loadScriptOnce(PY_URL+'pyodide.js');
    var py=await loadPyodide({indexURL:PY_URL});window.__pyodide=py;return py;})();
  return window.__pyPromise;}
function cleanErr(msg){if(!msg)return 'error';var lines=String(msg).trim().split('\n');return lines.slice(-3).join('\n');}
function execUser(py,code){var output='',err=null;
  try{py.runPython('import sys, io\n__old_out = sys.stdout\nsys.stdout = io.StringIO()\nsys.stderr = sys.stdout');
    try{var ns=py.globals.get('dict')();py.runPython(code,{globals:ns});ns.destroy();}
    catch(e){err=cleanErr(e.message);}
    output=py.runPython('sys.stdout.getvalue()');}
  catch(e2){err=cleanErr((e2&&e2.message)||String(e2));}
  finally{try{py.runPython('sys.stdout = __old_out\nsys.stderr = __old_out');}catch(e3){}}
  return {output:output,err:err};}
async function runPy(n){
  var out=document.getElementById('ce-out-'+n),btn=document.getElementById('run-btn-'+n);
  out.className='code-output show';out.textContent='Loading Python (first run may take a few seconds)...';
  if(btn)btn.disabled=true;var py;
  try{py=await ensurePy();}catch(e){out.className='code-output show err';
    out.textContent='Could not load the Python engine. Check your connection and try Run again.';if(btn)btn.disabled=false;return;}
  var code=document.getElementById('ce-'+n).value;var res=execUser(py,code);
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);
  if(res.err){out.className='code-output show err';out.textContent='\u2717 Error:\n'+res.err;}
  else{var got=(res.output||'').replace(/\s+$/,'');var exp=CE_EXPECTED[n];
    var shown=res.output&&res.output.length?res.output.replace(/\n$/,''):'(no output)';
    if(exp!==undefined&&got===exp){out.className='code-output show ok';out.textContent='\u2713 Correct! Output:\n'+shown;if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}
    else if(exp!==undefined){out.className='code-output show err';out.textContent='Output:\n'+shown+'\n\nTarget: '+exp+'\nKeep going, or press Hint.';}
    else{out.className='code-output show';out.textContent='Output:\n'+shown;}
    if(typeof exp!=='undefined')_activity({activity:'exercise-1',item:'ce-'+n,correct:(got===exp)});}
  if(btn)btn.disabled=false;}
function showHint(n){var box=document.getElementById('ce-hint-'+n);
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]===undefined)CE_HINT_IDX[n]=0;var hints=CE_HINTS[n]||[];
  if(hints.length===0)return;
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]>=hints.length)CE_HINT_IDX[n]=hints.length-1;
  var shown=CE_HINT_IDX[n]+1;var text='';
  for(var i=0;i<shown;i++){text+='Hint '+(i+1)+': '+hints[i]+(i<shown-1?'\n\n':'');}
  box.textContent=text;box.className='code-hint show';box.style.whiteSpace='pre-wrap';
  LESSON_USAGE.hints[n]=shown;LESSON_USAGE.totalHints=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.hints);updateUsage();
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]<hints.length-1)CE_HINT_IDX[n]++;
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}
function showSol(n){var box=document.getElementById('ce-sol-'+n);box.textContent=CE_SOL[n]||'';box.className='code-solution show';
  LESSON_USAGE.solutions[n]=1;LESSON_USAGE.totalSolutions=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.solutions);updateUsage();}
var vtScore=0,vtQ=0,vtStreak=0,vtAnswered=false;
function vtRender(){if(vtQ>=VT_QS.length){vtShowResults();return;}vtAnswered=false;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  document.getElementById('vt-qn').textContent=(vtQ+1)+'/'+VT_QS.length;
  document.getElementById('vt-streak').textContent=vtStreak;
  var codeEl=document.getElementById('vt-code');codeEl.innerHTML='';
  q.lines.forEach(function(line,i){var span=document.createElement('span');
    span.className='vt-line'+(i===q.hl?' hl':'');span.textContent=line;codeEl.appendChild(span);});
  document.getElementById('vt-question').textContent=q.q;
  var optEl=document.getElementById('vt-options');optEl.innerHTML='';
  q.choices.forEach(function(ch,i){var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='vt-btn';btn.textContent=ch;
    btn.onclick=(function(idx){return function(){vtAnswer(idx);};})(i);optEl.appendChild(btn);});
  document.getElementById('vt-fb').className='vt-fb';document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next';}
function vtAnswer(idx){if(vtAnswered)return;vtAnswered=true;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  var btns=document.querySelectorAll('.vt-btn');btns.forEach(function(b){b.onclick=null;});
  var fb=document.getElementById('vt-fb');
  if(idx===q.correct){vtScore++;vtStreak++;btns[idx].classList.add('c');fb.textContent='\u2713 Correct! '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb c';}
  else{vtStreak=0;btns[idx].classList.add('w');btns[q.correct].classList.add('rv');fb.textContent='\u2717 Not quite. '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb w';}
  document.getElementById('vt-score').textContent=vtScore;document.getElementById('vt-streak').textContent=vtStreak;
  document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next show';}
function vtNext(){vtQ++;vtRender();}
function vtShowResults(){document.getElementById('vt-active').style.display='none';

  _activity({activity:'exercise-2',earned:vtScore,possible:VT_QS.length});}
function vtRestart(){vtScore=0;vtQ=0;vtStreak=0;vtAnswered=false;
  document.getElementById('vt-results').className='vt-results';
  document.getElementById('vt-active').style.display='block';
  document.getElementById('vt-score').textContent='0';vtRender();}
vtRender();
</script>

  .ps-str{color:#86efac!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#86efac!important;}

  /* CALLOUTS */

  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}

  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}

  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}

  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}

  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */

  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}

  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}

  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}

  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}

  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}

  /* GAME */

  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Write a one-way selection (IF) and a two-way selection (IF/ELSE) in Python and AP pseudocode</span></li>
        <li><span>Build conditions using relational operators and the logical operators NOT, AND, and OR</span></li>
        <li><span>Avoid the number-one Python conditional trap: using = when you need ==</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain why two separate IF statements can behave differently from a single IF/ELSE</span></li>
        <li><span>Trace conditional code to determine exactly which branch runs and what is displayed</span></li>
        <li><span>Identify a meaningful selection statement for your Create Performance Task written response</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span><strong>Exam weight:</strong> Selection is one of the most frequently tested ideas in Big Idea 3, which is 30 to 35 percent of the exam. Conditional questions show up as tracing, spot-the-bug, and Boolean-logic items, and selection is a required feature of your Create Task program. This topic pays off twice.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>Every program that reacts to you is running conditionals. Your phone decides "low battery" below 20 percent. A game decides "game over" when lives reach zero. A login decides "welcome back" or "wrong password." Without selection, a program does the exact same thing every time no matter the input. Conditionals are how a program makes a decision, and learning to predict which decision it makes is the core skill this lesson builds.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>One-Way Selection: the IF Statement</h2>
      <p>A <strong>conditional statement</strong> (an "if statement") runs a block of code only when a <strong>condition</strong> is true. The condition is a Boolean expression, so it evaluates to either true or false. A <strong>one-way selection</strong> has a single IF and no ELSE: when the condition is true the block runs, and when it is false nothing happens and the program simply moves on.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-1')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-1')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-1-py"><pre><span class="py-var">battery</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">15</span>
<span class="py-kw">if</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">battery</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"><</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">20</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-str">"low battery"</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-str">"done"</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-1-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">battery</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">15</span>
<span class="ps-kw">IF</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">battery</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">20</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"low battery"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"done"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Here <code>battery</code> is 15, so <code>battery < 20</code> is true and the program prints <code>low battery</code> and then <code>done</code>. If <code>battery</code> were 80, the condition would be false, the indented block would be skipped, and only <code>done</code> would print. Notice that in Python the block is marked by <strong>indentation</strong>, while AP pseudocode uses <strong>curly braces</strong>. Both show exactly which statements belong to the IF.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam reference sheet gives you</div>
        <p>On the exam, one-way selection is written <code>IF(condition) { <block> }</block></code>. The block runs only if the Boolean expression is true, and no action is taken if it is false. You never memorize syntax for the exam, you read it. Your job is to determine the result.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="mini-ex">

      <h2>Two-Way Selection: IF / ELSE</h2>
      <p>A <strong>two-way selection</strong> adds an <strong>ELSE</strong>. Now the program always does exactly one of two things: the IF block when the condition is true, or the ELSE block when it is false. There is no way for both to run and no way for neither to run. Exactly one branch executes, every time.</p>

When you move from reading pseudocode to writing Python for the Create Task, this is the mistake that breaks the most programs.</p>
