      <h2>Building the Condition</h2>
      <p>The power of a conditional is in its condition. A condition is any Boolean expression, and you build it from two families of operators from the exam reference sheet.</p>

      <h3>Relational operators</h3>
      <p>Relational operators compare two values and produce a Boolean. The exam reference sheet lists six: <code>=</code>, <code>≠</code>, <code>></code>, <code><</code>, <code>≥</code>, and <code>≤</code>. In Python these become <code>==</code>, <code>!=</code>, <code>></code>, <code><</code>, <code>>=</code>, and <code><=</code>. The two you must watch are the boundary pairs: <code>></code> versus <code>≥</code> and <code><</code> versus <code>≤</code>. A single wrong boundary is the most common conditional bug on the exam, and it fails for exactly one input value.</p>

      <h3>Logical operators: NOT, AND, OR</h3>
      <p>Logical operators combine or flip Boolean values. <code>NOT</code> reverses a condition. <code>AND</code> is true only when <em>both</em> sides are true. <code>OR</code> is true when <em>at least one</em> side is true. Mixing up AND and OR is the second most common conditional error, because an OR is far easier to satisfy than an AND.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-3')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-3')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-3-py"><pre><span class="py-var">age</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">70</span>
<span class="py-comment"># kids under 13 OR seniors 65+</span>
<span class="py-kw">if</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">age</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"><</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">13</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">or</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">age</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">></span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">65</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-str">"half price"</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">else</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-str">"full price"</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-3-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">age</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">70</span>

<span class="ps-kw">IF</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">age</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">13</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">OR</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">age</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">></span><span class="ps-var">=</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">65</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"half price"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">ELSE</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"full price"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <h3>MOD for divisibility (even, odd, multiples)</h3>
      <p>A condition often needs to know if a number divides evenly. The <code>MOD</code> operator (written <code>%</code> in Python) gives the remainder after division. <code>n MOD 2</code> is 0 when <code>n</code> is even and 1 when <code>n</code> is odd, so <code>n MOD 2 = 0</code> is the standard test for "even." More generally, <code>n MOD d = 0</code> means <code>n</code> is a multiple of <code>d</code>. You will use this constantly in conditions.</p>

      <h2>Two Separate IFs Are Not the Same as IF / ELSE</h2>
      <p>This distinction is a favorite exam trap. With <strong>IF/ELSE</strong>, the two blocks are mutually exclusive, so exactly one runs. With <strong>two separate IF statements</strong>, each condition is checked on its own, so zero, one, or both blocks can run. The difference becomes visible whenever the first block changes a variable that the second condition then tests.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-4')">🐛 Two separate IFs</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-4')">📋 IF / ELSE</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-4-py"><pre><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">6</span>
<span class="py-kw">if</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">></span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">5</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">-</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">4</span>
<span class="py-kw">if</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">></span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">5</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">10</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment"># 2</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-4-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">6</span>
<span class="ps-kw">IF</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">></span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">5</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">4</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">ELSE</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">10</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-comment">// 2</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>In the two-IF version on the left, <code>n</code> starts at 6, the first IF is true so <code>n</code> becomes 2, and then the second IF checks the <em>new</em> value: 2 is not greater than 5, so it is skipped and the result is 2. In this specific case the IF/ELSE version also gives 2, because only the first condition was ever true. But change the starting value and they diverge: for a value where the first block pushes <code>n</code> back above 5, the two-IF version runs the second block too, while IF/ELSE never would. The lesson: with separate IFs, always re-check each condition using the most current value.</p>

        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 Exam habit</div>
        <p>When you see two IF statements in a row, do not assume they are exclusive. Trace them one at a time and update your variable table after each block. The moment the first block changes a variable, the second condition may flip.</p>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How to Trace a Conditional</h2>
      <p>Tracing selection is a repeatable procedure. Do it the same way every time and these questions stop being guesswork:</p>
      <ol>
        <li>Write down the current value of every variable the condition uses.</li>
        <li>Substitute those values into the Boolean expression and evaluate it to true or false. Evaluate <code>NOT</code> first, then <code>AND</code>, then <code>OR</code>.</li>
        <li>If the condition is true, run the IF block. If it is false, run the ELSE block, or skip entirely when there is no ELSE.</li>
        <li>Update your variable table with any changes the block made.</li>
        <li>Continue to the next statement. If it is another IF, start over at step 1 with the updated values.</li>
      </ol>

      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Four bugs the exam hides in conditionals</div>
        <p>Watch for these on every tracing item: a wrong boundary (<code>></code> where <code>≥</code> was needed), the wrong logical operator (<code>OR</code> where <code>AND</code> was meant), swapped branch bodies (the IF and ELSE actions traded places), and a single <code>=</code> used where equality <code>==</code> was intended in Python. Each one fails in a narrow, predictable way, which is exactly why the exam uses them.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="cpt-connection-label">📋 Create Performance Task • How selection earns points</div>
      <p>Selection is not optional on the Create Task. Your program must use at least one conditional, and your written response has to point to it and explain it. Graders are looking for a specific, accurate description, not a vague mention. Conditionals are also the natural place to show your program "manages complexity" and "handles varied input," which are the exact phrases the rubric rewards.</p>
      <h3>What a point-earning answer looks like</h3>
      <p>Suppose your Create Task is a workout tracker and this is your selection:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">minutes = 45
IF (minutes >= 30)
{
    DISPLAY("goal met")
}
ELSE
{
    DISPLAY("keep going")
}</div>
      <p>A shallow response ("I used an if statement to check minutes") earns nothing. A response that earns the point identifies the statement, states the condition, describes <em>both</em> branches, and ties it to the program's purpose:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"The selection statement tests the condition <code>minutes >= 30</code>."</li>
        <li>"When the condition is true, the program displays <code>goal met</code>; when it is false, it displays <code>keep going</code>."</li>
        <li>"This selection lets the program respond differently to different input values, which is how it gives the user meaningful feedback instead of the same message every time."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The reachability rule that quietly costs points</h3>
      <p>Both branches must be <strong>meaningful and reachable</strong>. If one branch can never run for any valid input, your conditional does not really demonstrate selection. For example, <code>IF (age >= 0)</code> around your whole program is technically a conditional, but since age is never negative the ELSE never runs, so it earns nothing. Choose a condition that genuinely can go both ways for the inputs your program accepts. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between one-way and two-way selection?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A one-way selection is a single IF with no ELSE. The block runs only when the condition is true, and nothing happens when it is false. A two-way selection is IF/ELSE, where exactly one of the two blocks always runs: the IF block when the condition is true, the ELSE block when it is false.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why does Python use == instead of = in a condition?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">In Python a single <code>=</code> means assignment (store a value into a variable) and a double <code>==</code> means "are these equal?" A condition needs a true or false result, so it must use <code>==</code>. Writing <code>if x = 5:</code> is a syntax error and the program will not run. AP pseudocode uses a single <code>=</code> for equality, so switching to <code>==</code> is a habit you build when you start writing real Python.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How is IF/ELSE different from two separate IF statements?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">With IF/ELSE the two blocks are mutually exclusive, so exactly one runs. With two separate IF statements, each condition is checked independently, so zero, one, or both blocks can run. This matters most when the first block changes a variable that the second condition tests, because the second IF then sees the updated value and may behave in a way IF/ELSE never could.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">When should I use > versus >= in a condition?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Use <code>>=</code> when the boundary value itself should count, and <code>></code> when it should not. "At least 60" or "60 and up" includes 60, so use <code>>= 60</code>. "More than 60" excludes 60, so use <code>> 60</code>. Boundary errors fail for exactly one input value, which is why the exam loves to test them. Always ask yourself what should happen at the exact boundary.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How does this topic help my Create Performance Task?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Your Create Task program must use selection, and your written response has to identify the conditional, state its condition, describe both branches, and explain how it contributes to the program's purpose. Both branches must be meaningful and reachable for the selection to demonstrate the skill. Practicing conditionals here is directly practicing a scored part of the task.</div>

function execUser(py,code){var output='',err=null;
  try{py.runPython('import sys, io\n__old_out = sys.stdout\nsys.stdout = io.StringIO()\nsys.stderr = sys.stdout');
    try{var ns=py.globals.get('dict')();py.runPython(code,{globals:ns});ns.destroy();}

    output=py.runPython('sys.stdout.getvalue()');}
  catch(e2){err=cleanErr((e2&&e2.message)||String(e2));}
  finally{try{py.runPython('sys.stdout = __old_out\nsys.stderr = __old_out');}catch(e3){}}
  return {output:output,err:err};}

  for(var i=0;i<shown;i++){text+='Hint '+(i+1)+': '+hints[i]+(i<shown-1?'\n\n':'');}
  box.textContent=text;box.className='code-hint show';box.style.whiteSpace='pre-wrap';
  LESSON_USAGE.hints[n]=shown;LESSON_USAGE.totalHints=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.hints);updateUsage();
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]<hints.length-1)CE_HINT_IDX[n]++;
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}
function showSol(n){var box=document.getElementById('ce-sol-'+n);box.textContent=CE_SOL[n]||'';box.className='code-solution show';
  LESSON_USAGE.solutions[n]=1;LESSON_USAGE.totalSolutions=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.solutions);updateUsage();}
var vtScore=0,vtQ=0,vtStreak=0,vtAnswered=false;
function vtRender(){if(vtQ>=VT_QS.length){vtShowResults();return;}vtAnswered=false;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  document.getElementById('vt-qn').textContent=(vtQ+1)+'/'+VT_QS.length;
  document.getElementById('vt-streak').textContent=vtStreak;
  var codeEl=document.getElementById('vt-code');codeEl.innerHTML='';
  q.lines.forEach(function(line,i){var span=document.createElement('span');
    span.className='vt-line'+(i===q.hl?' hl':'');span.textContent=line;codeEl.appendChild(span);});
  document.getElementById('vt-question').textContent=q.q;
  var optEl=document.getElementById('vt-options');optEl.innerHTML='';
  q.choices.forEach(function(ch,i){var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='vt-btn';btn.textContent=ch;
    btn.onclick=(function(idx){return function(){vtAnswer(idx);};})(i);optEl.appendChild(btn);});
  document.getElementById('vt-fb').className='vt-fb';document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next';}
function vtAnswer(idx){if(vtAnswered)return;vtAnswered=true;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  var btns=document.querySelectorAll('.vt-btn');btns.forEach(function(b){b.onclick=null;});
  var fb=document.getElementById('vt-fb');
  if(idx===q.correct){vtScore++;vtStreak++;btns[idx].classList.add('c');fb.textContent='\u2713 Correct! '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb c';}
  else{vtStreak=0;btns[idx].classList.add('w');btns[q.correct].classList.add('rv');fb.textContent='\u2717 Not quite. '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb w';}
  document.getElementById('vt-score').textContent=vtScore;document.getElementById('vt-streak').textContent=vtStreak;
  document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next show';}
function vtNext(){vtQ++;vtRender();}
function vtShowResults(){document.getElementById('vt-active').style.display='none';
  document.getElementById('vt-results').className='vt-results show';
  document.getElementById('vt-res-score').textContent=vtScore+'/'+VT_QS.length;
  document.getElementById('vt-res-msg').textContent=VT_MSGS[Math.min(vtScore,VT_MSGS.length-1)];
  _activity({activity:'exercise-2',earned:vtScore,possible:VT_QS.length});}
function vtRestart(){vtScore=0;vtQ=0;vtStreak=0;vtAnswered=false;
  document.getElementById('vt-results').className='vt-results';
  document.getElementById('vt-active').style.display='block';
  document.getElementById('vt-score').textContent='0';vtRender();}
vtRender();
</script>

  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .game-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .vt-stat{text-align:center;}
  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .vt-line{display:block;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;white-space:pre;}
  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .vt-question{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-options{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-btn{padding:12px;border-radius:9px;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);cursor:pointer;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;font-family:monospace;transition:all .15s;}
  .vt-btn:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:rgba(26,86,219,.2);}
  .vt-btn.c{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.15);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;}
  .vt-btn.w{border-color:#f87171;background:rgba(248,113,113,.15);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .vt-btn.rv{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.08);}
  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}
  .vt-fb.w{background:rgba(248,113,113,.1);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;display:block;}
  .vt-next{display:none;width:100%;padding:12px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .vt-next.show{display:block;}
  .vt-results{display:none;text-align:center;padding:20px;}
  .vt-results.show{display:block;}
  .vt-res-score{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:52px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-res-lbl{font-size:14px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .vt-res-msg{font-size:14px;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;margin-bottom:20px;line-height:1.6;}
  .vt-restart{background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;padding:11px 24px;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

  /* CODE EDITOR (Pyodide live) */
  .code-editor-section{background:#0f172a;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .code-editor-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .code-editor-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:22px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .code-editor-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .code-problem{background:rgba(255,255,255,.04);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08);border-radius:10px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .scaffold-badge{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:3px 10px;border-radius:100px;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .code-problem-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .code-problem-prompt{font-size:14px!important;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}

  .code-textarea{width:100%;min-height:120px;background:#020617;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0!important;resize:vertical;outline:none;line-height:1.8;}

  .code-btn-row{display:flex;gap:8px;margin-top:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;}
  .code-run-btn{padding:9px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:7px!important;font-size:13px!important;font-weight:700!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .code-run-btn:disabled{opacity:.6;cursor:wait;}
  .code-hint-btn,.code-sol-btn{padding:9px 16px!important;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06)!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.12)!important;border-radius:7px!important;font-size:13px!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .code-output{margin-top:10px;background:#020617;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;min-height:44px;display:none;line-height:1.7;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  .code-output.ok{color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;}
  .code-output.err{color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .code-hint{margin-top:8px;background:rgba(147,197,253,.06);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.2);border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;display:none;line-height:1.6;}
  .code-hint.show{display:block;}
  .code-solution{margin-top:8px;background:rgba(74,222,128,.06);border:1px solid rgba(74,222,128,.2);border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#bbf7d0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bbf7d0!important;display:none;white-space:pre;line-height:1.8;overflow-x:auto;}
  .code-solution.show{display:block;}

  /* FAQ */
  .faq-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .faq-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .faq-item{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:10px;margin-bottom:10px;overflow:hidden;}
  .faq-q{width:100%;text-align:left;padding:16px 20px;background:none;border:none;cursor:pointer;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;font-family:inherit!important;line-height:1.4!important;}
  .faq-q:hover{background:#f8fafc;}
  .faq-icon{font-size:18px;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0;transition:transform .2s;font-style:normal;}

  .faq-a{display:none;padding:0 20px 16px;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.7!important;border-top:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .faq-item.open .faq-a{display:block;}
  .faq-a code{background:#eef2ff;color:#1e3a8a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e3a8a!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}

  /* RELATED + SUPERPACK + TEACHER + NAV */
  .related-links{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:12px;padding:24px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .related-links h3{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;}
  .related-links-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(200px,1fr));gap:8px;}

  .related-ext{color:var(--slate)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--slate)!important;border-color:#e2e8f0;}
  .superpack-slim{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:10px;padding:16px 20px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:16px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:36px;}
  .superpack-slim-icon{width:36px;height:36px;border-radius:8px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:16px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .superpack-slim-text{font-size:14px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;font-weight:600;line-height:1.3;}
  .superpack-slim-sub{font-size:12px;color:var(--slate);font-weight:400;display:block;margin-top:2px;}
  .superpack-slim-btn{display:inline-flex!important;align-items:center!important;gap:6px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;padding:9px 18px!important;border-radius:7px!important;font-size:13px!important;font-weight:600!important;text-decoration:none!important;white-space:nowrap!important;}
  .superpack-slim-btn:link,.superpack-slim-btn:visited{color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;}

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Explain that data abstraction gives data a name and hides detail to manage complexity</span></li>
        <li><span>Describe how a list represents multiple related values with a single variable name</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain why one list is better than many separate variables like score1, score2, score3</span></li>
        <li><span>Access a list element by its index and know the list name refers to the whole collection</span></li>
        <li><span>Distinguish Python 0-indexing from AP pseudocode 1-indexing to avoid off-by-one errors</span></li>
        <li><span>Use a named value or constant as an abstraction in your Create Performance Task</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span><strong>Exam weight:</strong> Data abstraction is foundational for all of Big Idea 3. Index questions, especially the Python 0-indexed versus AP pseudocode 1-indexed difference, appear on tracing and spot-the-bug items, and a list that manages complexity earns a point on the Create Performance Task.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>Imagine tracking the scores of thirty students with thirty separate variables: score1, score2, all the way to score30. It would be a nightmare to write and impossible to change. Now imagine one name, scores, that holds all thirty at once. That single move, giving a collection of data one name and hiding the rest of the detail, is data abstraction. This lesson is about naming data with lists and reaching individual values by index without slipping on the off-by-one trap.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What Data Abstraction Means</h2>
      <p><strong>Data abstraction</strong> is the practice of giving data a name and hiding its underlying detail so the programmer can manage complexity (AAP-1.D). Instead of tracking many loose pieces of information, you bundle related data under one meaningful name and then work with that name. The details are still there, but you no longer have to think about all of them at once. That is the whole point of abstraction: it lets you focus on what the data represents rather than how it is stored.</p>
      <p>The most common tool for this in AP CSP is the <strong>list</strong>. A list lets multiple related items be represented with a single variable name (AAP-1.C). One name, <code>scores</code>, can stand for an entire collection of test scores. You do not need <code>score1</code>, <code>score2</code>, <code>score3</code>, and so on; you need one list.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-1')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-1')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-1-py"><pre><span class="py-comment"># many separate variables</span>
<span class="py-var">score1</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">90</span>
<span class="py-var">score2</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">85</span>
<span class="py-var">score3</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">88</span>

<span class="py-comment"># one abstraction: a single list</span>
<span class="py-var">scores</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">90</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">85</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">88</span><span class="py-var">]</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-1-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">score1</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">90</span>
<span class="ps-var">score2</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">85</span>
<span class="ps-var">score3</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">88</span>

<span class="ps-var">scores</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-num">90</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">85</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">88</span><span class="ps-var">]</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>On the left, three separate variables each hold one value and share nothing. On the right, a single list groups the same three values under one name. If you later have thirty scores instead of three, the separate-variable approach becomes unmanageable, while the list approach does not change shape at all.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>The CED says abstraction manages complexity by "hiding details." On the exam, be ready to explain <em>why</em> one list is better than many variables: it gives the collection a single name, it scales to any amount of data, and it lets the program refer to the whole collection at once.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">✍ Mini Exercise 1 • Predict the output</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">Python lists start counting at 0. What does this print?</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-code"><pre style="margin:0;white-space:pre;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0;"><span class="py-var">data</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">4</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">8</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">15</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">16</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">23</span><span class="py-var">]</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">data</span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var">]</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="me1-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me1','A','B','me1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> 8</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me1','B','B','me1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> 15</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me1','C','B','me1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> 16</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me1','D','B','me1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> nothing prints</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="me1-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Accessing Elements by Index</h2>
      <p>Once data lives in a list, you reach individual values by their <strong>index</strong>, the position number written in square brackets after the list name. The list name by itself refers to the <em>whole</em> collection; the list name plus an index refers to <em>one</em> element inside it. Understanding that difference is the core skill of this topic.</p>
      <p>Here is the trap that catches more students than any other in Big Idea 3: the two languages you must know count positions differently.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-2')">🐛 Python (0-indexed)</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-2')">📋 Pseudocode (1-indexed)</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-2-py"><pre><span class="py-var">scores</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">90</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">85</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">88</span><span class="py-var">]</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">scores</span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">0</span><span class="py-var">]</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">scores</span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var">]</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-2-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">scores</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-num">90</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">85</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">88</span><span class="ps-var">]</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">scores</span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-num">1</span><span class="ps-var">]</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">scores</span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-num">3</span><span class="ps-var">]</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>In <strong>Python</strong>, the first element is at index <code>0</code>, so <code>scores[0]</code> is 90 and <code>scores[2]</code> is 88. In <strong>AP pseudocode</strong>, the first element is at index <code>1</code>, so <code>scores[1]</code> is 90 and <code>scores[3]</code> is 88. Both panels above print the same two values, 90 then 88, but the index numbers are different by one. Read the label before you trust an index.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ The off-by-one trap</div>
        <p>Python lists are <strong>0-indexed</strong> (first element is index 0). AP pseudocode lists are <strong>1-indexed</strong> (first element is index 1). If you reach for the first element with index 1 in Python, you get the <em>second</em> element instead. If a four-item Python list is indexed at 4, that index does not exist and the program raises an out-of-range error, because the valid indexes are 0, 1, 2, and 3. On the exam, always check which language a question is written in before you count.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">✍ Mini Exercise 2 • Spot the off-by-one</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A student wanted the <strong>first</strong> element of this Python list but wrote index 1. What actually prints?</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-code"><pre style="margin:0;white-space:pre;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0;"><span class="py-var">nums</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">7</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">9</span><span class="py-var">]</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">nums</span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">1</span><span class="py-var">]</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>The List Name Is the Whole Collection</h2>
      <p>It is worth stating plainly: a list name refers to the entire collection of values, in order. When you use the name alone you are talking about all of the data at once; when you attach an index you are picking out one specific item.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-4')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-4')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-4-py"><pre><span class="py-var">names</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-str">"Ana"</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-str">"Ben"</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-str">"Cy"</span><span class="py-var">]</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">names</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">names</span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">1</span><span class="py-var">]</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-4-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">names</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-str">"Ana"</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-str">"Ben"</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-str">"Cy"</span><span class="ps-var">]</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">names</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">names</span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var">]</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>The first line prints the whole list, brackets and all, because <code>names</code> by itself is the collection. The second line prints just <code>names[1]</code>, which in Python is the second element, "Ben." This is exactly why a list is such a powerful abstraction: one name can behave as the whole group or, with an index, as any single member of it.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 Forward reference</div>
        <p>This lesson stops at naming data and reading single elements by index. Looping through every element, adding items, and removing items are the job of <strong>Topic 3.10 Lists</strong>. Here, master the abstraction and the indexing first; the traversal skills build directly on top of them.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Named Values as Abstractions</h2>
      <p>A list is not the only kind of data abstraction. Giving a plain value a meaningful name is abstraction too. A <strong>named value</strong>, often called a constant when it is meant to stay fixed, replaces a mystery number with a word that explains what the number means.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-3')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-3')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-3-py"><pre><span class="py-var">TAX_RATE</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">0.07</span>
<span class="py-var">price</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">20</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">price</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">price</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">TAX_RATE</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-3-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">TAX_RATE</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">0.07</span>
<span class="ps-var">price</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">20</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">price</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">price</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">*</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">TAX_RATE</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Reading <code>price + price * TAX_RATE</code> tells you instantly that the program adds tax to a price. If the code said <code>price + price * 0.07</code>, a reader would have to guess what 0.07 stands for. The name hides the raw detail behind an idea, and if the tax rate ever changes you update it in one place. That is data abstraction managing complexity on a small scale.</p>

      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>Suppose your program stores several quiz scores and reports one of them. Using a list gives the whole set a single name:</p>

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is data abstraction?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Data abstraction means giving data a name and hiding its underlying detail so you can manage complexity. Instead of tracking many separate values, you bundle related data under one meaningful name, such as a list called <code>scores</code>, and work with that name.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why use a list instead of separate variables?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A list represents multiple related values with a single variable name. That one name can refer to the whole collection, it scales to any amount of data without adding new variables, and you can reach any element by its index. Separate variables like <code>score1</code>, <code>score2</code>, and <code>score3</code> share nothing and become unmanageable as the data grows.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why does index 0 give the first element in Python?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Python lists are <strong>0-indexed</strong>, which means the first element is at position 0, the second at position 1, and so on. So <code>scores[0]</code> is the first element. Reaching for the first element with index 1 gives you the second element instead.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How is AP pseudocode indexing different?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">AP pseudocode lists are <strong>1-indexed</strong>: the first element is at index 1. So on the exam reference sheet, <code>list[1]</code> is the first element, while in Python <code>list[0]</code> is the first element. Always check which language a question uses before you count.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is a named value or constant?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A named value gives a meaningful name to a fixed value, like <code>TAX_RATE = 0.07</code>. It is a small data abstraction: the name explains what the number means and hides the raw detail, and if the value ever changes you update it in one place.</div>
      </div>

  finally{try{py.runPython('sys.stdout = __old_out\nsys.stderr = __old_out');}catch(e3){}}

  /* CALLOUTS */

  .callout-exam-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--amber)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--amber)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}

  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}

  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}

  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .vt-question{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-options{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-btn{padding:12px;border-radius:9px;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);cursor:pointer;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;font-family:monospace;transition:all .15s;}

  .vt-btn.w{border-color:#f87171;background:rgba(248,113,113,.15);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .vt-btn.rv{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.08);}
  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}
  .vt-fb.w{background:rgba(248,113,113,.1);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;display:block;}
  .vt-next{display:none;width:100%;padding:12px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Explain that algorithms combine sequencing, selection, and iteration</span></li>
        <li><span>Build the accumulator pattern to count items that meet a condition</span></li>
        <li><span>Sum a filtered subset of values with a conditional inside a loop</span></li>
        <li><span>Find a maximum or minimum using the best so far pattern with correct initialization</span></li>
        <li><span>Recognize when two different algorithms produce the same result</span></li>
        <li><span>Identify a meaningful loop-with-a-condition algorithm for your Create Performance Task</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span><strong>Exam weight:</strong> Developing algorithms sits at the center of Big Idea 3. Trace, spot-the-bug, and equivalent-algorithm questions about accumulator loops appear across the exam, and a loop with a condition is the surest way to earn the algorithm point on the Create Task.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>How does an app know that you have 3 unread messages, or that your highest score this week was 940? It does not store those answers. It walks through a list of items and, for each one, makes a small decision: does this count? Repeat that decision for every item and keep a running tally, and you have built an algorithm. This lesson is about combining a loop and a condition to count, total, and find the best.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Algorithms Are Built From Three Blocks</h2>
      <p>An <strong>algorithm</strong> is a finite set of instructions that accomplishes a task. The AP CSP course makes a strong claim about how every algorithm is built: no matter how complicated a program looks, it is assembled from exactly three building blocks combined and sequenced together. Those blocks are <strong>sequencing</strong> (running steps in order), <strong>selection</strong> (an if that chooses a path), and <strong>iteration</strong> (a loop that repeats). Developing an algorithm is the craft of arranging these three pieces so the program produces the right result.</p>
      <p>Up to now you have practiced each block on its own. This topic is where they combine. The single most useful combination in all of AP CSP is a <strong>conditional placed inside a loop</strong>. That pairing lets a program make a decision repeatedly, once for every item it processes, which is how programs count, filter, and search real data.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>The CED states that algorithms can be created by combining and modifying existing algorithms or using sequencing, selection, and iteration (AAP-2.M). It also states that different algorithms can be developed to solve the same problem (AAP-2.L). Expect questions that ask you to trace a loop-with-a-condition, spot a bug in one, or decide whether two different algorithms give the same output.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>The Accumulator Pattern: Count and Sum</h2>
      <p>The most common algorithm you will build combines a loop, a condition, and a running variable called an <strong>accumulator</strong>. The recipe never changes: initialize the accumulator <em>before</em> the loop, then update it <em>inside</em> the loop, but only when a condition is met. To <strong>count</strong> items that meet a rule, start a counter at 0 and add 1 each time the condition is true.</p>

The initialization <code>count = 0</code> must sit before the loop; if it were inside, it would reset on every pass and the count would be wrong.</p>

      <h2>Finding a Maximum: Best So Far</h2>
      <p>To find the largest (or smallest) value, use the <strong>best so far</strong> pattern. Keep a variable holding the best value seen up to this point. For each new value, compare it to the current best, and if the new value is better, update the best. The subtle part is the <strong>initialization</strong>, and it is a favorite exam trap.</p>

<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">best</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">v</span>

      <p>The buggy version on the left starts <code>best</code> at 0. Every value in the list is negative, so <code>v > best</code> is never true, the best is never updated, and the program wrongly prints 0, a number that is not even in the list. The safe fix, shown on the right, is to start <code>best</code> at the <strong>first element</strong> of the list. Then the best is always a real value from the data, and the comparison works for negatives, positives, and everything in between.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Initialization trap</div>
        <p>Initializing a max search to 0 quietly breaks whenever the data can be negative. Initializing a sum to anything other than 0, or a count to anything other than 0, corrupts the result too. Before you trust any accumulator, ask two questions: is it initialized to the right starting value, and is that initialization outside the loop?</p>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Different Algorithms, Same Result</h2>
      <p>A single problem can be solved by more than one algorithm (AAP-2.L). The two solutions may look nothing alike, may run different numbers of steps, and may use different variables, yet still return the identical output for every input. Recognizing when two algorithms are equivalent, and when they only look equivalent, is a tested skill.</p>
