<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">1</span>

<span class="ps-kw">FOR</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">EACH</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">IN</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">nums</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">IF</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">MOD</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">=</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Both segments compute how many values are even. Algorithm A starts at 0 and counts up when it finds an even. Algorithm B starts at the full length and counts down when it finds an odd. For the list shown, both produce 2. They are different developed algorithms for one problem. Two algorithms are truly equivalent only when they agree on <em>every</em> possible input, not just the one example in front of you, so be careful before declaring two segments the same.</p>

      <h2>A Procedure for Building and Tracing</h2>
      <p>When you develop or trace one of these algorithms, follow one disciplined routine:</p>
      <ol>
        <li>Name the accumulator and set its starting value <strong>before</strong> the loop (0 to count or sum; the first element to find a max or min).</li>
        <li>Enter the loop. For each item, evaluate the condition using the current value.</li>
        <li>Update the accumulator <strong>only</strong> when the condition is true. Leave it unchanged otherwise.</li>
        <li>After the loop finishes, and not before, use or print the accumulator.</li>
        <li>Sanity check: is the final value one that could actually come from this data?</li>
      </ol>
      <p>The order in that routine is the whole game. An update that belongs inside the loop but sits outside it will run only once. An initialization that belongs outside but sits inside will reset every pass. Most algorithm bugs on the exam are one of these two placement mistakes.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="cpt-connection">
      <div class="cpt-connection-label">📋 Create Performance Task • A loop with a condition earns the algorithm point</div>
      <p>The Create Task rubric awards a point for an algorithm that includes <strong>sequencing, selection, and iteration</strong> and that is built to accomplish the program purpose. An accumulator loop is the cleanest way to earn it: it sequences a setup step, iterates over data, and selects which items to act on. One well-chosen loop-with-a-condition can carry this entire point.</p>
      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>Suppose your program stores quiz scores and must report how many are passing:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">passing <- 0
FOR EACH s IN scores
{
    IF (s >= 60)
    {
        passing <- passing + 1
    }
}
DISPLAY(passing)</div>
      <p>In your written response, identify the algorithm and name all three blocks it uses:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"My algorithm uses <strong>iteration</strong> to examine each score, <strong>selection</strong> to test whether a score is at least 60, and <strong>sequencing</strong> to build the result before displaying it."</li>
        <li>"The accumulator <code>passing</code> starts at 0 before the loop and increases by 1 only when the condition is true, so it counts exactly the scores that meet the rule."</li>
        <li>"This algorithm accomplishes the program purpose by summarizing the data instead of handling a single value."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The trap to avoid</h3>
      <p>Keep the initialization outside the loop and the update inside it. If <code>passing <- 0</code> slips inside the FOR EACH, the count resets every pass and your algorithm no longer works, which can cost the point even though the code looks complete. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

<script>(function(){
(function(){
  var g = document.getElementById('rd-game');
  var LEVELS = [
    { size:5, start:{r:4,c:0,dir:0}, goal:{r:0,c:0}, walls:[],
      tip:'The robot already faces up. A straight climb needs only MOVE_FORWARD.' },
    { size:5, start:{r:4,c:0,dir:0}, goal:{r:0,c:4}, walls:[],
      tip:'Reaching a corner needs a turn. Move to one edge, ROTATE, then finish.' },
    { size:6, start:{r:5,c:0,dir:0}, goal:{r:0,c:5},
      walls:['3,0','3,1','3,2','3,3','3,4','1,1','1,2','1,3','1,4','1,5'],
      tip:'Walls block the direct path. Find the gaps and zig-zag through them.' },
    { size:7, start:{r:6,c:0,dir:0}, goal:{r:0,c:6},
      walls:['4,0','4,1','4,2','4,3','4,4','2,2','2,3','2,4','2,5','2,6'],
      tip:'Two wall rows, gaps on opposite sides. Plan the whole route before running.' }
  ];
  var DR=[-1,0,1,0], DC=[0,1,0,-1];               // dir: 0=N,1=E,2=S,3=W
  var ARROWS=['\u25B2','\u25B6','\u25BC','\u25C0'];

  var levelIdx=0, program=[], robot={}, angle=0, running=false, solved=false, totalStars=0;
  var cellPct=20, optimalM=0;

  var el={
    grid:document.getElementById('rd-grid'), robot:document.getElementById('rd-robot'),
    prog:document.getElementById('rd-prog'), fb:document.getElementById('rd-feedback'),
    lvl:document.getElementById('rd-lvl'), stars:document.getElementById('rd-stars'),
    len:document.getElementById('rd-len'), run:document.getElementById('rd-run'),
    undo:document.getElementById('rd-undo'), clear:document.getElementById('rd-clear'),
    next:document.getElementById('rd-next'), play:document.getElementById('rd-play'),
    win:document.getElementById('rd-winscreen')
  };

  function sleep(ms){ return new Promise(function(res){ setTimeout(res,ms); }); }

  // BFS over (r,c,dir) states -> minimum number of commands to reach goal cell
  function optimal(L){
    var N=L.size, walls={}; L.walls.forEach(function(w){ walls[w]=1; });
    var start=L.start.r+','+L.start.c+','+L.start.dir;
    var q=[[L.start.r,L.start.c,L.start.dir,0]], seen={}; seen[start]=1;
    while(q.length){
      var s=q.shift(), r=s[0], c=s[1], d=s[2], n=s[3];
      if(r===L.goal.r && c===L.goal.c) return n;
      var turns=[(d+3)%4,(d+1)%4], i, k;
      for(i=0;i<2;i++){ k=r+','+c+','+turns[i]; if(!seen[k]){ seen[k]=1; q.push([r,c,turns[i],n+1]); } }
      var nr=r+DR[d], nc=c+DC[d];
      if(nr>=0&&nr<N&&nc>=0&&nc<N&&!walls[nr+','+nc]){
        k=nr+','+nc+','+d; if(!seen[k]){ seen[k]=1; q.push([nr,nc,d,n+1]); }
      }
    }
    return -1;
  }

  function loadLevel(){
    var L=LEVELS[levelIdx];
    solved=false; program=[]; running=false;
    optimalM=optimal(L);
    cellPct=100/L.size;
    // build grid
    el.grid.style.gridTemplateColumns='repeat('+L.size+',1fr)';
    el.grid.style.gridTemplateRows='repeat('+L.size+',1fr)';
    el.grid.innerHTML='';
    var walls={}; L.walls.forEach(function(w){ walls[w]=1; });
    for(var r=0;r<L.size;r++){ for(var c=0;c<L.size;c++){
      var cell=document.createElement('div');
      cell.className='rd-cell';
      if(walls[r+','+c]) cell.className+=' wall';
      if(r===L.goal.r && c===L.goal.c){ cell.className+=' rd-goalcell';
        var f=document.createElement('span'); f.className='rd-flag'; f.innerHTML='🏁'; cell.appendChild(f); }
      el.grid.appendChild(cell);
    }}
    // robot
    robot={ r:L.start.r, c:L.start.c, dir:L.start.dir };
    angle=L.start.dir*90;
    setRobot(false);
    el.next.classList.add('rd-hidden');
    el.lvl.textContent=(levelIdx+1)+' / '+LEVELS.length;
    el.stars.textContent=totalStars;
    setFeedback('info','<b>Level '+(levelIdx+1)+'.</b> '+L.tip+' Best possible: ~'+optimalM+' commands.');
    renderProg();
    setCmdEnabled(true);
  }

  function setRobot(animate){
    if(!animate) el.robot.classList.add('nomove');
    el.robot.style.width=cellPct+'%';
    el.robot.style.height=cellPct+'%';
    el.robot.style.left=(robot.c*cellPct)+'%';
    el.robot.style.top=(robot.r*cellPct)+'%';
    el.robot.style.transform='rotate('+angle+'deg)';
    if(!animate){ el.robot.offsetHeight; el.robot.classList.remove('nomove'); }
  }

  function setFeedback(kind,html){
    el.fb.className='rd-feedback'+(kind==='good'?' good':kind==='bad'?' bad':'');
    el.fb.innerHTML=html;
  }

  var CMD={ F:{cls:'mv',ic:'\u2191',name:'MOVE'}, L:{cls:'rot',ic:'\u21BA',name:'LEFT'}, R:{cls:'rot',ic:'\u21BB',name:'RIGHT'} };
  function renderProg(active){
    el.len.textContent=program.length+(program.length===1?' command':' commands');
    if(!program.length){ el.prog.innerHTML='<span class="rd-empty">No commands yet. Click MOVE / ROTATE above to build a program.</span>'; return; }
    el.prog.innerHTML='';
    program.forEach(function(cmd,i){
      var c=CMD[cmd];
      var chip=document.createElement('span');
      chip.className='rd-chip '+c.cls+(active===i?' active':'');
      chip.innerHTML='<span class="rd-num">'+(i+1)+'</span>'+c.ic+' '+c.name+' <span class="x">×</span>';
      chip.addEventListener('click',function(){ if(running) return; program.splice(i,1); resetRun(); renderProg(); });
      el.prog.appendChild(chip);
    });
  }

  function resetRun(){
    // return robot to start position without penalty (lets player edit + rerun)
    var L=LEVELS[levelIdx];
    robot={ r:L.start.r, c:L.start.c, dir:L.start.dir };
    angle=L.start.dir*90;
    solved=false;
    el.next.classList.add('rd-hidden');
    setRobot(false);
  }

  function setCmdEnabled(on){
    document.getElementById('rd-add-F').disabled=!on;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-L').disabled=!on;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-R').disabled=!on;
    el.run.disabled=!on;
    el.undo.disabled=!on; el.clear.disabled=!on;
  }

  function addCmd(c){ if(running) return; resetRun(); program.push(c); renderProg(); }

  async function run(){
    if(running || !program.length) return;
    running=true; solved=false; setCmdEnabled(false);
    resetRun();
    await sleep(220);
    var L=LEVELS[levelIdx], walls={}; L.walls.forEach(function(w){ walls[w]=1; });
    for(var i=0;i<program.length;i++){
      renderProg(i);
      var cmd=program[i];
      if(cmd==='L'){ robot.dir=(robot.dir+3)%4; angle-=90; setRobot(true); }
      else if(cmd==='R'){ robot.dir=(robot.dir+1)%4; angle+=90; setRobot(true); }
      else {
        var nr=robot.r+DR[robot.dir], nc=robot.c+DC[robot.dir];
        if(nr<0||nr>=L.size||nc<0||nc>=L.size){
          fail(i,'The robot tried to move <b>off the grid</b> while facing '+ARROWS[robot.dir]+'. In AP CSP, MOVE_FORWARD off the edge is a failed run  -  ROTATE before you reach the wall.');
          return;
        }
        if(walls[nr+','+nc]){
          fail(i,'The robot hit a <b>blocked cell</b> (wall). MOVE_FORWARD can never enter a wall  -  plan a route around it.');
          return;
        }
        robot.r=nr; robot.c=nc; setRobot(true);
      }
      await sleep(430);
    }
    renderProg(-1);
    if(robot.r===L.goal.r && robot.c===L.goal.c){ succeed(); }
    else {
      running=false; setCmdEnabled(true);
      setFeedback('bad','The program finished but the robot stopped at row '+robot.r+', col '+robot.c+'  -  <b>not on the flag</b>. Re-trace each command and count the cells and turns.');
    }
  }

  function fail(i,msg){
    el.robot.classList.add('bad');
    setTimeout(function(){ el.robot.classList.remove('bad'); },420);
    renderProg(i);
    running=false; setCmdEnabled(true);
    setFeedback('bad','<b>Command '+(i+1)+' failed.</b> '+msg);
  }

  function succeed(){
    running=false; solved=true;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-F').disabled=true;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-L').disabled=true;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-R').disabled=true;
    el.run.disabled=true; el.undo.disabled=true; el.clear.disabled=true;
    var n=program.length, stars = n<=optimalM?3 : n<=optimalM+2?2 : 1;
    totalStars+=stars;
    el.stars.textContent=totalStars;
    var st=''; for(var s=0;s<3;s++) st += s<stars? '\u2605':'\u2606';
    var eff = n<=optimalM ? 'Perfectly efficient!' : 'You can trim this  -  the optimal uses fewer commands.';
    setFeedback('good','<b>'+st+' Solved in '+n+' commands</b> (best possible ~'+optimalM+'). '+eff);
    el.next.classList.remove('rd-hidden');
    el.next.textContent = (levelIdx+1<LEVELS.length) ? 'Next Level \u2192' : 'See Results \u2192';
  }

  function nextLevel(){
    if(levelIdx+1<LEVELS.length){ levelIdx++; loadLevel(); }
    else showWin();
  }

  function showWin(){
    el.play.classList.add('rd-hidden');
    el.win.classList.remove('rd-hidden');
    var maxStars=LEVELS.length*3;
    el.win.innerHTML=
      '<div class="rd-win">'+
      '<h2>You directed the robot home! 🎉</h2>'+
      '<p>You planned command sequences with MOVE_FORWARD, ROTATE_LEFT, and ROTATE_RIGHT, traced them cell by cell, and kept the robot on the grid  -  exactly the algorithmic thinking the AP CSP robot questions test.</p>'+
      '<div class="big">'+totalStars+' / '+maxStars+' stars \u2605</div>'+
      '<p>Fewer commands = a more efficient algorithm. Rerun to earn every star.</p>'+
      '<button class="rd-btn next" id="rd-again" style="max-width:220px;margin:8px auto 0;">Play Again</button>'+
      '</div>';

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What are the three building blocks of every algorithm?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Sequencing, selection, and iteration. Sequencing runs steps in order, selection uses a condition to choose a path, and iteration repeats steps with a loop. The CED (AAP-2.M) says algorithms are built by combining and sequencing these blocks.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the accumulator pattern?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">It is an algorithm that builds a running result across a loop. You initialize a variable before the loop, then update it inside the loop, usually only when a condition is true. Counting starts at 0 and adds 1; summing starts at 0 and adds the value; a max search starts at the first element and keeps the larger value.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why must the accumulator be initialized outside the loop?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">If the initialization sits inside the loop, it resets on every pass and the running total is destroyed, leaving only the last value. The starting value must be set once, before the loop begins, so the updates can build on each other.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why is starting a maximum search at 0 a bug?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">If the data can contain negative numbers, none of them will ever be greater than 0, so the best value stays 0, which is not even in the list. Start the best value at the first element of the list instead, so it is always a real value from the data.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Can two different algorithms solve the same problem?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Yes. AAP-2.L states that different algorithms can be developed to solve the same problem. They may use different steps or variables yet return the same output. Two algorithms are equivalent only when they agree for every possible input, not just one example.</div>
      </div>

  finally{try{py.runPython('sys.stdout = __old_out\nsys.stderr = __old_out');}catch(e3){}}

  /* CALLOUTS */

  .callout-exam-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--amber)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--amber)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}

  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}

  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}

  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .vt-question{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-options{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-btn{padding:12px;border-radius:9px;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);cursor:pointer;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;font-family:monospace;transition:all .15s;}

  .vt-btn.w{border-color:#f87171;background:rgba(248,113,113,.15);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .vt-btn.rv{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.08);}
  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}
  .vt-fb.w{background:rgba(248,113,113,.1);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;display:block;}
  .vt-next{display:none;width:100%;padding:12px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Define a procedure in Python with def and in AP pseudocode with PROCEDURE</span></li>
        <li><span>Add a parameter that generalizes a procedure so one definition works for many inputs</span></li>
        <li><span>Return a computed value with return, and know a missing return hands back None</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain that a parameter is a local placeholder, not the caller's variable</span></li>
        <li><span>Describe procedural abstraction and its benefits: reuse, readability, and hiding detail</span></li>
        <li><span>Write a Create Task procedure with a parameter, selection, and iteration</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span><strong>Exam weight:</strong> Writing procedures with parameters and return values (AAP-3.B) and explaining procedural abstraction (AAP-3.C) appear on the MCQ and are directly scored on the Create Task. The None trap and the local-parameter trap are frequent MCQ targets.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>You have called <code>print</code> hundreds of times without knowing how it works inside. That is abstraction: a name you trust, details you ignore. Now you become the author. When you write <code>def double(n): return n * 2</code>, you create a name others can call the same way, once, and reuse forever. This lesson is about building your own procedures with parameters and return values, and knowing exactly what comes back.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Writing Your Own Procedure</h2>
      <p>A <strong>procedure</strong> is a named block of code that you can call by name. Until now you have mostly called procedures other people wrote, like <code>print</code> or <code>len</code>. Now you will <strong>define</strong> your own. In Python you write <code>def name(parameters):</code> and then the indented body. The definition does not run on its own. The body only executes when the procedure is <strong>called</strong>.</p>
      <p>Two pieces make a procedure powerful. A <strong>parameter</strong> is a placeholder listed in the header that stands for a value the caller will supply. A <strong>return value</strong> is the result the procedure hands back with the <code>return</code> keyword, so the caller can store it or print it. Python uses <code>def</code> and <code>return</code>; AP pseudocode uses <code>PROCEDURE name(param)</code> and <code>RETURN(...)</code>. They express the same idea.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-1')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-1')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-1-py"><pre><span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">double</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">return</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">2</span>

<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">double</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">5</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-1-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-kw">PROCEDURE</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">double</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">RETURN</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">*</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>

<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">double</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">5</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Here <code>double</code> is defined once with a parameter <code>n</code>. The call <code>double(5)</code> sends the value 5 into <code>n</code>, the body computes <code>5 * 2</code>, and <code>return</code> hands 10 back to the caller, which then prints 10. The parameter is what lets one definition work for any number you pass.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>The CED (AAP-3.B) asks you to write a procedure with a parameter and a return value. On the AP reference sheet the shape is <code>PROCEDURE name(param){ ... RETURN(expression) }</code>. Know that <code>RETURN</code> both hands back a value and ends the procedure.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">✍ Mini Exercise 1 • Predict the output</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">The procedure has a parameter and a return. What does this print?</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-code"><pre style="margin:0;white-space:pre;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0;"><span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">double</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Return vs No Return: the None Trap</h2>
      <p>A procedure only hands back a value if you actually write <code>return</code>. If the body computes something but never returns it, the procedure finishes and hands back the special value <code>None</code>. This is one of the most common bugs in early code: you compute the right answer inside the procedure, but forget to return it, so storing or printing the call gives <code>None</code>.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-3')">🐛 Python (buggy)</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-3')">📋 Pseudocode (fixed)</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-3-py"><pre><span class="py-comment"># forgot to return</span>
<span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">area</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">s</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">s</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">s</span>

<span class="py-var">x</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">area</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">5</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">x</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-3-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-comment"># fixed: hand back the value</span>
<span class="ps-kw">PROCEDURE</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">area</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">s</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">s</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">*</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">s</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">RETURN</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>

<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">area</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">5</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>On the left, <code>area</code> computes <code>a</code> but never returns it, so <code>x</code> receives <code>None</code> and the program prints <code>None</code> instead of 25. The fix on the right adds <code>RETURN(a)</code> so the value actually leaves the procedure. Always ask: does the value I computed ever get returned?</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ None means "no return"</div>
        <p>A procedure with no <code>return</code> statement returns <code>None</code> by default. So <code>print(f(3))</code> shows <code>None</code>, and <code>y = f(3)</code> stores <code>None</code>. If your output is mysteriously <code>None</code>, the first thing to check is whether the procedure returned its result.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Parameters Are Local Placeholders</h2>
      <p>A parameter is a <strong>local</strong> name that exists only inside the procedure while it runs. When you call <code>double(5)</code>, the parameter <code>n</code> becomes 5 for that call, then disappears when the procedure ends. A parameter is <strong>not</strong> the same variable as the one in the caller, even if they happen to share a name. Reassigning a parameter inside the body does not change the caller's variable.</p>
      <p>The whole point of a parameter is to <strong>generalize</strong>. Instead of writing one block for a square of side 4 and another block for a square of side 7, you write one procedure with a parameter and call it with 4, then 7, then any value. One definition, many uses. That is exactly the repetition that procedures remove.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">

<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">return</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-str">"fail"</span>

<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">RETURN</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"pass"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>

<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">RETURN</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"fail"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>

      <p>The <code>label</code> procedure has a parameter <code>score</code> and uses <code>selection</code> to return one of two results. Calling <code>label(72)</code> returns <code>"pass"</code>; calling <code>label(40)</code> returns <code>"fail"</code>. The parameter is what makes the single procedure answer for every possible score.</p>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Procedural Abstraction and Its Benefits</h2>
      <p><strong>Procedural abstraction</strong> (AAP-3.C) means giving a name to a process and then using that name without worrying about the details inside. Once <code>double</code> exists, you write <code>double(5)</code> and think "double it," not "multiply by two." The details are hidden behind the name. This is the same idea as calling <code>print</code>: you use it constantly without knowing how it works internally.</p>
      <p>The benefits are practical, and the exam names them directly:</p>
      <ul class="rules">
        <li>it <strong>removes duplicate code</strong> by naming a process once and reusing it</li>
        <li>it makes a program <strong>easier to read</strong>, because a good name explains intent</li>
        <li>it makes a program <strong>easier to change</strong>, because you fix the logic in one place</li>
        <li>it <strong>hides the implementation detail</strong> so you can reason about what, not how</li>
      </ul>
      <p>Notice what abstraction does <strong>not</strong> do: it does not change the result the program computes. Replacing three copied blocks with one procedure produces the exact same output; it just organizes the program better. That distinction is a favorite exam trap.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 Say it the exam's way</div>
        <p>If asked why a programmer wrote a procedure, strong answers mention reuse and readability: "the procedure lets the same logic be called from several places without duplicating code, and the name makes the program easier to read and modify."</p>
      </div>

      <p>This topic is the heart of a scored Create Task requirement. You must include a <strong>student-developed procedure</strong> that has a <strong>parameter which affects its behavior</strong>, and whose body includes both <strong>selection</strong> and <strong>iteration</strong>. A built-in call like <code>print</code> does not count. You have to define it yourself.</p>
      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>A procedure that counts how many values in a list are above a cutoff, where the cutoff is the parameter that changes the result:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">PROCEDURE countAbove(values, cutoff)
{
    total <- 0
    FOR EACH v IN values
    {
        IF (v > cutoff)
        {
            total <- total + 1
        }
    }
    RETURN(total)
}</div>
      <p>This one procedure earns the point because it has a parameter, iteration, and selection all working together. In your written response, use these sentence stems:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"My procedure <code>countAbove(values, cutoff)</code> takes a parameter <code>cutoff</code>; calling it with a different cutoff produces a different count, so the parameter affects the result."</li>
        <li>"The procedure uses iteration, the <code>FOR EACH</code> loop over <code>values</code>, and selection, the <code>IF (v > cutoff)</code> test, to build up the total."</li>
        <li>"The procedure returns <code>total</code>, which the main program uses to decide what to display."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The trap to avoid</h3>
      <p>Do not describe a procedure that ignores its parameter, and do not forget the <code>return</code>. A parameter that never changes the behavior, or a procedure that computes but returns <code>None</code>, will not earn the point. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

    x = x * <span class="n">2</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> x
f(x)
<span class="k">print</span>(x)</div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q3-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','A','C','q3-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> 10</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','B','C','q3-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> None</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','C','C','q3-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> 5</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','D','C','q3-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> an error message</button>
</div>
<div id="q3-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The parameter x is a local placeholder. Doubling it inside f does not change the outer x, and the returned value was not stored.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The outer x was assigned 5 and is never reassigned from the call, so it prints 5, not None.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. f(x) returns 10 but that value is discarded because it is not assigned. The outer x is a separate variable and stays 5, so 5 prints.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Reusing the name x as a parameter is legal. The outer x simply keeps its value of 5.</div>
      </div>

        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 4 of 6<span class="diff-tag">I, II, III</span>
</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text">Which of the following correctly define a procedure that <strong>returns</strong> the square of its parameter?</div>

          <li>
<strong>I.</strong> def sq(n): return n * n</li>
          <li>
<strong>II.</strong> def sq(n): n * n</li>
          <li>
<strong>III.</strong> PROCEDURE sq(n) { RETURN(n * n) }</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q4-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','A','C','q4-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> I only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','B','C','q4-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> I and II only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','C','C','q4-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> I and III only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','D','C','q4-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> I, II, and III</button>
</div>
<div id="q4-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. I is correct, but III also returns the square using the AP pseudocode RETURN.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. II lacks a return, so it hands back None instead of the square. It is not correct.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. I and III both hand back n * n. II computes n * n but has no return, so it returns None, not the square.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. II has no return statement, so it does not return the square. Only I and III are correct.</div>

        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 5 of 6<span class="diff-tag">NOT question</span>
</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text">Which of the following is <strong>NOT</strong> a benefit of procedural abstraction?</div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q5-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','A','A','q5-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> It changes the result the program computes so the output differs</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','B','A','q5-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> It removes duplicate code by naming a process once and reusing it</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','C','A','q5-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> It makes a program easier to read and to change later</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','D','A','q5-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> It hides the details of how a step is carried out</button>
</div>
<div id="q5-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Abstraction reorganizes a program without changing what it computes. The output stays the same, so this is not a benefit it provides.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Removing duplicate code through reuse is a real benefit of abstraction.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Improved readability and easier changes are genuine benefits of abstraction.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Hiding implementation detail is exactly what abstraction provides.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q6">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 6 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Abstraction</span>
</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text">A programmer replaces three nearly identical blocks that each compute a different rectangle's area with one procedure <code>area(w, h)</code> called three times. What is the main role of the parameters <code>w</code> and <code>h</code>?</div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q6-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','A','D','q6-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> They make the procedure run faster than the original three blocks</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','B','D','q6-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> They change which area values the program ultimately computes</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','C','D','q6-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> They act as global variables shared with the rest of the program</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','D','D','q6-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> They generalize the procedure so one definition works for many rectangles</button>
</div>
<div id="q6-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Parameters generalize the code; they do not make it inherently faster. The purpose is reuse, not speed.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The computed areas are the same as before. Abstraction reorganizes the program without changing its output.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Parameters are local placeholders inside the procedure, not global variables shared with the whole program.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Parameters generalize a procedure. One definition of area(w, h) handles any rectangle, which is why the three duplicate blocks collapse into one.</div>

    var N=L.size, walls={}; L.walls.forEach(function(w){ walls[w]=1; });
    var start=L.start.r+','+L.start.c+','+L.start.dir;
    var q=[[L.start.r,L.start.c,L.start.dir,0]], seen={}; seen[start]=1;
    while(q.length){
      var s=q.shift(), r=s[0], c=s[1], d=s[2], n=s[3];
      if(r===L.goal.r && c===L.goal.c) return n;
      var turns=[(d+3)%4,(d+1)%4], i, k;
      for(i=0;i<2;i++){ k=r+','+c+','+turns[i]; if(!seen[k]){ seen[k]=1; q.push([r,c,turns[i],n+1]); } }
      var nr=r+DR[d], nc=c+DC[d];
      if(nr>=0&&nr<N&&nc>=0&&nc<N&&!walls[nr+','+nc]){
        k=nr+','+nc+','+d; if(!seen[k]){ seen[k]=1; q.push([nr,nc,d,n+1]); }
      }
    }
    return -1;
  }

  function loadLevel(){
    var L=LEVELS[levelIdx];
    solved=false; program=[]; running=false;
    optimalM=optimal(L);
    cellPct=100/L.size;
    // build grid
    el.grid.style.gridTemplateColumns='repeat('+L.size+',1fr)';
    el.grid.style.gridTemplateRows='repeat('+L.size+',1fr)';
    el.grid.innerHTML='';
    var walls={}; L.walls.forEach(function(w){ walls[w]=1; });
    for(var r=0;r<L.size;r++){ for(var c=0;c<L.size;c++){
      var cell=document.createElement('div');
      cell.className='rd-cell';
      if(walls[r+','+c]) cell.className+=' wall';
      if(r===L.goal.r && c===L.goal.c){ cell.className+=' rd-goalcell';
        var f=document.createElement('span'); f.className='rd-flag'; f.innerHTML='🏁'; cell.appendChild(f); }
      el.grid.appendChild(cell);
    }}
    // robot
    robot={ r:L.start.r, c:L.start.c, dir:L.start.dir };
    angle=L.start.dir*90;
    setRobot(false);
    el.next.classList.add('rd-hidden');
    el.lvl.textContent=(levelIdx+1)+' / '+LEVELS.length;
    el.stars.textContent=totalStars;
    setFeedback('info','<b>Level '+(levelIdx+1)+'.</b> '+L.tip+' Best possible: ~'+optimalM+' commands.');
    renderProg();
    setCmdEnabled(true);
  }

  function setRobot(animate){
    if(!animate) el.robot.classList.add('nomove');
    el.robot.style.width=cellPct+'%';
    el.robot.style.height=cellPct+'%';
    el.robot.style.left=(robot.c*cellPct)+'%';
    el.robot.style.top=(robot.r*cellPct)+'%';
    el.robot.style.transform='rotate('+angle+'deg)';
    if(!animate){ el.robot.offsetHeight; el.robot.classList.remove('nomove'); }
  }

  function setFeedback(kind,html){
    el.fb.className='rd-feedback'+(kind==='good'?' good':kind==='bad'?' bad':'');
    el.fb.innerHTML=html;
  }

  var CMD={ F:{cls:'mv',ic:'\u2191',name:'MOVE'}, L:{cls:'rot',ic:'\u21BA',name:'LEFT'}, R:{cls:'rot',ic:'\u21BB',name:'RIGHT'} };
  function renderProg(active){
    el.len.textContent=program.length+(program.length===1?' command':' commands');
    if(!program.length){ el.prog.innerHTML='<span class="rd-empty">No commands yet. Click MOVE / ROTATE above to build a program.</span>'; return; }
    el.prog.innerHTML='';
    program.forEach(function(cmd,i){
      var c=CMD[cmd];
      var chip=document.createElement('span');
      chip.className='rd-chip '+c.cls+(active===i?' active':'');
      chip.innerHTML='<span class="rd-num">'+(i+1)+'</span>'+c.ic+' '+c.name+' <span class="x">×</span>';
      chip.addEventListener('click',function(){ if(running) return; program.splice(i,1); resetRun(); renderProg(); });
      el.prog.appendChild(chip);
    });
  }

  function resetRun(){
    // return robot to start position without penalty (lets player edit + rerun)
    var L=LEVELS[levelIdx];
    robot={ r:L.start.r, c:L.start.c, dir:L.start.dir };
    angle=L.start.dir*90;
    solved=false;
    el.next.classList.add('rd-hidden');
    setRobot(false);
  }

  function setCmdEnabled(on){
    document.getElementById('rd-add-F').disabled=!on;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-L').disabled=!on;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-R').disabled=!on;
    el.run.disabled=!on;
    el.undo.disabled=!on; el.clear.disabled=!on;
  }

  function addCmd(c){ if(running) return; resetRun(); program.push(c); renderProg(); }

  async function run(){
    if(running || !program.length) return;
    running=true; solved=false; setCmdEnabled(false);
    resetRun();
    await sleep(220);
    var L=LEVELS[levelIdx], walls={}; L.walls.forEach(function(w){ walls[w]=1; });
    for(var i=0;i<program.length;i++){
      renderProg(i);
      var cmd=program[i];
      if(cmd==='L'){ robot.dir=(robot.dir+3)%4; angle-=90; setRobot(true); }
      else if(cmd==='R'){ robot.dir=(robot.dir+1)%4; angle+=90; setRobot(true); }
      else {
        var nr=robot.r+DR[robot.dir], nc=robot.c+DC[robot.dir];
        if(nr<0||nr>=L.size||nc<0||nc>=L.size){
          fail(i,'The robot tried to move <b>off the grid</b> while facing '+ARROWS[robot.dir]+'. In AP CSP, MOVE_FORWARD off the edge is a failed run  -  ROTATE before you reach the wall.');
          return;
        }
        if(walls[nr+','+nc]){
          fail(i,'The robot hit a <b>blocked cell</b> (wall). MOVE_FORWARD can never enter a wall  -  plan a route around it.');
          return;
        }
        robot.r=nr; robot.c=nc; setRobot(true);
      }
      await sleep(430);
    }
    renderProg(-1);
    if(robot.r===L.goal.r && robot.c===L.goal.c){ succeed(); }
    else {
      running=false; setCmdEnabled(true);
      setFeedback('bad','The program finished but the robot stopped at row '+robot.r+', col '+robot.c+'  -  <b>not on the flag</b>. Re-trace each command and count the cells and turns.');
    }
  }

  function fail(i,msg){
    el.robot.classList.add('bad');
    setTimeout(function(){ el.robot.classList.remove('bad'); },420);
    renderProg(i);
    running=false; setCmdEnabled(true);
    setFeedback('bad','<b>Command '+(i+1)+' failed.</b> '+msg);
  }

  function succeed(){
    running=false; solved=true;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-F').disabled=true;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-L').disabled=true;
    document.getElementById('rd-add-R').disabled=true;
    el.run.disabled=true; el.undo.disabled=true; el.clear.disabled=true;
    var n=program.length, stars = n<=optimalM?3 : n<=optimalM+2?2 : 1;
    totalStars+=stars;
    el.stars.textContent=totalStars;
    var st=''; for(var s=0;s<3;s++) st += s<stars? '\u2605':'\u2606';
    var eff = n<=optimalM ? 'Perfectly efficient!' : 'You can trim this  -  the optimal uses fewer commands.';
    setFeedback('good','<b>'+st+' Solved in '+n+' commands</b> (best possible ~'+optimalM+'). '+eff);
    el.next.classList.remove('rd-hidden');
    el.next.textContent = (levelIdx+1<LEVELS.length) ? 'Next Level \u2192' : 'See Results \u2192';
  }

  function nextLevel(){
    if(levelIdx+1<LEVELS.length){ levelIdx++; loadLevel(); }
    else showWin();
  }

  function showWin(){
    el.play.classList.add('rd-hidden');
    el.win.classList.remove('rd-hidden');
    var maxStars=LEVELS.length*3;
    el.win.innerHTML=
      '<div class="rd-win">'+
      '<h2>You directed the robot home! 🎉</h2>'+
      '<p>You planned command sequences with MOVE_FORWARD, ROTATE_LEFT, and ROTATE_RIGHT, traced them cell by cell, and kept the robot on the grid  -  exactly the algorithmic thinking the AP CSP robot questions test.</p>'+
      '<div class="big">'+totalStars+' / '+maxStars+' stars \u2605</div>'+
      '<p>Fewer commands = a more efficient algorithm. Rerun to earn every star.</p>'+
      '<button class="rd-btn next" id="rd-again" style="max-width:220px;margin:8px auto 0;">Play Again</button>'+
      '</div>';
    document.getElementById('rd-again').addEventListener('click',function(){
      levelIdx=0; totalStars=0; el.win.classList.add('rd-hidden'); el.play.classList.remove('rd-hidden'); loadLevel();
    });
    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsGameScore',{detail:{value:totalStars}}));
  }

  document.getElementById('rd-add-F').addEventListener('click',function(){ addCmd('F'); });
  document.getElementById('rd-add-L').addEventListener('click',function(){ addCmd('L'); });
  document.getElementById('rd-add-R').addEventListener('click',function(){ addCmd('R'); });
  el.run.addEventListener('click',run);
  el.undo.addEventListener('click',function(){ if(running||!program.length) return; program.pop(); resetRun(); renderProg(); });
  el.clear.addEventListener('click',function(){ if(running) return; program=[]; resetRun(); renderProg();
    setFeedback('info','Program cleared. Plan a new route to the flag.'); });
  el.next.addEventListener('click',nextLevel);

  loadLevel();
})();
})();</script>

      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A <strong>parameter</strong> is the placeholder name in the procedure header, like <code>n</code> in <code>def double(n)</code>. An <strong>argument</strong> is the actual value you pass at the call, like <code>5</code> in <code>double(5)</code>. The argument is copied into the parameter for that call.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What does a procedure return if it has no return statement?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">It returns the special value <code>None</code>. So if you print or store the result of a procedure that never returns, you get <code>None</code>. If your output is unexpectedly None, check whether the procedure actually returned its computed value.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Does changing a parameter inside a procedure change the caller's variable?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">No. A parameter is a local placeholder that exists only while the procedure runs. Reassigning it does not affect the caller's variables, even if they share the same name. To send a result back, you must <code>return</code> it and the caller must store it.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is procedural abstraction and why is it useful?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Procedural abstraction means giving a name to a process and using that name without worrying about the details inside. It removes duplicate code, makes programs easier to read and change, and hides implementation detail. It does not change what the program computes; it just organizes it better.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What does my Create Task procedure need to include?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">It must be a procedure you wrote yourself with a <strong>parameter that affects its behavior</strong>, and its body must include <strong>selection</strong> and <strong>iteration</strong>. In your written response, name the parameter, point to the loop and the conditional, and explain what the procedure returns.</div>

function loadScriptOnce(src){return new Promise(function(res,rej){
  if(document.querySelector('script[data-pyodide]')){res();return;}
  var s=document.createElement('script');s.src=src;s.setAttribute('data-pyodide','1');

  document.head.appendChild(s);});}

function cleanErr(msg){if(!msg)return 'error';var lines=String(msg).trim().split('\n');return lines.slice(-3).join('\n');}
function execUser(py,code){var output='',err=null;
  try{py.runPython('import sys, io\n__old_out = sys.stdout\nsys.stdout = io.StringIO()\nsys.stderr = sys.stdout');
    try{var ns=py.globals.get('dict')();py.runPython(code,{globals:ns});ns.destroy();}
    catch(e){err=cleanErr(e.message);}
    output=py.runPython('sys.stdout.getvalue()');}
  catch(e2){err=cleanErr((e2&&e2.message)||String(e2));}
  finally{try{py.runPython('sys.stdout = __old_out\nsys.stderr = __old_out');}catch(e3){}}
  return {output:output,err:err};}
