<style>
  @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=DM+Serif+Display:ital@0;1&family=DM+Sans:ital,opsz,wght@0,9..40,300;0,9..40,400;0,9..40,500;0,9..40,600;0,9..40,700;1,9..40,400&display=swap');
  :root{--navy:#0f1f3d;--bi3:#1a56db;--bi3-lt:#93c5fd;--bi3-bg:#eff6ff;--bi3-dk:#1e40af;--green:#16a34a;--amber:#d97706;--red:#dc2626;--slate:#64748b;--white:#ffffff;--py:#3b82f6;--pseudo:#8b5cf6;}
  *{box-sizing:border-box;margin:0;padding:0;}
  .lesson-page{font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;color:var(--navy);background:#f8fafc;line-height:1.6;}

  .lesson-breadcrumb{background:#fff;border-bottom:1px solid #e2e8f0;padding:12px 24px;}
  .lesson-breadcrumb-inner{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .lesson-breadcrumb a{color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;text-decoration:none;font-weight:500;}
  .bc-sep{color:#cbd5e1;}

  .social-proof-bar{background:#fff;border-bottom:1px solid #e2e8f0;padding:10px 24px;}
  .social-proof-inner{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:6px 20px;font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .social-proof-item{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;font-weight:500;}
  .social-proof-item strong{color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}

  .lesson-hero{background:var(--navy);background-image:radial-gradient(ellipse 60% 70% at 90% 20%,rgba(26,86,219,.28) 0%,transparent 60%);padding:48px 24px 40px;}
  .lesson-hero-inner{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;}
  .lesson-hero-meta{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .lesson-num-badge{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:44px;height:44px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;font-size:14px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;flex-shrink:0;}
  .lesson-eyebrow{font-size:12px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;}
  .lesson-hero h1{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:clamp(26px,4vw,40px)!important;line-height:1.2!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;}
  .lesson-hero-pills{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-pill{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.08);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);padding:5px 12px;border-radius:100px;font-size:12px;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .ced-tag{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;background:rgba(26,86,219,.25);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.3);padding:4px 10px;border-radius:100px;font-size:11px;font-weight:600;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;letter-spacing:.04em;}

  /* PROGRESS STRIP */
  .bi3-progress{background:#fff!important;border-bottom:1px solid #e2e8f0!important;padding:14px 20px!important;overflow-x:auto!important;-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch!important;}
  .bi3-progress-inner{display:flex!important;flex-direction:row!important;flex-wrap:nowrap!important;align-items:center!important;gap:0!important;width:max-content!important;min-width:100%!important;}
  .prog-step{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-step-link{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;text-decoration:none!important;cursor:pointer!important;}
  .prog-step-link:hover .prog-dot{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-dot{width:26px!important;height:26px!important;border-radius:50%!important;display:flex!important;align-items:center!important;justify-content:center!important;font-size:9px!important;font-weight:700!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-dot.active{background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;}
  .prog-dot.upcoming{background:#f1f5f9!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;}
  .prog-dot.done{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border:2px solid var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-label{font-size:8px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;line-height:1.2!important;white-space:nowrap!important;}
  .prog-label.active-label{color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-arrow{flex:1 0 4px!important;height:2px!important;background:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:18px!important;min-width:4px!important;max-width:16px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}

  /* MAIN */
  .lesson-main{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;padding:40px 24px 80px;}
  .lesson-objectives{background:var(--bi3-bg);border-left:4px solid var(--bi3);border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin-bottom:28px;}
  .lesson-objectives h2{font-size:14px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;text-transform:uppercase!important;letter-spacing:.06em!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .lesson-objectives ul{list-style:none;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-objectives li{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#1e3a8a;line-height:1.5;}
  .lesson-objectives li::before{content:"\2713";color:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:1px;}
  .score-impact{background:#f0fdf4;border:1px solid #bbf7d0;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 18px;margin-bottom:28px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#14532d;}
  .score-impact strong{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}

  /* HOOK */
  .hook-box{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:32px;}
  .hook-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .hook-box p{font-size:15px!important;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:0!important;}

  /* LESSON SECTIONS */
  .lesson-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .lesson-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .lesson-section h3{font-size:17px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-top:24px!important;margin-bottom:10px!important;}
  .lesson-section p{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section ul,.lesson-section ol{padding-left:20px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section li{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .lesson-section code{background:#eef2ff;color:#1e3a8a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e3a8a!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}

  /* DUAL CODE PANEL */
  .code-panel-wrap{margin:20px 0;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;}
  .code-panel-tabs{display:flex;background:#1e293b;}
  .code-tab{padding:8px 16px;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;border:none;background:transparent;letter-spacing:.04em;transition:background .15s;font-family:inherit;}
  .code-tab.py{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.pseudo{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.active{background:rgba(255,255,255,.15)!important;}
  .code-tab-label{font-size:10px;opacity:.6;margin-left:4px;font-weight:400;}
  .code-pane{background:#0f172a;padding:18px 20px;overflow-x:auto;height:0;overflow:hidden;padding:0;}
  .code-pane.active{height:auto;overflow-x:auto;padding:18px 20px;}
  .code-pane pre{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:0;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;max-width:100%;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-kw{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .py-fn{color:#6ee7b7!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#6ee7b7!important;}
  .py-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .py-str{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .py-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .py-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-op{color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;}
  .ps-kw{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .ps-op{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .ps-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .ps-str{color:#86efac!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#86efac!important;}
  .ps-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .ps-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* CALLOUTS */
  .callout-exam{background:#fffbeb;border:1px solid #fcd34d;border-left:4px solid var(--amber);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-exam-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--amber)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--amber)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-exam p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}
  .callout-trap{background:#fef2f2;border:1px solid #fca5a5;border-left:4px solid var(--red);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-opt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;padding:10px 14px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;font-family:monospace;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;background:#f8fafc;text-align:left;width:100%;transition:border-color .15s;}
  .mini-opt:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mini-opt.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}

    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>A program that greets one user is easy. A program that greets a thousand users, or keeps asking for a password until it is correct, needs to repeat itself. That repetition is iteration. Sometimes you know the exact count ahead of time, like sending five reminder emails. Sometimes you do not, like rolling a die until you get a six. This lesson is about controlling exactly how many times your code runs, and never one time too many or too few.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What Iteration Means</h2>
      <p><strong>Iteration</strong> is the repetition of a portion of an algorithm. Instead of writing the same instruction over and over, you write it once and tell the program how many times, or under what condition, to repeat it. Iteration is one of the three fundamental building blocks of every algorithm, alongside sequencing and selection, and it is exactly what the Create Performance Task rubric looks for.</p>
      <p>There are two flavors. <strong>Definite iteration</strong> repeats a fixed, known number of times. In AP pseudocode this is <code>REPEAT n TIMES</code>, and in Python it is <code>for i in range(n)</code>. <strong>Indefinite iteration</strong> repeats until some condition is met, and you do not know in advance how many passes that will take. That is <code>REPEAT UNTIL(condition)</code> in pseudocode and <code>while</code> in Python.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-1')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-1')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-1-py"><pre><span class="py-kw">for</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">i</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">in</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">range</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">3</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-str">"hi"</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-1-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-kw">REPEAT</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">3</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">TIMES</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"hi"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>The loop above runs <strong>exactly three times</strong> because <code>range(3)</code> produces the values 0, 1, and 2. The important idea for definite iteration: <code>range(n)</code> runs the body <strong>n times</strong>, but the loop variable takes the values 0 through n minus 1, not 1 through n. That gap is the source of the most common loop bug on the exam.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>The CED (AAP-2.J and AAP-2.K) requires you to read and write both loop types. Memorize the mapping: <code>REPEAT n TIMES</code> equals <code>for i in range(n)</code>, and <code>REPEAT UNTIL(cond)</code> equals <code>while not cond</code>. A definite loop always runs a countable number of times; an indefinite loop runs an unknown number of times.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Counters and Accumulators</h2>
      <p>Two patterns power almost every useful loop. A <strong>counter</strong> is a variable that goes up by one each pass to tally how many times something happened. An <strong>accumulator</strong> is a variable that keeps a running total, updated on every pass, so that by the end it holds the combined result of the whole loop.</p>
      <p>The recipe is always the same: set the variable to a starting value <strong>before</strong> the loop, update it <strong>inside</strong> the loop, and read it <strong>after</strong> the loop. Forgetting the initialization, or putting the final <code>print</code> inside the loop instead of after it, are classic mistakes.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-2')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-2')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-2-py"><pre><span class="py-var">total</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">0</span>
<span class="py-kw">for</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">i</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">in</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">range</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">1</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">6</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">total</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">total</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">i</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">total</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-2-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">total</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">0</span>
<span class="ps-var">i</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>
<span class="ps-kw">REPEAT</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">5</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">TIMES</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">total</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">total</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">i</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">i</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">i</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">total</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>This loop adds 1, then 2, then 3, 4, and 5 into <code>total</code>, so it prints 15. Notice the Python <code>range(1, 6)</code> stops <strong>before</strong> 6, giving the values 1 through 5. The pseudocode reaches the same result with <code>REPEAT 5 TIMES</code> and its own counter. Both are definite iteration; they run a fixed five times.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 Final value matters</div>
        <p>Exam questions love to ask for the value of the accumulator or the loop counter <strong>after</strong> the loop ends, not during it. Trace every pass, then report the value once the loop has finished. Do not stop tracing one pass too early.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>REPEAT UNTIL Is the Opposite of while</h2>
      <p>This is the single most tested idea in this topic, and it trips up students every year. A Python <code>while</code> loop keeps going <strong>while its condition is true</strong> and stops when the condition becomes false. An AP <code>REPEAT UNTIL</code> loop is the mirror image: it keeps going <strong>until its condition becomes true</strong>, checking after nothing and stopping the moment the condition is true.</p>
      <p>Because they are opposites, translating between them means <strong>negating the condition</strong>. A loop that should continue while <code>count < 3</code> in Python becomes <code>REPEAT UNTIL (count >= 3)</code> in pseudocode. Same behavior, flipped condition.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-3')">🐛 Python (while continues while TRUE)</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-3')">📋 Pseudocode (REPEAT UNTIL stops at TRUE)</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-3-py"><pre><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">0</span>
<span class="py-kw">while</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"><</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">3</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">count</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">1</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-3-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">0</span>
<span class="ps-kw">REPEAT</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">UNTIL</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">></span><span class="ps-var">=</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">3</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">count</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Both loops above print 0, 1, 2 and then stop. The Python version continues <strong>while</strong> <code>count < 3</code> is true. The pseudocode version repeats <strong>until</strong> <code>count >= 3</code> is true. Read the two conditions and confirm they are logical opposites of each other. If you ever see a REPEAT UNTIL and want to think in Python, mentally rewrite it as <code>while not (condition)</code>.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ The direction trap</div>
        <p>If a question gives you a <code>REPEAT UNTIL (x > 10)</code> and you read it as if it were a Python <code>while x > 10</code>, you will get the loop backwards and pick the wrong answer every time. UNTIL means stop when true. WHILE means continue when true. They are not the same word.</p>
      </div>

      <h2>Zero Passes and Infinite Loops</h2>
      <p>Two boundary cases show up again and again. First, a loop can run its body <strong>zero times</strong>. If a <code>REPEAT UNTIL</code> condition is <strong>already true</strong> when the loop is first reached, the body never runs at all. The same happens in Python when a <code>while</code> condition is false from the start.</p>

<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"run"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">x</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">x</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-str">"done"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Here <code>x</code> is 10, so the Python condition <code>x < 5</code> is false immediately and the body is skipped; the program prints only <code>done</code>. The pseudocode <code>REPEAT UNTIL (x >= 5)</code> is already true (10 is at least 5), so it also skips the body. A loop running zero times is not an error, it is a legal and common outcome.</p>
      <p>Second, an <strong>infinite loop</strong> happens when the stopping condition never becomes true. In a counter loop this almost always means you forgot to update the counter, so the condition is stuck. Every indefinite loop must contain something that eventually makes it stop.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Off-by-one</div>
        <p><code>range(1, 5)</code> gives 1, 2, 3, 4. It stops <strong>before</strong> the second number. To include 5, you need <code>range(1, 6)</code>. Whenever a loop prints or sums the wrong count of items by exactly one, suspect the range bounds first.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="cpt-connection">
      <div class="cpt-connection-label">📋 Create Performance Task • Iteration earns a required rubric point</div>
      <p>The Create Task rubric awards a point for an algorithm that includes <strong>sequencing, selection, AND iteration</strong> working together. A loop is not optional decoration; it is one of the three ingredients the readers must be able to point to. Iteration is also how your program processes a whole collection of input instead of a single value.</p>
      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>Imagine a program that adds up the numbers 1 through <code>n</code> to produce a running total:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">sum <- 0
count <- 1
REPEAT UNTIL (count > n)
{
    sum <- sum + count
    count <- count + 1
}
DISPLAY(sum)</div>
      <p>In your written response, identify the loop and explain what it repeats and how it stops:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"The iteration repeats the body once for each value from 1 up to <code>n</code>, so it runs a number of times that depends on the input."</li>
        <li>"On each pass, the accumulator <code>sum</code> is updated by adding the current <code>count</code>, which builds the running total."</li>
        <li>"The counter <code>count</code> increases every pass, so the stopping condition <code>count > n</code> eventually becomes true and the loop ends."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The trap to avoid</h3>
      <p>Make sure the loop actually stops. If you forget the <code>count <- count + 1</code> line, the condition never becomes true and you have an infinite loop, which earns no point and freezes the program. Also confirm your range covers the right values, an off-by-one loop that misses the first or last item is a partial-credit killer. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between definite and indefinite iteration?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Definite iteration repeats a fixed, known number of times, like <code>REPEAT n TIMES</code> or <code>for i in range(n)</code>. Indefinite iteration repeats until a condition is met and you do not know the count in advance, like <code>REPEAT UNTIL(condition)</code> or a Python <code>while</code> loop.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why is REPEAT UNTIL the opposite of a Python while loop?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A <code>while</code> loop continues <strong>while</strong> its condition is true and stops when it becomes false. A <code>REPEAT UNTIL</code> loop continues <strong>until</strong> its condition becomes true, so it stops when the condition is true. To translate one to the other you negate the condition: <code>REPEAT UNTIL(c)</code> is the same as <code>while not c</code>.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How many times does range(n) run?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Exactly n times. The loop variable takes the values 0, 1, 2, up to n minus 1, which is n values total. This is why range(3) runs three times but never uses the value 3, and it is the source of most off-by-one bugs.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What causes an infinite loop?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">An infinite loop happens when the stopping condition never becomes true. In a counter loop this usually means you forgot to update the counter inside the loop, so the condition stays the same on every pass. Every indefinite loop needs something inside it that eventually makes the condition stop the loop.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Can a loop body run zero times?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Yes. If a <code>REPEAT UNTIL</code> condition is already true when the loop is first reached, or a Python <code>while</code> condition is false from the start, the body never runs. Running zero times is a legal, common outcome, not an error.</div>
      </div>

  try{py=await ensurePy();}catch(e){out.className='code-output show err';
    out.textContent='Could not load the Python engine. Check your connection and try Run again.';if(btn)btn.disabled=false;return;}
  var code=document.getElementById('ce-'+n).value;var res=execUser(py,code);
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);
  if(res.err){out.className='code-output show err';out.textContent='\u2717 Error:\n'+res.err;}
  else{var got=(res.output||'').replace(/\s+$/,'');var exp=CE_EXPECTED[n];
    var shown=res.output&&res.output.length?res.output.replace(/\n$/,''):'(no output)';
    if(exp!==undefined&&got===exp){out.className='code-output show ok';out.textContent='\u2713 Correct! Output:\n'+shown;if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}
    else if(exp!==undefined){out.className='code-output show err';out.textContent='Output:\n'+shown+'\n\nTarget: '+exp+'\nKeep going, or press Hint.';}
    else{out.className='code-output show';out.textContent='Output:\n'+shown;}
    if(typeof exp!=='undefined')_activity({activity:'exercise-1',item:'ce-'+n,correct:(got===exp)});}
  if(btn)btn.disabled=false;}
function showHint(n){var box=document.getElementById('ce-hint-'+n);
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]===undefined)CE_HINT_IDX[n]=0;var hints=CE_HINTS[n]||[];
  if(hints.length===0)return;
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]>=hints.length)CE_HINT_IDX[n]=hints.length-1;
  var shown=CE_HINT_IDX[n]+1;var text='';
  for(var i=0;i<shown;i++){text+='Hint '+(i+1)+': '+hints[i]+(i<shown-1?'\n\n':'');}
  box.textContent=text;box.className='code-hint show';box.style.whiteSpace='pre-wrap';
  LESSON_USAGE.hints[n]=shown;LESSON_USAGE.totalHints=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.hints);updateUsage();
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]<hints.length-1)CE_HINT_IDX[n]++;
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}

  LESSON_USAGE.solutions[n]=1;LESSON_USAGE.totalSolutions=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.solutions);updateUsage();}
var vtScore=0,vtQ=0,vtStreak=0,vtAnswered=false;
function vtRender(){if(vtQ>=VT_QS.length){vtShowResults();return;}vtAnswered=false;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  document.getElementById('vt-qn').textContent=(vtQ+1)+'/'+VT_QS.length;
  document.getElementById('vt-streak').textContent=vtStreak;
  var codeEl=document.getElementById('vt-code');codeEl.innerHTML='';
  q.lines.forEach(function(line,i){var span=document.createElement('span');
    span.className='vt-line'+(i===q.hl?' hl':'');span.textContent=line;codeEl.appendChild(span);});
  document.getElementById('vt-question').textContent=q.q;
  var optEl=document.getElementById('vt-options');optEl.innerHTML='';
  q.choices.forEach(function(ch,i){var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='vt-btn';btn.textContent=ch;
    btn.onclick=(function(idx){return function(){vtAnswer(idx);};})(i);optEl.appendChild(btn);});
  document.getElementById('vt-fb').className='vt-fb';document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next';}
function vtAnswer(idx){if(vtAnswered)return;vtAnswered=true;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  var btns=document.querySelectorAll('.vt-btn');btns.forEach(function(b){b.onclick=null;});
  var fb=document.getElementById('vt-fb');
  if(idx===q.correct){vtScore++;vtStreak++;btns[idx].classList.add('c');fb.textContent='\u2713 Correct! '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb c';}
  else{vtStreak=0;btns[idx].classList.add('w');btns[q.correct].classList.add('rv');fb.textContent='\u2717 Not quite. '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb w';}
  document.getElementById('vt-score').textContent=vtScore;document.getElementById('vt-streak').textContent=vtStreak;
  document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next show';}
function vtNext(){vtQ++;vtRender();}
function vtShowResults(){document.getElementById('vt-active').style.display='none';
  document.getElementById('vt-results').className='vt-results show';
  document.getElementById('vt-res-score').textContent=vtScore+'/'+VT_QS.length;
  document.getElementById('vt-res-msg').textContent=VT_MSGS[Math.min(vtScore,VT_MSGS.length-1)];
  _activity({activity:'exercise-2',earned:vtScore,possible:VT_QS.length});}
function vtRestart(){vtScore=0;vtQ=0;vtStreak=0;vtAnswered=false;
  document.getElementById('vt-results').className='vt-results';
  document.getElementById('vt-active').style.display='block';
  document.getElementById('vt-score').textContent='0';vtRender();}
vtRender();

  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}

  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}

  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}

  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .game-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .vt-stat{text-align:center;}
  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .vt-line{display:block;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;white-space:pre;}
  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .vt-question{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-options{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-btn{padding:12px;border-radius:9px;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);cursor:pointer;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;font-family:monospace;transition:all .15s;}
  .vt-btn:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:rgba(26,86,219,.2);}
  .vt-btn.c{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.15);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;}
  .vt-btn.w{border-color:#f87171;background:rgba(248,113,113,.15);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .vt-btn.rv{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.08);}
  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}
  .vt-fb.w{background:rgba(248,113,113,.1);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;display:block;}
  .vt-next{display:none;width:100%;padding:12px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

  .vt-results{display:none;text-align:center;padding:20px;}
  .vt-results.show{display:block;}
  .vt-res-score{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:52px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}

  .code-editor-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .code-problem-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}

  /* FAQ */

  .related-links-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(200px,1fr));gap:8px;}

  <div class="lesson-main">

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Explain that a library is a reusable collection of procedures and a form of procedural abstraction</span></li>
        <li><span>Import a library and call its procedures with the correct arguments</span></li>
        <li><span>Read an API or documentation to predict what a procedure call returns</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain why reusing well-tested library code saves time and reduces errors</span></li>
        <li><span>Recognize that a library hides its internal implementation behind its API</span></li>
        <li><span>Separate a library call from your own student-developed procedure on the Create Task</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span><strong>Exam weight:</strong> Library questions in Big Idea 3 hand you a documented procedure and ask you to predict a result or spot a call that breaks the documentation. They reward careful reading of an API, and they connect directly to procedural abstraction elsewhere in the unit.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>You use libraries every day without thinking about it. When your phone finds the square root for a calculator, sorts your photos by date, or draws a map, it is calling procedures someone else already wrote and tested. You did not build those from scratch, and neither should your programs. A library lets you reach for a ready-made, reliable procedure by name. This lesson is about how to import one, read its documentation, and predict exactly what it gives back.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What a Library Is</h2>
      <p>A <strong>library</strong> is a collection of procedures that other programmers have already written, tested, and packaged so you can reuse them. Instead of writing your own square-root routine from scratch, you reach into a library and call the procedure that is already there. A library is a form of <strong>procedural abstraction</strong>: it lets you use powerful operations by name without knowing, or caring, how they are built internally.</p>
      <p>In Python you bring a library into your program with <code>import</code>, then call its procedures with the library name, a dot, and the procedure name. The example below imports the <code>math</code> library and calls its <code>sqrt</code> procedure.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-1')">🐛 Python (math library)</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-1')">📋 Pseudocode (library call)</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-1-py"><pre><span class="py-kw">import</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">math</span>

<span class="py-var">x</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">16</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">math</span><span class="py-var">.</span><span class="py-var">sqrt</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">x</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-1-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">x</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">16</span>
<span class="ps-var">result</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">squareRoot</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">x</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">result</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Notice what you did <strong>not</strong> have to do: you never wrote the algorithm that computes a square root. You only had to know the procedure's name and what it expects. That is the whole point of a library. On the right, AP pseudocode has no <code>import</code> keyword, but the idea is identical: a library provides a procedure like <code>squareRoot</code> that you simply call.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>The CED (AAP-3.D) says a library is a collection of procedures that may be used in creating new programs, and that using existing, correct library code saves time and reduces errors. You are not expected to memorize any real library. You are expected to read a short description of a procedure and predict what a call to it produces.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">✍ Mini Exercise 1 • Predict the output</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">The library procedure <code>floor(x)</code> returns the largest integer that is not greater than <code>x</code>. What does this print?</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-code"><pre style="margin:0;white-space:pre;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0;"><span class="py-kw">import</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">math</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">math</span><span class="py-var">.</span><span class="py-var">floor</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">6.99</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="me1-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me1','A','A','me1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> 6</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me1','B','A','me1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> 7</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me1','C','A','me1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> 6.99</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me1','D','A','me1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> 7.0</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="me1-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>An API Is the Instructions</h2>
      <p>An <strong>API</strong>, short for application program interface, is the description of how to use a library: the names of its procedures, what arguments each one takes, and what each one returns. The API is the contract between you and the library. You read the API, sometimes called the documentation, to learn how to call a procedure correctly, exactly the way you read the instructions on a microwave without knowing the electronics inside.</p>
      <p>Because the API hides the internal details, two things follow. First, you must supply the <strong>right arguments in the right order</strong>, because that is what the documentation promises. Second, you can predict a procedure's result from its documented behavior alone. The <code>math</code> library documents that <code>floor</code> rounds down and <code>ceil</code> rounds up:</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-3')">🐛 Python (reading the API)</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-3')">📋 Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-3-py"><pre><span class="py-kw">import</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">math</span>

<span class="py-comment"># floor: largest integer not greater than x</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">math</span><span class="py-var">.</span><span class="py-var">floor</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">7.9</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-comment"># ceil: smallest integer not less than x</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">math</span><span class="py-var">.</span><span class="py-var">ceil</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">7.1</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-3-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">floor</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">7.9</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">ceil</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">7.1</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Reading that documentation tells you <code>floor(7.9)</code> is <code>7</code> and <code>ceil(7.1)</code> is <code>8</code>, even though you never see the code that computes them. That is what an exam question means when it hands you a described procedure and asks for the result.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Wrong arguments, wrong result</div>
        <p>A library procedure only behaves as documented if you call it as documented. If the API says <code>pow(base, exponent)</code> needs two arguments and you pass one, the program raises an error, not a guess. A favorite trap gives you a procedure with a specific argument order and a call that swaps or drops an argument. Always match the call to the API.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">✍ Mini Exercise 2 • Spot the flaw</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">Assume nothing else has run. Why does this line fail instead of printing <code>9.0</code>?</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-code"><pre style="margin:0;white-space:pre;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0;"><span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">math</span><span class="py-var">.</span><span class="py-var">sqrt</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">81</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="me2-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me2','A','A','me2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> the math library was never imported, so math.sqrt is undefined</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me2','B','A','me2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> sqrt requires two arguments</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me2','C','A','me2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> 81 is not a perfect square</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('me2','D','A','me2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> print cannot display a decimal number</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="me2-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Use It, or Rebuild It Yourself</h2>
      <p>Why does a library matter? Because reusing existing, well-tested code <strong>saves development time and reduces errors</strong>. Someone already debugged the square-root procedure across millions of inputs. If you rewrote it yourself you would spend hours and probably introduce a bug the library long ago fixed. Choosing to call a library procedure instead of reimplementing it is one of the most practical decisions a programmer makes.</p>
      <p>You can also build your own small library: a set of procedures you write once and then call by name throughout a program. That is exactly what procedural abstraction gives you, and it is why a library and a procedure are the same idea at different scales. Here is a two-procedure mini library and a call to it:</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-2')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-2')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-2-py"><pre><span class="py-comment"># a tiny library of procedures</span>
<span class="py-kw">def</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">area</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">w</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">h</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">:</span>
<span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-kw">return</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">w</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">h</span>

<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">area</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">4</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">3</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-2-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-kw">PROCEDURE</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">area</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">w</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">h</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">RETURN</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">w</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">*</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">h</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-var">}</span>

<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">area</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">4</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">3</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Once <code>area</code> exists, the rest of the program just calls <code>area(4, 3)</code> and trusts it to return <code>12</code>. The caller does not re-derive width times height every time. That reuse is the benefit, whether the procedure came from Python's <code>math</code> library or from a library you wrote yourself.</p>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Predicting a Result From Documentation</h2>
      <p>Most library questions on the exam are not about writing code at all. They give you a procedure's documented behavior and one or two calls, then ask what is displayed. Use a short, mechanical routine:</p>
      <ol>
        <li>Read the documentation sentence and restate the rule in your own words.</li>
        <li>Identify each argument in the call and match it to the documented parameter.</li>
        <li>Apply the rule to those exact argument values.</li>
        <li>Do not assume any behavior the documentation did not promise.</li>
      </ol>
      <p>For instance, a library documents <code>clamp(v, lo, hi)</code> as: returns <code>v</code> when it lies between <code>lo</code> and <code>hi</code>, returns <code>lo</code> when <code>v</code> is smaller, and returns <code>hi</code> when <code>v</code> is larger. Then <code>clamp(12, 0, 10)</code> must return <code>10</code>, because 12 is larger than the high bound. You solved that with the documentation alone, never seeing inside <code>clamp</code>. That is exactly the skill AAP-3.D is testing.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 Abstraction hides the how</div>
        <p>When a question asks what a library gives you, the answer is a way to use a procedure without knowing its implementation. You interact through the API. Any answer choice that claims you must understand the internal code to call a library procedure is describing the opposite of abstraction, and is wrong.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="cpt-connection-label">📋 Create Performance Task • Libraries help, but the abstraction point is yours</div>
      <p>Libraries are welcome in your Create Task program, and calling well-tested code is smart engineering. But there is a rule you must not miss: the point for a student-developed procedure requires a procedure that <strong>you</strong> wrote, with a parameter that affects the procedure's behavior. Calling a library procedure alone does not earn that point.</p>
      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>Suppose your program uses the math library to compute a distance, then feeds it into a procedure you wrote:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">PROCEDURE distanceLabel(d)
{
    IF (d > 100)
    {
        RETURN("far")
    }
    ELSE
    {
        RETURN("near")
    }
}

gap <- squareRoot(dx * dx + dy * dy)
DISPLAY(distanceLabel(gap))</div>
      <p>In your written response, separate what the library did from what you did:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"I used a library procedure, <code>squareRoot</code>, to compute the distance, which saved time and avoided errors."</li>
        <li>"I developed my own procedure <code>distanceLabel</code> whose parameter <code>d</code> changes the returned label, so it demonstrates abstraction."</li>
        <li>"The parameter generalizes the procedure so it works for any distance the program produces, not one fixed value."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The trap to avoid</h3>
      <p>Do not point to a library call, like <code>squareRoot</code> or <code>sqrt</code>, as your student-developed procedure. The reader is looking for a procedure you defined with a parameter that affects its behavior. Use libraries freely, but make sure your abstraction is your own. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is a library in AP CSP?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A library is a collection of procedures that other programmers have already written and tested, packaged so you can reuse them in a new program. Using a library saves development time and reduces errors because the code is already known to work.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is an API?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">An API, or application program interface, is the description of how to use a library. It lists each procedure, the arguments it takes, and what it returns. You read the API, also called the documentation, to call a procedure correctly without seeing its internal code.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why is a library considered abstraction?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A library lets you use a procedure by name through its API without knowing how it is implemented inside. That hiding of detail is procedural abstraction. You only need to know what the procedure does, not how it does it.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Do I have to memorize real libraries for the exam?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">No. The exam gives you a short description of a procedure and asks you to predict what a call returns, or to spot a call that does not match the documentation. The skill is reading documentation, not memorizing any specific library.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Can a library procedure earn my Create Task abstraction point?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">No. The student-developed procedure point requires a procedure you wrote yourself with a parameter that affects its behavior. You may use library procedures freely in your program, but your abstraction must be your own code.</div>
      </div>
