  if(el){el.innerHTML='Hints used: <strong>'+LESSON_USAGE.totalHints+'</strong> • Solutions viewed: <strong>'+LESSON_USAGE.totalSolutions+'</strong>';}
  try{document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('lessonUsage',{detail:LESSON_USAGE}));}catch(e){}
}
function loadScriptOnce(src){return new Promise(function(res,rej){
  if(document.querySelector('script[data-pyodide]')){res();return;}
  var s=document.createElement('script');s.src=src;s.setAttribute('data-pyodide','1');
  s.onload=function(){res();};s.onerror=function(){rej(new Error('script load failed'));};
  document.head.appendChild(s);});}
function ensurePy(){if(window.__pyPromise)return window.__pyPromise;
  window.__pyPromise=(async function(){await loadScriptOnce(PY_URL+'pyodide.js');
    var py=await loadPyodide({indexURL:PY_URL});window.__pyodide=py;return py;})();
  return window.__pyPromise;}
function cleanErr(msg){if(!msg)return 'error';var lines=String(msg).trim().split('\n');return lines.slice(-3).join('\n');}
function execUser(py,code){var output='',err=null;
  try{py.runPython('import sys, io\n__old_out = sys.stdout\nsys.stdout = io.StringIO()\nsys.stderr = sys.stdout');
    try{var ns=py.globals.get('dict')();py.runPython(code,{globals:ns});ns.destroy();}
    catch(e){err=cleanErr(e.message);}
    output=py.runPython('sys.stdout.getvalue()');}
  catch(e2){err=cleanErr((e2&&e2.message)||String(e2));}
  finally{try{py.runPython('sys.stdout = __old_out\nsys.stderr = __old_out');}catch(e3){}}
  return {output:output,err:err};}
async function runPy(n){
  var out=document.getElementById('ce-out-'+n),btn=document.getElementById('run-btn-'+n);
  out.className='code-output show';out.textContent='Loading Python (first run may take a few seconds)...';
  if(btn)btn.disabled=true;var py;
  try{py=await ensurePy();}catch(e){out.className='code-output show err';
    out.textContent='Could not load the Python engine. Check your connection and try Run again.';if(btn)btn.disabled=false;return;}
  var code=document.getElementById('ce-'+n).value;var res=execUser(py,code);
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);
  if(res.err){out.className='code-output show err';out.textContent='\u2717 Error:\n'+res.err;}
  else{var got=(res.output||'').replace(/\s+$/,'');var exp=CE_EXPECTED[n];
    var shown=res.output&&res.output.length?res.output.replace(/\n$/,''):'(no output)';
    if(exp!==undefined&&got===exp){out.className='code-output show ok';out.textContent='\u2713 Correct! Output:\n'+shown;if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}
    else if(exp!==undefined){out.className='code-output show err';out.textContent='Output:\n'+shown+'\n\nTarget: '+exp+'\nKeep going, or press Hint.';}
    else{out.className='code-output show';out.textContent='Output:\n'+shown;}
    if(typeof exp!=='undefined')_activity({activity:'exercise-1',item:'ce-'+n,correct:(got===exp)});}
  if(btn)btn.disabled=false;}
function showHint(n){var box=document.getElementById('ce-hint-'+n);
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]===undefined)CE_HINT_IDX[n]=0;var hints=CE_HINTS[n]||[];
  if(hints.length===0)return;
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]>=hints.length)CE_HINT_IDX[n]=hints.length-1;
  var shown=CE_HINT_IDX[n]+1;var text='';
  for(var i=0;i<shown;i++){text+='Hint '+(i+1)+': '+hints[i]+(i<shown-1?'\n\n':'');}
  box.textContent=text;box.className='code-hint show';box.style.whiteSpace='pre-wrap';
  LESSON_USAGE.hints[n]=shown;LESSON_USAGE.totalHints=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.hints);updateUsage();
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]<hints.length-1)CE_HINT_IDX[n]++;
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}
function showSol(n){var box=document.getElementById('ce-sol-'+n);box.textContent=CE_SOL[n]||'';box.className='code-solution show';
  LESSON_USAGE.solutions[n]=1;LESSON_USAGE.totalSolutions=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.solutions);updateUsage();}
var vtScore=0,vtQ=0,vtStreak=0,vtAnswered=false;
function vtRender(){if(vtQ>=VT_QS.length){vtShowResults();return;}vtAnswered=false;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  document.getElementById('vt-qn').textContent=(vtQ+1)+'/'+VT_QS.length;
  document.getElementById('vt-streak').textContent=vtStreak;
  var codeEl=document.getElementById('vt-code');codeEl.innerHTML='';
  q.lines.forEach(function(line,i){var span=document.createElement('span');
    span.className='vt-line'+(i===q.hl?' hl':'');span.textContent=line;codeEl.appendChild(span);});
  document.getElementById('vt-question').textContent=q.q;
  var optEl=document.getElementById('vt-options');optEl.innerHTML='';
  q.choices.forEach(function(ch,i){var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='vt-btn';btn.textContent=ch;
    btn.onclick=(function(idx){return function(){vtAnswer(idx);};})(i);optEl.appendChild(btn);});
  document.getElementById('vt-fb').className='vt-fb';document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next';}
function vtAnswer(idx){if(vtAnswered)return;vtAnswered=true;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  var btns=document.querySelectorAll('.vt-btn');btns.forEach(function(b){b.onclick=null;});
  var fb=document.getElementById('vt-fb');
  if(idx===q.correct){vtScore++;vtStreak++;btns[idx].classList.add('c');fb.textContent='\u2713 Correct! '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb c';}
  else{vtStreak=0;btns[idx].classList.add('w');btns[q.correct].classList.add('rv');fb.textContent='\u2717 Not quite. '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb w';}

  document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next show';}

function vtRestart(){vtScore=0;vtQ=0;vtStreak=0;vtAnswered=false;
  document.getElementById('vt-results').className='vt-results';
  document.getElementById('vt-active').style.display='block';
  document.getElementById('vt-score').textContent='0';vtRender();}
vtRender();

  /* CPT CONNECTION */

  /* MCQ */

  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}

  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}

  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}

  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}

      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span><strong>Exam weight:</strong> Lists power a large share of Big Idea 3 tracing and spot-the-bug items, and a list is a required element of the Create Task. The 0-indexed versus 1-indexed gap and out-of-range indexing are among the most common traps on the whole exam.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>A playlist does not use a separate variable for every song. It uses one list and reaches song number 4 by its position. But here is the catch that costs points every year: Python calls the first song position 0, while the AP pseudocode reference sheet calls it position 1. Same songs, different numbers. This lesson makes that gap, and every list operation around it, automatic.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What a List Is, and the Indexing Gap</h2>
      <p>A <strong>list</strong> stores many values under one name. Instead of <code>a</code>, <code>b</code>, <code>c</code>, and <code>d</code>, you keep four related values in one ordered collection and reach any of them by its position, called an <strong>index</strong>. Lists are how a program manages a group of data whose size you may not know in advance.</p>
      <p>Here is the single most tested idea in this topic, and it trips up students on every exam: the two notations you will see count from different starting points. <strong>Python lists are 0-indexed</strong>, so the first element is at index 0 and the last is at index <code>len(list) - 1</code>. <strong>AP pseudocode lists are 1-indexed</strong>, so the first element is at index 1 and the last is at index <code>LENGTH(list)</code>. Same list, same values, different index numbers.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-1')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-1')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-1-py"><pre><span class="py-var">nums</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">10</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">20</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">30</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">40</span><span class="py-var">]</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">nums</span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">0</span><span class="py-var">]</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">nums</span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-num">3</span><span class="py-var">]</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-1-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">nums</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-num">10</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">20</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">30</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">40</span><span class="ps-var">]</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">nums</span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-num">1</span><span class="ps-var">]</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">nums</span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-num">4</span><span class="ps-var">]</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Look closely: both panels print 10 and then 40, the first and last values. But Python reaches the first value with <code>nums[0]</code> and the last with <code>nums[3]</code>, while AP pseudocode reaches the exact same values with <code>nums[1]</code> and <code>nums[4]</code>. Read every index question by first asking which notation you are in.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>On the reference sheet, <code>aList[1]</code> is the FIRST element and <code>aList[LENGTH(aList)]</code> is the LAST. When a question is written in Python instead, index 0 is the first element and <code>len(aList) - 1</code> is the last. Decide the notation before you count, and the off-by-one traps disappear.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Updating, Appending, and Length</h2>
      <p>Once a list exists you can change an element in place by assigning to its index: <code>nums[1] = 99</code> replaces whatever was at index 1. You can grow the list from the end with <code>append</code>, which always adds one new element after the current last one. And <code>len(nums)</code> reports how many elements the list currently holds, a value that changes every time you add or remove.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-2')">🐛 Python</button>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Insert and Remove: Everything Shifts</h2>
      <p>Inserting or removing an element in the middle of a list does more than change one spot. Every element after the change <strong>shifts</strong> to a new index to keep the list packed with no gaps. This shifting is where index bugs are born, because a position you were pointing at a moment ago may now hold a different value.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-3')">🐛 Python (0-indexed)</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-3')">📋 Pseudocode (1-indexed)</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-3-py"><pre><span class="py-var">letters</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">[</span><span class="py-str">"a"</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-str">"b"</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-str">"c"</span><span class="py-var">]</span>
<span class="py-var">letters</span><span class="py-var">.</span><span class="py-var">insert</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">1</span><span class="py-var">,</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-str">"x"</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-var">letters</span><span class="py-var">.</span><span class="py-var">pop</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">0</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">letters</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-3-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">letters</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">[</span><span class="ps-str">"a"</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-str">"b"</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-str">"c"</span><span class="ps-var">]</span>
<span class="ps-kw">INSERT</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">letters</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-str">"x"</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">REMOVE</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">letters</span><span class="ps-var">,</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">1</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">letters</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Start with <code>["a", "b", "c"]</code>. In Python, <code>insert(1, "x")</code> drops <code>"x"</code> at index 1 and pushes <code>"b"</code> and <code>"c"</code> right, giving <code>["a", "x", "b", "c"]</code>. Then <code>pop(0)</code> removes the element at index 0, and everything shifts left, leaving <code>["x", "b", "c"]</code>. The pseudocode reaches the identical result, but its <code>INSERT</code> uses index 2 and its <code>REMOVE</code> uses index 1 because it counts from 1.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ The shift trap</div>
        <p>After you remove an element, the list gets one shorter and the largest valid index drops by one. Code that still reaches for the old last index will run past the end and crash. After you insert, values move to higher indices. Never assume an element kept its old position across an insert or remove.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Traversing a List with a Loop</h2>
      <p>A <strong>traversal</strong> visits every element of a list one at a time, usually with a loop. Traversal is how you sum values, search for a target, or count how many match a rule, no matter how long the list is. The most common Python form is <code>for element in list</code>, which hands you each value in order without you managing an index at all.</p>
      <p>You can also traverse by index with <code>for i in range(len(list))</code>. That form is powerful, but it is exactly where the bounds trap lives: the valid indices are 0 through <code>len(list) - 1</code>, so you loop <code>range(len(list))</code>. If you loop one step too far, you index past the end and the program crashes.</p>

<span class="ps-var">{</span>
<span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">total</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">total</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">s</span>

      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why do Python and AP pseudocode number list elements differently?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">They just use different starting points. Python is 0-indexed, so the first element is at index 0 and the last is at index <code>len(list) - 1</code>. AP pseudocode is 1-indexed, so the first element is at index 1 and the last is at index <code>LENGTH(list)</code>. Decide which notation a question uses before you count positions.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the last valid index of a list?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">In Python it is <code>len(list) - 1</code>, because indexing starts at 0. In AP pseudocode it is <code>LENGTH(list)</code>, because indexing starts at 1. Reaching for one position past the last valid index is the most common list error and it causes an out-of-range crash.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What happens to the other elements when I insert or remove?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">They shift. Inserting pushes every later element to a higher index to make room. Removing pulls every later element to a lower index to close the gap, and the list gets one shorter. Never assume an element kept its old index across an insert or remove.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What does it mean to traverse a list?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Traversing means visiting every element in order, usually with a loop, so you can sum values, search for a target, or count matches. In Python, <code>for element in list</code> gives you each value directly, while <code>for i in range(len(list))</code> gives you each index.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How do lists help my Create Task?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A list lets your program manage many related values under one name instead of dozens of separate variables, which earns the collection point. Traversing that list with a loop earns toward the algorithm point. Describe the list by name and explain how the traversal uses it in your written response.</div>

  try{py.runPython('import sys, io\n__old_out = sys.stdout\nsys.stdout = io.StringIO()\nsys.stderr = sys.stdout');

  .lesson-breadcrumb a{color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;text-decoration:none;font-weight:500;}
  .bc-sep{color:#cbd5e1;}

  .social-proof-bar{background:#fff;border-bottom:1px solid #e2e8f0;padding:10px 24px;}
  .social-proof-inner{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:6px 20px;font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .social-proof-item{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;font-weight:500;}
  .social-proof-item strong{color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}

  .lesson-hero{background:var(--navy);background-image:radial-gradient(ellipse 60% 70% at 90% 20%,rgba(26,86,219,.28) 0%,transparent 60%);padding:48px 24px 40px;}
  .lesson-hero-inner{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;}
  .lesson-hero-meta{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .lesson-num-badge{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:44px;height:44px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;font-size:14px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;flex-shrink:0;}
  .lesson-eyebrow{font-size:12px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;}
  .lesson-hero h1{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:clamp(26px,4vw,40px)!important;line-height:1.2!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;}
  .lesson-hero-pills{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-pill{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.08);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);padding:5px 12px;border-radius:100px;font-size:12px;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .ced-tag{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;background:rgba(26,86,219,.25);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.3);padding:4px 10px;border-radius:100px;font-size:11px;font-weight:600;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;letter-spacing:.04em;}

  /* PROGRESS STRIP */
  .bi3-progress{background:#fff!important;border-bottom:1px solid #e2e8f0!important;padding:14px 20px!important;overflow-x:auto!important;-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch!important;}
  .bi3-progress-inner{display:flex!important;flex-direction:row!important;flex-wrap:nowrap!important;align-items:center!important;gap:0!important;width:max-content!important;min-width:100%!important;}
  .prog-step{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-step-link{display:flex!important;flex-direction:column!important;align-items:center!important;min-width:46px!important;text-align:center!important;flex-shrink:0!important;text-decoration:none!important;cursor:pointer!important;}
  .prog-step-link:hover .prog-dot{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-dot{width:26px!important;height:26px!important;border-radius:50%!important;display:flex!important;align-items:center!important;justify-content:center!important;font-size:9px!important;font-weight:700!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-dot.active{background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;}
  .prog-dot.upcoming{background:#f1f5f9!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;}
  .prog-dot.done{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border:2px solid var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-label{font-size:8px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;line-height:1.2!important;white-space:nowrap!important;}
  .prog-label.active-label{color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-arrow{flex:1 0 4px!important;height:2px!important;background:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:18px!important;min-width:4px!important;max-width:16px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}

  /* MAIN */
  .lesson-main{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;padding:40px 24px 80px;}
  .lesson-objectives{background:var(--bi3-bg);border-left:4px solid var(--bi3);border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin-bottom:28px;}
  .lesson-objectives h2{font-size:14px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;text-transform:uppercase!important;letter-spacing:.06em!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .lesson-objectives ul{list-style:none;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-objectives li{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#1e3a8a;line-height:1.5;}
  .lesson-objectives li::before{content:"\2713";color:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:1px;}
  .score-impact{background:#f0fdf4;border:1px solid #bbf7d0;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 18px;margin-bottom:28px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#14532d;}
  .score-impact strong{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}

  /* HOOK */
  .hook-box{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:32px;}
  .hook-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .hook-box p{font-size:15px!important;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:0!important;}

  /* LESSON SECTIONS */
  .lesson-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .lesson-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .lesson-section h3{font-size:17px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-top:24px!important;margin-bottom:10px!important;}
  .lesson-section p{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section ul,.lesson-section ol{padding-left:20px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section li{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .lesson-section code{background:#eef2ff;color:#1e3a8a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e3a8a!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}

  /* DUAL CODE PANEL */
  .code-panel-wrap{margin:20px 0;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;}
  .code-panel-tabs{display:flex;background:#1e293b;}
  .code-tab{padding:8px 16px;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;border:none;background:transparent;letter-spacing:.04em;transition:background .15s;font-family:inherit;}
  .code-tab.py{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.pseudo{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.active{background:rgba(255,255,255,.15)!important;}
  .code-tab-label{font-size:10px;opacity:.6;margin-left:4px;font-weight:400;}
  .code-pane{background:#0f172a;padding:18px 20px;overflow-x:auto;height:0;overflow:hidden;padding:0;}
  .code-pane.active{height:auto;overflow-x:auto;padding:18px 20px;}
  .code-pane pre{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:0;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;max-width:100%;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-kw{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .py-fn{color:#6ee7b7!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#6ee7b7!important;}
  .py-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .py-str{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .py-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .py-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-op{color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;}
  .ps-kw{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .ps-op{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .ps-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .ps-str{color:#86efac!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#86efac!important;}
  .ps-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .ps-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* CALLOUTS */
  .callout-exam{background:#fffbeb;border:1px solid #fcd34d;border-left:4px solid var(--amber);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-exam-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--amber)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--amber)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-exam p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}
  .callout-trap{background:#fef2f2;border:1px solid #fca5a5;border-left:4px solid var(--red);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-opt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;padding:10px 14px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;font-family:monospace;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;background:#f8fafc;text-align:left;width:100%;transition:border-color .15s;}
  .mini-opt:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mini-opt.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}

</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>Almost every program does math. A game adds up a score, a store applies a tax, a clock wraps from 59 minutes back to 0. All of that is built from a handful of arithmetic operators and one special operator, MOD, that hands you the remainder after a division. This lesson is about writing expressions that evaluate to exactly the value you intend, and knowing whether that value comes out as a whole number or a decimal.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Expressions and the Arithmetic Operators</h2>
      <p>An <strong>expression</strong> is any piece of code that the computer <strong>evaluates to a single value</strong>. The value <code>5</code> is an expression, the variable <code>x</code> is an expression, and <code>3 * x + 1</code> is an expression too. When a program runs, it replaces the whole expression with the one value it produces, and an algorithm can then store that value, display it, or test it. This is the idea the CED calls out: expressions evaluate to a value, and algorithms are built out of them.</p>
      <p>AP Computer Science Principles uses five arithmetic operators. Four are the ones you already know: <code>+</code> for addition, <code>-</code> for subtraction, <code>*</code> for multiplication, and <code>/</code> for division. The fifth is <strong>MOD</strong>, which gives the remainder after division. In Python the MOD operator is written <code>%</code>, but the AP exam reference sheet writes it as the word <code>MOD</code>. They mean exactly the same thing.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-1')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-1')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-1-py"><pre><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">7</span>
<span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">2</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">-</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">a</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">b</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-1-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">7</span>
<span class="ps-var">b</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">b</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">b</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">a</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">*</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">b</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Notice that each operator combines two values and produces one new value. Because an expression is always worth a single value, you can nest expressions inside larger expressions: the result of <code>a + b</code> can itself be multiplied, compared, or stored. That composability is what lets a short line of math do real work inside an algorithm.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam expects</div>
        <p>On the AP CSP exam, arithmetic appears in pseudocode using <code>+</code>, <code>-</code>, <code>*</code>, <code>/</code>, and <code>MOD</code>. The reference sheet states that <code>a MOD b</code> evaluates to the remainder when <code>a</code> is divided by <code>b</code>, and that the result has the same behavior as Python <code>%</code> for the non-negative values you will see. Read <code>MOD</code> as "remainder" and you will not be surprised.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Order of Operations</h2>
      <p>When an expression mixes operators, the computer does not simply work left to right. It follows a fixed <strong>order of operations</strong>, the same precedence you learned in math class:</p>
      <ol>
        <li>
<strong>Parentheses</strong> first: anything inside <code>( )</code> is evaluated before it is used.</li>
        <li>Then <strong>multiplication, division, and MOD</strong> (<code>*</code>, <code>/</code>, <code>%</code>), left to right.</li>
        <li>Then <strong>addition and subtraction</strong> (<code>+</code>, <code>-</code>), left to right.</li>
      </ol>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-3')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-3')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-3-py"><pre><span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">3</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">4</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">+</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">3</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">*</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">4</span><span class="py-var">)</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">20</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">-</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">6</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">/</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var">)</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-3-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">3</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">*</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">4</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">+</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">3</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">*</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">4</span><span class="ps-var">)</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">20</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">6</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">/</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var">)</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>The first line prints <code>14</code> because <code>3 * 4</code> is done before the <code>+</code>. The second line prints <code>20</code> because the parentheses force <code>2 + 3</code> first. The third line prints <code>17.0</code> because <code>6 / 2</code> runs before the subtraction. If you ever want a different order, add parentheses, they are the one tool that always overrides precedence.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ The parentheses trap</div>
        <p>The most common expression bug is a missing pair of parentheses. To average <code>a</code> and <code>b</code> you must write <code>(a + b) / 2</code>. Writing <code>a + b / 2</code> divides only <code>b</code> by 2 and then adds <code>a</code>, which is a completely different value. When an average or a percentage comes out wrong, check your parentheses first.</p>
      </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>MOD: the Remainder Operator</h2>
      <p><strong>MOD</strong> (written <code>%</code> in Python) gives the amount left over after a division. For example <code>17 % 5</code> is <code>2</code>, because 5 goes into 17 three times with 2 left over. The result of <code>a % b</code> is always between 0 and <code>b - 1</code> for the non-negative values you will meet on the exam, which is exactly why MOD is so useful for cycling and classifying numbers.</p>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-4')">🐛 Python</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-4')">📋 AP Pseudocode</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-4-py"><pre><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">=</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">47</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">%</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment"># 1  -> n is odd</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-var">n</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">%</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">10</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment"># 7  -> the last digit</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-4-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"><</span><span class="ps-var">-</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">47</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">MOD</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-comment"># 1  -> n is odd</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-var">n</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">MOD</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">10</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-comment"># 7  -> the last digit</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Three patterns come up constantly, and each is worth memorizing:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Even or odd:</strong> <code>n % 2</code> is <code>0</code> when <code>n</code> is even and <code>1</code> when <code>n</code> is odd.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Last digit:</strong> <code>n % 10</code> gives the ones digit of a whole number, for example <code>3947 % 10</code> is <code>7</code>.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Wrapping or cycling:</strong> <code>n % k</code> keeps a value in the range 0 to <code>k - 1</code>, which is how clocks, calendars, and turn counters loop back around.</li>
      </ul>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Division Three Ways: / vs // vs %</h2>
      <p>Division is where Python trips people up, because Python has three different operators and the AP exam cares about the difference between the values they produce.</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<code>/</code> is <strong>float division</strong>. It always produces a decimal (a float), so <code>7 / 2</code> is <code>3.5</code> and even <code>6 / 2</code> is <code>3.0</code>, not <code>3</code>.</li>
        <li>
<code>//</code> is <strong>integer (floor) division</strong>. It divides and then drops the fractional part, so <code>7 // 2</code> is <code>3</code>. This is the AP pseudocode idea of a whole-number quotient.</li>
        <li>
<code>%</code> is <strong>MOD</strong>, the remainder that is left over, so <code>7 % 2</code> is <code>1</code>.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="code-panel-wrap">
  <div class="code-panel-tabs">
    <button class="code-tab py active" onclick="switchTab(this,'py','pan-2')">🐛 Python (/ // %)</button>
    <button class="code-tab pseudo" onclick="switchTab(this,'pseudo','pan-2')">📋 Pseudocode (/ MOD)</button>
  </div>
  <div class="code-pane active" id="pan-2-py"><pre><span class="py-comment"># three ways to "divide" in Python</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">7</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">/</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment"># float division  -> 3.5</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">7</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment">// 2)   # integer division -> 3</span>
<span class="py-kw">print</span><span class="py-var">(</span><span class="py-num">7</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var">%</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-num">2</span><span class="py-var">)</span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-var"> </span><span class="py-comment"># remainder (MOD)  -> 1</span></pre></div>
  <div class="code-pane" id="pan-2-pseudo"><pre><span class="ps-comment"># AP pseudocode has two operators</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">7</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var">/</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-comment"># division -> 3.5</span>
<span class="ps-kw">DISPLAY</span><span class="ps-var">(</span><span class="ps-num">7</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-kw">MOD</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-num">2</span><span class="ps-var">)</span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-var"> </span><span class="ps-comment"># remainder -> 1</span></pre></div>
</div>
      <p>Together, <code>//</code> and <code>%</code> split a division into its two parts: <code>7 // 2</code> is how many whole 2s fit (3) and <code>7 % 2</code> is what is left over (1). AP pseudocode writes remainder as <code>MOD</code> and a plain <code>/</code> for division, so when you translate pseudocode to Python you must decide whether the problem wants the decimal answer (<code>/</code>) or the whole-number answer (<code>//</code>).</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 Integer vs float</div>
        <p>A favorite trap: is the result an integer or a float? <code>7 / 2</code> is <code>3.5</code>, but <code>7 // 2</code> is <code>3</code>. When a distractor differs only by <code>3</code> versus <code>3.5</code> versus <code>3.0</code>, the question is testing whether you know which division operator was used. Predict the exact printed form before you look at the choices.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="mini-ex">

    <div class="cpt-connection">
      <div class="cpt-connection-label">📋 Create Performance Task • Mathematical expressions in your program</div>
      <p>The Create Task rubric rewards a program that uses mathematical or logical concepts to process input into output. A well-chosen arithmetic expression, an average, a percentage, a running total, is one of the cleanest ways to show that your code actually computes something rather than just storing values.</p>
      <h3>A point-earning example</h3>
      <p>Imagine a quiz app that turns a number of correct answers into a percentage score:</p>
      <div class="cpt-code">correct <- 17
total <- 20
percent <- (correct / total) * 100
DISPLAY(percent)</div>
      <p>In your written response, name the expression and describe how it transforms the input:</p>
      <ul class="cpt-stems">
        <li>"The expression <code>(correct / total) * 100</code> uses division and multiplication to convert a raw count into a percentage."</li>
        <li>"The parentheses force the division to happen before the multiplication, so the value is computed in the correct order."</li>
        <li>"The single value this expression produces is stored in <code>percent</code> and then displayed, so the program processes input into meaningful output."</li>
      </ul>
      <h3>The trap to avoid</h3>
      <p>Two topic-specific mistakes cost points here. First, dropping the parentheses: <code>correct / total * 100</code> happens to work by left-to-right rule, but <code>correct / (total * 100)</code> would not, so always be deliberate. Second, using integer division when you need a decimal: in Python <code>17 // 20</code> is <code>0</code>, which would make every percentage look like zero. Match the operator to the value you actually want. <a href="/pages/ap-csp-course-create-task">See the full Create Task module →</a></p>

      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is an expression in AP CSP?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">An expression is any code that evaluates to a single value. A number, a variable, and a combination like <code>3 * x + 1</code> are all expressions. When the program runs, the whole expression is replaced by the one value it produces, and an algorithm can then store, display, or test that value.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What does MOD do, and how is it written?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">MOD gives the remainder after division. For example <code>17 MOD 5</code> is 2, because 5 goes into 17 three times with 2 left over. AP pseudocode writes it as the word <code>MOD</code>; in Python the same operation is written with the percent sign, <code>%</code>.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between / and // in Python?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">The single slash <code>/</code> is float division and always gives a decimal, so <code>7 / 2</code> is <code>3.5</code> and <code>6 / 2</code> is <code>3.0</code>. The double slash <code>//</code> is integer division; it divides and drops the fractional part, so <code>7 // 2</code> is <code>3</code>. Choose based on whether you want a decimal or a whole-number answer.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What order does Python evaluate operators in?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Parentheses are evaluated first, then multiplication, division, and MOD from left to right, and finally addition and subtraction from left to right. So <code>2 + 3 * 4</code> is 14, while <code>(2 + 3) * 4</code> is 20. When in doubt, add parentheses to force the order you want.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How do mathematical expressions help my Create Task?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">They let your program process input into output, such as an average, a percentage, or a running total, which is exactly what the rubric rewards. In your written response you name the expression and describe how it transforms the input, and you make sure the operators and parentheses produce the value you intend.</div>
      </div>

function execUser(py,code){var output='',err=null;
  try{py.runPython('import sys, io\n__old_out = sys.stdout\nsys.stdout = io.StringIO()\nsys.stderr = sys.stdout');
    try{var ns=py.globals.get('dict')();py.runPython(code,{globals:ns});ns.destroy();}
    catch(e){err=cleanErr(e.message);}
    output=py.runPython('sys.stdout.getvalue()');}
  catch(e2){err=cleanErr((e2&&e2.message)||String(e2));}
  finally{try{py.runPython('sys.stdout = __old_out\nsys.stderr = __old_out');}catch(e3){}}
  return {output:output,err:err};}

  LESSON_USAGE.hints[n]=shown;LESSON_USAGE.totalHints=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.hints);updateUsage();
  if(CE_HINT_IDX[n]<hints.length-1)CE_HINT_IDX[n]++;
  var solBtn=document.getElementById('sol-btn-'+n);if(solBtn)solBtn.style.display='inline-block';}
function showSol(n){var box=document.getElementById('ce-sol-'+n);box.textContent=CE_SOL[n]||'';box.className='code-solution show';
  LESSON_USAGE.solutions[n]=1;LESSON_USAGE.totalSolutions=_sumv(LESSON_USAGE.solutions);updateUsage();}
var vtScore=0,vtQ=0,vtStreak=0,vtAnswered=false;
function vtRender(){if(vtQ>=VT_QS.length){vtShowResults();return;}vtAnswered=false;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  document.getElementById('vt-qn').textContent=(vtQ+1)+'/'+VT_QS.length;
  document.getElementById('vt-streak').textContent=vtStreak;
  var codeEl=document.getElementById('vt-code');codeEl.innerHTML='';
  q.lines.forEach(function(line,i){var span=document.createElement('span');
    span.className='vt-line'+(i===q.hl?' hl':'');span.textContent=line;codeEl.appendChild(span);});
  document.getElementById('vt-question').textContent=q.q;
  var optEl=document.getElementById('vt-options');optEl.innerHTML='';
  q.choices.forEach(function(ch,i){var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='vt-btn';btn.textContent=ch;
    btn.onclick=(function(idx){return function(){vtAnswer(idx);};})(i);optEl.appendChild(btn);});
  document.getElementById('vt-fb').className='vt-fb';document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next';}
function vtAnswer(idx){if(vtAnswered)return;vtAnswered=true;var q=VT_QS[vtQ];
  var btns=document.querySelectorAll('.vt-btn');btns.forEach(function(b){b.onclick=null;});
  var fb=document.getElementById('vt-fb');
  if(idx===q.correct){vtScore++;vtStreak++;btns[idx].classList.add('c');fb.textContent='\u2713 Correct! '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb c';}
  else{vtStreak=0;btns[idx].classList.add('w');btns[q.correct].classList.add('rv');fb.textContent='\u2717 Not quite. '+q.exp;fb.className='vt-fb w';}
  document.getElementById('vt-score').textContent=vtScore;document.getElementById('vt-streak').textContent=vtStreak;
  document.getElementById('vt-next').className='vt-next show';}
function vtNext(){vtQ++;vtRender();}
function vtShowResults(){document.getElementById('vt-active').style.display='none';
  document.getElementById('vt-results').className='vt-results show';
  document.getElementById('vt-res-score').textContent=vtScore+'/'+VT_QS.length;
  document.getElementById('vt-res-msg').textContent=VT_MSGS[Math.min(vtScore,VT_MSGS.length-1)];
  _activity({activity:'exercise-2',earned:vtScore,possible:VT_QS.length});}
function vtRestart(){vtScore=0;vtQ=0;vtStreak=0;vtAnswered=false;
  document.getElementById('vt-results').className='vt-results';
  document.getElementById('vt-active').style.display='block';
  document.getElementById('vt-score').textContent='0';vtRender();}
vtRender();
