    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>A video export takes your laptop 60 seconds using one processor core. You switch on all 3 cores and it finishes in 20 seconds, a speedup of 3. Excited, you imagine 100 cores finishing it in well under a second, but the real result barely dips below 15 seconds no matter how many cores you add. Why does throwing more processors at the job stop helping?</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Three Ways to Organize the Work</h2>
      <p>The exam draws a sharp line between three models of computing, and the difference is entirely about <strong>how the work is organized</strong>, not about how fast the hardware is.</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Sequential computing</strong> runs steps one after another, one at a time. Step two does not start until step one finishes.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Parallel computing</strong> breaks a single task into parts that run <strong>at the same time</strong> on multiple processors, then combines the partial results into one answer.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Distributed computing</strong> uses <strong>multiple computers or devices connected by a network</strong> to work on one problem together, which lets you tackle problems too large or too slow for any single machine.</li>
      </ul>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Model</th>
<th>How work is organized</th>
<th>Key idea</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Sequential</strong></td>
<td>One step at a time on one processor</td>
<td>Order matters; nothing overlaps.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Parallel</strong></td>
<td>Parts run simultaneously on several processors, then results are combined</td>
<td>Same machine, multiple processors, faster on a divisible task.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Distributed</strong></td>
<td>Many separate computers cooperate over a network</td>
<td>Scales to problems too big for one machine.</td>
</tr>
      </table>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>Read the stem for the words <strong>multiple processors</strong> (parallel) versus <strong>multiple computers</strong> or <strong>over a network</strong> (distributed). Parallel and distributed both do work at once, but distributed spreads it across separate networked machines. Sequential is the one with <strong>no overlap at all</strong>.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Speedup: Measuring the Payoff</h2>
      <p>Parallel computing is only worth it if it actually saves time, and the exam measures that with <strong>speedup</strong>. The formula is short and you must know it:</p>
      <p><code>speedup = (time to complete sequentially) / (time to complete in parallel)</code></p>
      <p>If a job takes 60 seconds run sequentially and 20 seconds run in parallel, then <code>speedup = 60 / 20 = 3</code>. A speedup of 3 means the parallel solution finished 3 times as fast. Speedup is a ratio, so it has no units; a speedup of 1 would mean parallelizing gained you nothing.</p>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A task takes 90 seconds when run sequentially and 30 seconds when run in parallel. What is the speedup?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-parallel-1-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-parallel-1','A','B','mc-parallel-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> 2</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-parallel-1','B','B','mc-parallel-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> 3</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-parallel-1','C','B','mc-parallel-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> 60</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-parallel-1','D','B','mc-parallel-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> 120</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-parallel-1-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Estimating Parallel Run Time</h2>
      <p>Most real tasks have a part that <strong>must</strong> run sequentially and a part that <strong>can</strong> be split across processors. A useful model for the exam:</p>
      <p><code>parallel time = (sequential part) + (parallelizable part / number of processors)</code></p>
      <p>Suppose a task takes 100 seconds total, of which 20 seconds must run sequentially and the other 80 seconds can be divided evenly. With 4 processors:</p>
      <pre>parallel time = 20 + (80 / 4)
             = 20 + 20
             = 40 seconds</pre>
      <p>Now push it: with 8 processors the parallel part becomes <code>80 / 8 = 10</code>, so the total is <code>20 + 10 = 30</code> seconds. Doubling the processors from 4 to 8 did <strong>not</strong> cut the time in half; it went from 40 to 30, because the 20 second sequential part cannot be sped up at all.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Why Adding Processors Stops Helping</h2>
      <p>Speedup has a ceiling. Two forces cap it:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>The <strong>sequential portion</strong> of a task cannot be parallelized. Even with infinite processors, the parallelizable part shrinks toward zero but the sequential part stays fixed, so the total time cannot fall below that sequential floor.</li>
        <li>Splitting the work and combining the partial results adds <strong>overhead</strong>. At some point the cost of coordinating one more processor outweighs the tiny time it saves.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>That is why each extra processor helps less than the one before it, a pattern called <strong>diminishing returns</strong>. In the run time example, 20 seconds is the hard floor: no number of processors gets the job below 20 seconds.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>Doubling the number of processors does <strong>not</strong> halve the total time when part of the task is sequential. Only the parallelizable portion is divided by the processor count; the sequential portion and the coordination overhead are unchanged. Any answer that assumes "twice the processors means half the time" for a mixed task is a distractor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A team keeps adding processors to a task, but the run time barely improves past a certain point. Which explanation best fits what the framework says about parallel computing?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-parallel-2-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-parallel-2','A','C','mc-parallel-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> Parallel computing always makes a task exactly N times faster with N processors</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-parallel-2','B','C','mc-parallel-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> Distributed computing is being used instead of parallel computing</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-parallel-2','C','C','mc-parallel-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> A portion of the task must run sequentially and there is overhead, so speedup is capped</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-parallel-2','D','C','mc-parallel-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> The processors are running the steps in the wrong order</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-parallel-2-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>When Distributed Computing Wins</h2>
      <p>Some problems are simply too large for one machine, whether because of the amount of data, the memory needed, or the sheer volume of computation. <strong>Distributed computing</strong> connects many computers over a network so they can each handle a slice of the problem. Searching for signals in astronomy data, training on enormous datasets, and running a web service for millions of users all rely on distributed systems. The trade off is the same limit in a new form: coordinating separate machines across a network adds communication overhead, and any part that cannot be divided still gates the whole job.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How 4.3 Is Tested on the Multiple-Choice Exam</h2>
      <p>Topic 4.3 shows up on the MCQ section in a few very consistent shapes, so knowing them is worth several fast points.</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Compute a speedup.</strong> You are given a sequential time and a parallel time and asked for the speedup. Use <code>speedup = sequential time / parallel time</code>. Given 60 seconds sequential and 20 seconds parallel, the speedup is <code>60 / 20 = 3</code>.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Compute a parallel run time.</strong> You are given a sequential portion, a parallelizable portion, and a processor count. Use <code>parallel time = sequential part + (parallelizable part / processors)</code>. Only the parallelizable part is divided by the processor count.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Explain the limit.</strong> You are asked why adding processors stops helping. The credited reason is that a portion of the task must run sequentially and there is overhead to split and recombine work, so speedup is capped and extra processors give diminishing returns.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Classify the model.</strong> You are asked whether a scenario is sequential, parallel, or distributed. Watch for <strong>multiple processors</strong> on one machine (parallel) versus <strong>multiple networked computers</strong> (distributed).</li>
      </ul>
      <p>The most common wrong answer treats a task as fully parallelizable, assuming N processors always give an N times speedup or that doubling processors always halves time. Whenever a stem names a sequential portion, that portion is a floor the total time cannot drop below.</p>

<div id="q6-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Going 3 to 4 gives 10 + 90/4 = 32.5 seconds, an improvement but smaller than doubling to 6.</div>

<div class="ps-game" id="ps-game">

<script>
(function(){
  var ROUNDS = [
    { tasks:3, procs:2, min:2, max:8 },
    { tasks:4, procs:2, min:2, max:9 },
    { tasks:5, procs:3, min:1, max:8 },
    { tasks:6, procs:3, min:1, max:9 },
    { tasks:7, procs:4, min:1, max:9 }
  ];
  var PERROUND = 1000;

  var state = null;
  var totalScore = 0;
  var roundIdx = 0;
  var selected = null; // task id currently selected

  var $ = function(id){ return document.getElementById(id); };
  var tray = $('ps-tray'), procsEl = $('ps-procs');

  function randInt(a,b){ return a + Math.floor(Math.random()*(b-a+1)); }

  // Optimal makespan via branch-and-bound assignment (small sizes only).
  function optimalMakespan(durs, P){
    var sorted = durs.slice().sort(function(a,b){ return b-a; });
    var loads = new Array(P).fill(0);
    var best = { v: sorted.reduce(function(a,b){return a+b;},0) }; // sequential upper bound
    function rec(i, curMax){
      if(curMax >= best.v) return;
      if(i === sorted.length){ best.v = curMax; return; }
      var seen = {};
      for(var p=0;p<P;p++){
        var key = loads[p];
        if(seen[key]) continue; // symmetry: identical loads are equivalent
        seen[key] = true;
        loads[p] += sorted[i];
        rec(i+1, Math.max(curMax, loads[p]));
        loads[p] -= sorted[i];
        if(loads[p] === 0) break; // placing on the first empty proc covers the rest
      }
    }
    rec(0, 0);
    return best.v;
  }

  function buildRound(i){
    var cfg = ROUNDS[i];
    var durs = [];
    for(var t=0;t<cfg.tasks;t++) durs.push(randInt(cfg.min, cfg.max));
    var opt = optimalMakespan(durs, cfg.procs);
    var seq = durs.reduce(function(a,b){ return a+b; }, 0);
    state = {
      cfg: cfg,
      tasks: durs.map(function(d,idx){ return { id: idx, dur: d, proc: -1 }; }),
      opt: opt,
      seq: seq,
      done: false
    };
    selected = null;
    renderRound();
  }

  function armedProc(){ return selected !== null; }

  function renderRound(){
    $('ps-round').textContent = (roundIdx+1) + ' / 5';
    $('ps-target').textContent = state.opt + 's';
    $('ps-score').textContent = totalScore;

    // tray
    tray.innerHTML = '';
    var anyTray = false;
    state.tasks.forEach(function(tk){
      if(tk.proc !== -1) return;
      anyTray = true;
      tray.appendChild(taskChip(tk, false));
    });
    tray.classList.toggle('empty', !anyTray);

    // processors
    procsEl.innerHTML = '';
    var P = state.cfg.procs;
    procsEl.style.gridTemplateColumns = 'repeat(' + (P >= 3 ? 2 : P) + ',1fr)';
    var loads = procLoads();
    var make = Math.max.apply(null, loads.concat([0]));
    var scale = Math.max(state.seq, 1);

    for(var p=0;p<P;p++){
      (function(p){
        var box = document.createElement('div');
        box.className = 'ps-proc' + (armedProc() ? ' arm' : '') + ((make>0 && loads[p]===make) ? ' slowp' : '');
        var slow = (make>0 && loads[p]===make);
        box.innerHTML =
          '<div class="ph"><span class="pn">Processor ' + (p+1) + '</span>' +
          '<span class="pt' + (slow?' slow':'') + '">' + loads[p] + 's</span></div>' +
          '<div class="ps-bar"><i style="width:' + Math.round(loads[p]/scale*100) + '%"></i></div>';
        var slot = document.createElement('div');
        slot.className = 'ps-slot';
        var got = false;
        state.tasks.forEach(function(tk){
          if(tk.proc === p){ got = true; slot.appendChild(taskChip(tk, true)); }
        });
        if(!got){ var h=document.createElement('span'); h.className='hint'; h.textContent = selected!==null ? 'Tap to place here' : 'Empty'; slot.appendChild(h); }
        box.appendChild(slot);
        box.onclick = function(e){
          if(e.target.closest('.ps-task')) return; // chip handles its own click
          if(selected !== null){ assign(selected, p); }
        };
        procsEl.appendChild(box);
      })(p);
    }

    // stats
    var speed = make>0 ? (state.seq/make) : 1;
    $('ps-seq').textContent = state.seq + 's';
    $('ps-make').textContent = (make>0 ? make : 0) + 's';
    $('ps-speed').textContent = speed.toFixed(1) + 'x';

    // run button enabled only when all assigned
    $('ps-run').disabled = anyTray || state.done;
  }

  function taskChip(tk, mini){
    var c = document.createElement('div');
    c.className = 'ps-task' + (mini?' mini':'') + (selected===tk.id ? ' sel' : '');
    c.innerHTML = '<span class="dur">' + tk.dur + 's</span><span class="lbl">job ' + (tk.id+1) + '</span>';
    c.onclick = function(ev){
      ev.stopPropagation();
      if(state.done) return;
      if(tk.proc !== -1){ // assigned chip -> return to tray
        tk.proc = -1; selected = tk.id; hideFb(); renderRound(); return;
      }
      selected = (selected === tk.id) ? null : tk.id;
      renderRound();
    };
    return c;
  }

  function assign(taskId, p){
    var tk = state.tasks[taskId];
    if(!tk || state.done) return;
    tk.proc = p;
    selected = null;
    hideFb();
    renderRound();
  }

  function procLoads(){
    var P = state.cfg.procs;
    var loads = new Array(P).fill(0);
    state.tasks.forEach(function(tk){ if(tk.proc>=0) loads[tk.proc]+=tk.dur; });
    return loads;
  }

  function hideFb(){ $('ps-fb').classList.remove('show'); }

  function longestTask(){
    return state.tasks.reduce(function(m,t){ return Math.max(m,t.dur); }, 0);
  }

  function runSchedule(){
    if(state.done) return;
    var loads = procLoads();
    var make = Math.max.apply(null, loads.concat([0]));
    var opt = state.opt;
    state.done = true;

    // score: reward closeness to optimal
    var ratio = opt / make; // <= 1
    var pts = Math.round(PERROUND * ratio);
    var perfect = (make === opt);
    if(perfect) pts += 200;
    totalScore += pts;
    $('ps-score').textContent = totalScore;

    var fb = $('ps-fb');
    var longest = longestTask();
    var speed = (state.seq/make).toFixed(2);
    var msg, cls;
    if(perfect){
      cls = 'good';
      msg = '<span class="fbt">🏆 Optimal schedule!</span>' +
        'Finish time <b>' + make + 's</b> matches the best possible. Sequential time was <b>' + state.seq + 's</b>, so you hit a <b>' + speed + 'x</b> speedup. ' +
        'Notice the finish can never drop below the single longest job (<b>' + longest + 's</b>). +' + pts + ' points.';
    } else if(make <= opt + 1){
      cls = 'good';
      msg = '<span class="fbt">✅ Very close!</span>' +
        'You finished in <b>' + make + 's</b>; the optimal was <b>' + opt + 's</b>. Speedup <b>' + speed + 'x</b> vs running all ' + state.seq + 's on one processor. +' + pts + ' points.';
    } else {
      cls = 'ok';
      msg = '<span class="fbt">💡 Unbalanced load</span>' +
        'Your finish was <b>' + make + 's</b> but <b>' + opt + 's</b> was possible. The slowest processor sets the finish time, so move work off it. ' +
        'Remember: parallelism only helps if the load is balanced, and it can never beat the longest single job (<b>' + longest + 's</b>). +' + pts + ' points.';
    }
    fb.className = 'ps-fb show ' + cls;
    fb.innerHTML = msg;

    $('ps-run').disabled = true;
    // morph clear button into next
    var run = $('ps-run');
    run.disabled = false;
    run.textContent = (roundIdx < ROUNDS.length-1) ? 'Next round' : 'See results';
    run.onclick = nextRound;
    renderChipsLocked();
  }

  function renderChipsLocked(){
    // re-render so chips are non-interactive-ish (state.done guards clicks)
    // keep visuals; nothing extra needed
  }

  function nextRound(){
    if(roundIdx < ROUNDS.length-1){
      roundIdx++;
      buildRound(roundIdx);
      var run = $('ps-run');
      run.textContent = 'Run the schedule';
      run.onclick = runSchedule;
      hideFb();
    } else {
      endGame();
    }
  }

  function endGame(){
    $('ps-play').classList.add('ps-hide');
    $('ps-end').classList.add('show');
    var maxScore = ROUNDS.length * (PERROUND + 200);
    $('ps-endscore').textContent = totalScore;
    var pct = totalScore / maxScore;
    var t, m;
    if(pct >= 0.92){ t = 'Scheduling master!'; }
    else if(pct >= 0.75){ t = 'Strong scheduler'; }
    else { t = 'Good effort'; }
    $('ps-endt').textContent = t;
    m = 'You balanced load across processors to shrink the finish time (the makespan). ' +
        'Key idea: parallel computing speeds work up only when the load is shared evenly, the finish time can never be shorter than the longest single task, and each extra processor helps less than the last. That is why real speedup has limits.';
    $('ps-endm').textContent = m;

    // fire final score for the leaderboard
    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsGameScore', { detail:{ value: totalScore } }));
  }

  function resetRound(){
    if(state.done) return;
    state.tasks.forEach(function(tk){ tk.proc = -1; });
    selected = null;
    hideFb();
    renderRound();
  }

  function playAgain(){
    totalScore = 0; roundIdx = 0;
    $('ps-play').classList.remove('ps-hide');
    $('ps-end').classList.remove('show');
    var run = $('ps-run');
    run.textContent = 'Run the schedule';
    run.onclick = runSchedule;
    buildRound(0);
  }

  $('ps-run').onclick = runSchedule;
  $('ps-clear').onclick = resetRound;
  $('ps-again').onclick = playAgain;

  buildRound(0);
})();
</script>

    <div class="faq-section">
      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between parallel and distributed computing?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Parallel computing splits one task across multiple processors, usually inside a single computer, so parts run at the same time and the results are combined. Distributed computing spreads the work across multiple separate computers connected by a network. Both do work simultaneously, but distributed uses many machines, which lets it handle problems too large for one.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How do I calculate speedup?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Divide the time to complete the task sequentially by the time to complete it in parallel: speedup = sequential time / parallel time. For example, 60 seconds sequential and 20 seconds parallel gives a speedup of 60 / 20 = 3, meaning the parallel version finished 3 times as fast.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How do I estimate the run time on several processors?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Split the task into the part that must run sequentially and the part that can be divided. Then parallel time = sequential part + (parallelizable part / number of processors). Only the parallelizable part is divided by the processor count; the sequential part stays the same.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why does adding more processors eventually stop helping?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Because part of the task must run sequentially and cannot be sped up, and splitting and recombining the work adds overhead. The sequential portion acts as a floor the total time cannot drop below, so each extra processor helps less than the last. This is called diminishing returns.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Does doubling the number of processors halve the run time?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Not for a realistic task. Only the parallelizable portion is divided by the processor count, so doubling processors halves just that portion, not the sequential part or the overhead. If a task has a sequential part, doubling processors always reduces the time by less than half.</div>
      </div>

  .mini-opt:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:var(--bi3-bg);}

  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .game-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .vt-stat{text-align:center;}
  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .vt-line{display:block;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;white-space:pre;}
  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .vt-question{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-options{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:8px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .vt-btn{padding:12px;border-radius:9px;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.15);background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);cursor:pointer;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;font-family:monospace;transition:all .15s;}
  .vt-btn:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:rgba(26,86,219,.2);}
  .vt-btn.c{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.15);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;}
  .vt-btn.w{border-color:#f87171;background:rgba(248,113,113,.15);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .vt-btn.rv{border-color:#4ade80;background:rgba(74,222,128,.08);}
  .vt-fb{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;margin-bottom:12px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .vt-fb.c{background:rgba(74,222,128,.1);color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;display:block;}
  .vt-fb.w{background:rgba(248,113,113,.1);color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;display:block;}
  .vt-next{display:none;width:100%;padding:12px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .vt-next.show{display:block;}
  .vt-results{display:none;text-align:center;padding:20px;}
  .vt-results.show{display:block;}
  .vt-res-score{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:52px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-res-lbl{font-size:14px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .vt-res-msg{font-size:14px;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;margin-bottom:20px;line-height:1.6;}
  .vt-restart{background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);border-radius:8px;padding:11px 24px;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}

  /* CODE EDITOR (Pyodide live) */
  .code-editor-section{background:#0f172a;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .code-editor-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .code-editor-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:22px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .code-editor-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .code-problem{background:rgba(255,255,255,.04);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08);border-radius:10px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .scaffold-badge{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:3px 10px;border-radius:100px;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .code-problem-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .code-problem-prompt{font-size:14px!important;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}

  .code-textarea{width:100%;min-height:120px;background:#020617;border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#e2e8f0!important;resize:vertical;outline:none;line-height:1.8;}
  .code-textarea:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .code-btn-row{display:flex;gap:8px;margin-top:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;}
  .code-run-btn{padding:9px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:7px!important;font-size:13px!important;font-weight:700!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .code-run-btn:disabled{opacity:.6;cursor:wait;}
  .code-hint-btn,.code-sol-btn{padding:9px 16px!important;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06)!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.12)!important;border-radius:7px!important;font-size:13px!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .code-output{margin-top:10px;background:#020617;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;min-height:44px;display:none;line-height:1.7;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  .code-output.ok{color:#4ade80!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#4ade80!important;}
  .code-output.err{color:#f87171!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f87171!important;}
  .code-hint{margin-top:8px;background:rgba(147,197,253,.06);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.2);border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;display:none;line-height:1.6;}

  .code-solution{margin-top:8px;background:rgba(74,222,128,.06);border:1px solid rgba(74,222,128,.2);border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#bbf7d0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bbf7d0!important;display:none;white-space:pre;line-height:1.8;overflow-x:auto;}
  .code-solution.show{display:block;}

  /* FAQ */
  .faq-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .faq-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .faq-item{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:10px;margin-bottom:10px;overflow:hidden;}
  .faq-q{width:100%;text-align:left;padding:16px 20px;background:none;border:none;cursor:pointer;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;font-family:inherit!important;line-height:1.4!important;}
  .faq-q:hover{background:#f8fafc;}
  .faq-icon{font-size:18px;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0;transition:transform .2s;font-style:normal;}

  .faq-a{display:none;padding:0 20px 16px;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.7!important;border-top:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .faq-item.open .faq-a{display:block;}
  .faq-a code{background:#eef2ff;color:#1e3a8a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e3a8a!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}

  /* RELATED + SUPERPACK + TEACHER + NAV */
  .related-links{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:12px;padding:24px;margin-bottom:40px;}

      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Distinguish a computing device, a computer network, the Internet, and the World Wide Web</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain what a protocol is and describe the roles of IP, TCP, UDP, and HTTP/HTTPS</span></li>
        <li><span>Trace how data is split into packets that are routed independently, may take different paths, arrive out of order, and are reassembled</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain how IP addresses uniquely identify devices and why the addressing system must scale (IPv4 versus IPv6)</span></li>
        <li><span>Distinguish bandwidth (a data rate) from latency, and connect redundancy to a scalable, fault-tolerant network</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span>Big Idea 4 (Computing Systems and Networks) is 11 to 15 percent of the AP CSP exam, and 4.1 supplies the vocabulary the whole unit is built on. Protocols, packets, IP addresses, and bandwidth show up as fast, factual multiple-choice points, and the trap questions (Internet versus Web, bandwidth versus latency) are easy to get right once you have seen them named.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>You click a link and a photo from a server thousands of miles away appears on your screen in under a second. That photo did not travel as one piece down one wire. It was chopped into hundreds of numbered pieces that scattered across different paths through a global web of networks, some arriving out of order, and your device stitched them back together perfectly. How does a system with no central controller pull that off every single time?</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Devices, Networks, the Internet, and the Web</h2>
      <p>These four words get used loosely in everyday speech, but the exam expects you to keep them separate. A <strong>computing device</strong> is a machine that processes and stores data: a laptop, a phone, a server, even a smart thermostat. A <strong>computer network</strong> is two or more computing devices connected so they can <strong>share data</strong>. The <strong>Internet</strong> is a <strong>network of networks</strong>, a global system that connects billions of devices by linking many smaller networks together.</p>
      <p>The <strong>World Wide Web</strong> is not the same thing as the Internet. The Web is a <strong>system of linked pages and resources</strong> (documents, images, videos) that are identified by addresses and accessed <strong>over</strong> the Internet using the HTTP protocol. Think of the Internet as the roads and the Web as one popular kind of traffic that travels on those roads. Email, video calls, and online games also run on the Internet without being part of the Web.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>"The Internet and the World Wide Web are the same thing." They are not. The <strong>Internet</strong> is the underlying network of networks; the <strong>Web</strong> is one service (linked pages and resources) that runs on top of it. If a question treats them as identical, that choice is wrong.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the Internet and the World Wide Web?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-internet-1-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-internet-1','A','C','mc-internet-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> They are two names for exactly the same system</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-internet-1','B','C','mc-internet-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> The Internet is a collection of web pages accessed through the Web</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-internet-1','C','C','mc-internet-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> The Web is a system of linked resources accessed over the Internet, which is a network of networks</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-internet-1','D','C','mc-internet-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> The Web is the physical wiring and the Internet is the software that runs on it</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-internet-1-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Protocols: The Rules That Let Everything Talk</h2>
      <p>A <strong>protocol</strong> is an agreed-upon set of <strong>rules</strong> for how data is formatted and transmitted between devices. Protocols are what make the Internet work across a huge variety of hardware and software: as long as two devices follow the same standardized <strong>open</strong> protocol, they can communicate even if they were built by different companies and run different operating systems. "Open" here means the rules are published and free to use, which is why any manufacturer's device can join the network and <strong>interoperate</strong>.</p>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Protocol</th>
<th>What it does</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td>
<strong>IP</strong> (Internet Protocol)</td>
<td>Handles <strong>addressing and routing</strong>: gives each device an IP address and gets packets from sender toward receiver across networks.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td>
<strong>TCP</strong> (Transmission Control Protocol)</td>
<td>Provides <strong>reliable, ordered delivery</strong>: numbers packets, acknowledges what arrives, and retransmits anything lost, then reassembles them in order.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td>
<strong>UDP</strong> (User Datagram Protocol)</td>
<td>
<strong>Faster but unreliable</strong>: sends packets without acknowledgements or retransmission. Used when speed matters more than perfection, like live video or games.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>HTTP / HTTPS</strong></td>
<td>Rules for requesting and delivering <strong>web pages and resources</strong>. HTTPS is the encrypted, secure version.</td>
</tr>
      </table>
      <p>Notice the division of labor: <strong>IP</strong> gets data to the right place, and <strong>TCP</strong> makes sure it all arrives correctly and in order. They are often mentioned together as TCP/IP because they work as a team.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>When a question asks which protocol guarantees that data arrives <strong>complete and in the correct order</strong>, the answer is <strong>TCP</strong> (it acknowledges and retransmits). When it asks what assigns addresses and <strong>routes</strong> packets, the answer is <strong>IP</strong>. When speed is prioritized over reliability, think <strong>UDP</strong>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A file must arrive complete, with every piece in the correct order, even if some packets are lost along the way. Which protocol is responsible for ensuring that reliable, ordered delivery?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-internet-2-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-internet-2','A','B','mc-internet-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> IP, because it assigns each device an address</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-internet-2','B','B','mc-internet-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> TCP, because it acknowledges and retransmits lost packets and reorders them</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-internet-2','C','B','mc-internet-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> UDP, because it sends packets as fast as possible</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-internet-2','D','B','mc-internet-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> HTTP, because it delivers web pages</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-internet-2-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Packets and Routing</h2>
      <p>Data does not travel across the Internet as one continuous stream. It is broken into small pieces called <strong>packets</strong>. Each packet carries a chunk of the data plus header information, including the destination address and a sequence number. Here is the key idea the exam loves: packets are <strong>routed independently</strong>. Each one may take a <strong>different path</strong> through the network depending on traffic and available links, so they can <strong>arrive out of order</strong> or arrive at slightly different times.</p>
      <p><strong>Routing</strong> is the process of finding a path from the sender to the receiver across the many connected networks. There is no single master computer directing traffic; routers pass packets along hop by hop toward the destination. Because a packet can be sent along whatever path is currently open, the network keeps working even when one route is busy or broken.</p>
      <p>At the destination, the packets are <strong>reassembled</strong> into the original data. TCP uses the sequence numbers to put everything back in the right order and requests a resend for any packet that never arrived. This is why you can watch a video that arrived in scrambled pieces and never notice.</p>
      <ul>
        <li>Data is split into <strong>packets</strong> before it is sent.</li>
        <li>Packets are <strong>routed independently</strong> and may follow <strong>different paths</strong>.</li>
        <li>They can <strong>arrive out of order</strong>; the destination <strong>reassembles</strong> them using sequence numbers.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>"All packets in a message follow the same route and always arrive in the order they were sent." False. Packets are routed <strong>independently</strong>, can take <strong>different paths</strong>, and may arrive <strong>out of order</strong>. Reassembly into the correct order happens at the destination, not automatically during transmission.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>IP Addresses and Scaling</h2>
      <p>Every device on the Internet needs a unique identifier so packets can find it. That identifier is an <strong>IP address</strong>. Just as a postal address lets mail reach one specific house, an IP address lets packets reach one specific device.</p>
      <p>The addressing system has to <strong>scale</strong> as more and more devices come online. The older standard, <strong>IPv4</strong>, uses 32-bit addresses, which allows only about <strong>4.3 billion</strong> unique addresses. With billions of phones, computers, and smart devices, that supply ran short. The newer standard, <strong>IPv6</strong>, uses 128-bit addresses, providing a vastly larger pool, effectively enough for every device imaginable. This is a direct example of designing a system to <strong>scale</strong>: expanding the address space so the Internet can keep growing.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Bandwidth, Redundancy, and Scale</h2>
      <p><strong>Bandwidth</strong> is the <strong>maximum amount of data that can be sent per unit of time</strong>, a <strong>rate</strong> usually measured in bits per second (bps). Higher bandwidth means more data moves through the connection each second, like a wider pipe carrying more water. Bandwidth is <strong>not</strong> the time it takes a single bit to travel from one point to another; that delay is called <strong>latency</strong>. A connection can have high bandwidth and still have noticeable latency, and vice versa.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>"Bandwidth is how fast a single bit gets from one place to another." No. That is <strong>latency</strong> (delay). <strong>Bandwidth</strong> is a <strong>rate</strong>: the maximum data per unit time. If an answer defines bandwidth as the travel time of one bit or one message, it is describing latency and is wrong.</p>
      </div>
      <p>Finally, the Internet was deliberately designed to be <strong>scalable</strong> (able to grow to more devices and more traffic) and <strong>redundant</strong> (offering <strong>multiple paths</strong> between points). Redundancy is why the network is <strong>fault tolerant</strong>: if one link or router fails, packets are simply routed along another available path and communication continues. That fault-tolerance idea is explored further in lesson 4.2.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-visual">
      <p class="lv-kicker">💡 See it in action</p>
    <div class="wgt" role="group" aria-label="Interactive packet routing and reassembly demo">
      <div class="wgt-h">Packets: Split, Scramble, Reassemble</div>
      <div class="wgt-sub">A message is split into numbered packets that travel separately and arrive out of order.</div>
      <div class="pkt-track" id="pktTrack"></div>
      <div class="pkt-msg" id="pktMsg" aria-live="polite"></div>
      <div class="wgt-note" id="pktNote">Packets arrived out of order. Reassemble puts them back by sequence number.</div>
      <div class="wgt-btns">
<button class="wgt-btn" id="pktShuffle" type="button">Scramble</button><button class="wgt-btn" id="pktDrop" type="button">Drop one</button><button class="wgt-btn" id="pktSort" type="button">Reassemble</button>
</div>
    </div>
    <script>(function(){
      var MSG='NETWORK',base=[];for(var i=0;i<MSG.length;i++)base.push({seq:i+1,ch:MSG[i],lost:false});
      var order=base.slice(),track=document.getElementById('pktTrack'),msg=document.getElementById('pktMsg'),note=document.getElementById('pktNote');
      function shuffle(a){for(var i=a.length-1;i>0;i--){var j=(i*3+2)%(i+1);var t=a[i];a[i]=a[j];a[j]=t;}return a;}
      function paint(){track.innerHTML='';order.forEach(function(p){var d=document.createElement('div');d.className='pkt'+(p.lost?' lost':'');d.innerHTML='<div class="seq">#'+p.seq+'</div><div class="ch">'+(p.lost?'?':p.ch)+'</div>';track.appendChild(d);});}
      function doScramble(){order=shuffle(base.slice());base.forEach(function(p){p.lost=false;});msg.textContent='';note.textContent='Packets arrived out of order. Reassemble puts them back by sequence number.';note.className='wgt-note';paint();}
      document.getElementById('pktShuffle').onclick=doScramble;
      document.getElementById('pktDrop').onclick=function(){var live=order.filter(function(p){return !p.lost;});if(live.length){live[(live.length*2)%live.length].lost=true;} msg.textContent='';note.textContent='A packet was dropped in transit. The receiver detects the gap by sequence number and requests a resend.';note.className='wgt-note warn';paint();};
      document.getElementById('pktSort').onclick=function(){order.sort(function(a,b){return a.seq-b.seq;});paint();
        if(order.some(function(p){return p.lost;})){msg.textContent='';note.textContent='Cannot finish: a packet is missing. Reliable delivery would resend it first.';note.className='wgt-note warn';}
        else{msg.textContent=order.map(function(p){return p.ch;}).join('');note.textContent='Reassembled in sequence order. The full message is recovered.';note.className='wgt-note good';}};
      doScramble();
    })();</script>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How 4.1 Is Tested on the Multiple-Choice Exam</h2>
      <p>Topic 4.1 is not a Create Performance Task skill; it is <strong>multiple-choice material</strong>, and the questions reward precise vocabulary rather than programming. Expect fast factual items and a few carefully worded traps. The most common ones are worth memorizing:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Internet versus Web.</strong> Any option that treats the Internet and the World Wide Web as the same thing is wrong. The Web is a system of linked resources accessed <strong>over</strong> the Internet.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Packets and routing.</strong> Remember that packets are routed <strong>independently</strong>, may take <strong>different paths</strong>, can arrive <strong>out of order</strong>, and are <strong>reassembled</strong> at the destination. Distractors often claim a fixed single path or guaranteed arrival order.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Redundancy and scalability.</strong> The Internet uses <strong>multiple paths</strong> (redundancy) so it keeps working when parts fail, and it is designed to <strong>scale</strong> (for example IPv6 expanding the address space).</li>
        <li>
<strong>Bandwidth versus latency.</strong> Bandwidth is a data <strong>rate</strong> (data per unit time), not the travel time of a single bit.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>When you see a protocol question, match the job to the protocol: IP for addressing and routing, TCP for reliable ordered delivery, UDP for fast unreliable delivery, HTTP/HTTPS for the web. Getting these definitions exactly right is where the points are.</p>

<script>
(function(){
  var SVGNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";
  var root = document.getElementById("irs-game");
  var svg = document.getElementById("irs-svg");
  var overlay = document.getElementById("irs-overlay");
  var noteEl = document.getElementById("irs-note");
  var fbEl = document.getElementById("irs-feedback");
  var elLevel = document.getElementById("irs-level");
  var elHops = document.getElementById("irs-hops");
  var elDelivered = document.getElementById("irs-delivered");
  var elScore = document.getElementById("irs-score");

  // ---- Level definitions ----
  var LEVELS = [
    {
      name:"First Hop",
      note:"Your <b>packet</b> travels one hop at a time. Tap a router that shares a link with your current position, all the way to the Server.",
      nodes:[
        {id:"S",x:70,y:200,label:"You",type:"source"},
        {id:"A",x:235,y:110,label:"R1"},
        {id:"B",x:235,y:290,label:"R2"},
        {id:"M",x:410,y:200,label:"R3"},
        {id:"D",x:560,y:200,label:"Server",type:"dest"}
      ],
      edges:[["S","A"],["S","B"],["A","M"],["B","M"],["A","B"],["M","D"]],
      brokenNodes:[],brokenEdges:[]
    },
    {
      name:"Route Around a Dead Link",
      note:"A <b>link is down</b> (red dashes). The Internet does not rely on one path  -  find a redundant route to the Server.",
      nodes:[
        {id:"S",x:70,y:200,label:"You",type:"source"},
        {id:"A",x:235,y:110,label:"R1"},
        {id:"B",x:235,y:290,label:"R2"},
        {id:"M",x:410,y:200,label:"R3"},
        {id:"D",x:560,y:200,label:"Server",type:"dest"}
      ],
      edges:[["S","A"],["S","B"],["A","M"],["B","M"],["A","B"],["M","D"]],
      brokenNodes:[],brokenEdges:[["A","M"]]
    },
    {
      name:"The Longer Way Round",
      note:"A whole <b>router has failed</b>. The short path is gone  -  the only working route is longer, but the packet still gets there.",
      nodes:[
        {id:"S",x:70,y:200,label:"You",type:"source"},
        {id:"A",x:300,y:95,label:"R1"},
        {id:"B",x:225,y:300,label:"R2"},
        {id:"C",x:415,y:300,label:"R3"},
        {id:"D",x:560,y:200,label:"Server",type:"dest"}
      ],
      edges:[["S","A"],["A","D"],["S","B"],["B","C"],["C","D"],["A","B"]],
      brokenNodes:["A"],brokenEdges:[]
    },
    {
      name:"Network Storm",
      note:"<b>Two failures at once.</b> Trace a surviving path through the mesh  -  redundancy means many routers can carry the packet.",
      nodes:[
        {id:"S",x:60,y:200,label:"You",type:"source"},
        {id:"A",x:195,y:95,label:"R1"},
        {id:"B",x:195,y:305,label:"R2"},
        {id:"C",x:345,y:95,label:"R3"},
        {id:"E",x:345,y:305,label:"R4"},
        {id:"F",x:470,y:200,label:"R5"},
        {id:"D",x:575,y:200,label:"Server",type:"dest"}
      ],
      edges:[["S","A"],["S","B"],["A","B"],["A","C"],["A","E"],["B","E"],["C","E"],["C","F"],["E","F"],["F","D"]],
      brokenNodes:["C","B"],brokenEdges:[]
    },
    {
      name:"Single Point of Failure",
      note:"This network has <b>no redundancy</b>: the Server sits behind one gateway. That gateway is down. Try to route  -  then see what a real outage looks like.",
      nodes:[
        {id:"S",x:70,y:200,label:"You",type:"source"},
        {id:"A",x:235,y:110,label:"R1"},
        {id:"B",x:235,y:290,label:"R2"},
        {id:"G",x:410,y:200,label:"GW"},
        {id:"D",x:560,y:200,label:"Server",type:"dest"}
      ],
      edges:[["S","A"],["S","B"],["A","B"],["A","G"],["B","G"],["G","D"]],
      brokenNodes:["G"],brokenEdges:[],
      unreachable:true
    }
  ];

  // ---- State ----
  var levelIdx = 0;
  var nodes = [], edges = [];
  var brokenNodes = {}, brokenEdges = {};
  var source = null, dest = null, current = null;
  var hops = 0, delivered = 0, score = 0;
  var optimal = null;
  var animating = false;
  var breakMode = false;
  var levelDone = false;
  var packet = null;

  function keyOf(a,b){ return a<b ? a+"|"+b : b+"|"+a; }
  function nodeById(id){ for(var i=0;i<nodes.length;i++){ if(nodes[i].id===id) return nodes[i]; } return null; }

  function neighbors(id){
    if(brokenNodes[id]) return [];
    var res=[];
    for(var i=0;i<edges.length;i++){
      var a=edges[i][0], b=edges[i][1];
      if(brokenEdges[keyOf(a,b)]) continue;
      if(a===id && !brokenNodes[b]) res.push(b);
      else if(b===id && !brokenNodes[a]) res.push(a);
    }
    return res;
  }

  function shortestPath(src,dst){
    if(brokenNodes[src] || brokenNodes[dst]) return null;
    var q=[src], seen={}, prev={};
    seen[src]=true;
    while(q.length){
      var cur=q.shift();
      if(cur===dst){
        var path=[dst];
        while(path[0]!==src) path.unshift(prev[path[0]]);
        return path;
      }
      var ns=neighbors(cur);
      for(var i=0;i<ns.length;i++){
        var n=ns[i];
        if(!seen[n]){ seen[n]=true; prev[n]=cur; q.push(n); }
      }
    }
    return null;
  }

  // ---- Rendering ----
  function clearSvg(){ while(svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild); }

  function mk(tag,attrs){
    var e=document.createElementNS(SVGNS,tag);
    for(var k in attrs){ if(attrs.hasOwnProperty(k)) e.setAttribute(k,attrs[k]); }
    return e;
  }

  function render(){
    clearSvg();
    // edges
    for(var i=0;i<edges.length;i++){
      var a=nodeById(edges[i][0]), b=nodeById(edges[i][1]);
      var broken = !!brokenEdges[keyOf(a.id,b.id)];
      var line = mk("line",{
        x1:a.x,y1:a.y,x2:b.x,y2:b.y,
        stroke: broken ? "#dc2626" : "#94a3b8",
        "stroke-width": broken ? 4 : 5,
        "stroke-linecap":"round",
        "stroke-dasharray": broken ? "9 8" : "0"
      });
      svg.appendChild(line);
      // wide transparent hit line for breaking
      var hit = mk("line",{x1:a.x,y1:a.y,x2:b.x,y2:b.y,stroke:"transparent","stroke-width":18});
      hit.style.cursor = breakMode ? "crosshair" : "default";
      (function(ea,eb){ hit.addEventListener("click",function(){ onEdgeClick(ea,eb); }); })(a.id,b.id);
      svg.appendChild(hit);
    }
    // nodes
    for(var j=0;j<nodes.length;j++){
      drawNode(nodes[j]);
    }
    // packet on top
    var cn = nodeById(current);
    packet = mk("circle",{cx:cn.x,cy:cn.y,r:9,fill:"#d97706",stroke:"#ffffff","stroke-width":3});
    packet.setAttribute("filter","");
    svg.appendChild(packet);
  }

  function drawNode(n){
    var g = mk("g",{});
    var broken = !!brokenNodes[n.id];
    var fill, stroke;
    if(broken){ fill="#dc2626"; stroke="#991b1b"; }
    else if(n.type==="source"){ fill="#1a56db"; stroke="#0f1f3d"; }
    else if(n.type==="dest"){ fill="#16a34a"; stroke="#14532d"; }
    else { fill="#0f1f3d"; stroke="#334155"; }

    var isCurrent = (n.id===current) && !broken;
    if(isCurrent){
      var ring = mk("circle",{cx:n.x,cy:n.y,r:31,fill:"none",stroke:"#d97706","stroke-width":3});
      g.appendChild(ring);
    }
    // highlight valid next hops
    var validNext = (!animating && !breakMode && !levelDone && neighbors(current).indexOf(n.id)>=0);
    var circle = mk("circle",{cx:n.x,cy:n.y,r:24,fill:fill,stroke: validNext ? "#d97706" : stroke,"stroke-width": validNext ? 4 : 2});
    circle.style.cursor="pointer";
    g.appendChild(circle);

    var lbl = mk("text",{x:n.x,y:n.y+4,"text-anchor":"middle","font-size":"12","font-weight":"700",fill:"#ffffff"});
    lbl.style.webkitTextFillColor="#ffffff";
    lbl.style.pointerEvents="none";
    lbl.textContent = broken ? "\u2715" : n.label;
    g.appendChild(lbl);

    if(n.type==="source" || n.type==="dest"){
      var cap = mk("text",{x:n.x,y:n.y+42,"text-anchor":"middle","font-size":"11","font-weight":"700",fill:"#334155"});
      cap.style.webkitTextFillColor="#334155";
      cap.style.pointerEvents="none";
      cap.textContent = n.type==="source" ? "SOURCE" : "DEST";
      g.appendChild(cap);
    }

    (function(id){ g.addEventListener("click",function(){ onNodeClick(id); }); })(n.id);
    svg.appendChild(g);
  }

  // ---- Feedback ----
  function say(msg,cls){
    fbEl.textContent = msg;
    fbEl.className = "irs-feedback " + (cls||"info");
  }

  function updateBar(){
    elLevel.textContent = (levelIdx+1) + " / " + LEVELS.length;
    elHops.textContent = hops;
    elDelivered.textContent = delivered;
    elScore.textContent = score;
  }

  // ---- Interactions ----
  function onNodeClick(id){
    var lvl = LEVELS[levelIdx];
    if(breakMode){
      var n = nodeById(id);
      if(n.type==="source" || n.type==="dest"){ say("You can't break the source or the destination themselves.","err"); return; }
      if(id===current && !brokenNodes[id]){ say("The packet is sitting on that router  -  move it first, or break a different node.","err"); return; }
      brokenNodes[id] = !brokenNodes[id];
      render();
      recomputeOptimal();
      say(brokenNodes[id] ? ("Router " + n.label + " disabled. If it was on your path, route around it.") : ("Router " + n.label + " restored."), "info");
      return;
    }
    if(animating || levelDone) return;
    if(id===current) return;
    var nbrs = neighbors(current);
    if(nbrs.indexOf(id)<0){
      say("No link there. Packets can only travel along an existing link between two routers.","err");
      flash(id);
      return;
    }
    movePacket(current,id,function(){
      current=id; hops++; updateBar(); render();
      if(id===dest){ onDelivered(); }
      else { say("Hop taken. Next router?","ok"); }
    });
  }

  function onEdgeClick(a,b){
    if(!breakMode) return;
    var k = keyOf(a,b);
    brokenEdges[k] = !brokenEdges[k];
    render();
    recomputeOptimal();
    say(brokenEdges[k] ? "Link disabled. Packets can no longer cross it  -  use a redundant link." : "Link restored.","info");
  }

  function flash(id){
    var g = svg.lastChild; // packet is last; find node circle instead
    // brief red pulse on the target node
    var n = nodeById(id);
    var pulse = mk("circle",{cx:n.x,cy:n.y,r:24,fill:"none",stroke:"#dc2626","stroke-width":4});
    svg.appendChild(pulse);
    var t=0;
    var iv=setInterval(function(){
      t++;
      pulse.setAttribute("r",24+t*3);
      pulse.setAttribute("stroke","rgba(220,38,38,"+(1-t/8)+")");
      if(t>=8){ clearInterval(iv); if(pulse.parentNode) pulse.parentNode.removeChild(pulse); }
    },30);
  }

  function movePacket(fromId,toId,cb){
    animating=true;
    render(); // clears next-hop highlights during motion
    var f=nodeById(fromId), t=nodeById(toId);
    var start=null, dur=430;
    function frame(now){
      if(start===null) start=now;
      var p=Math.min(1,(now-start)/dur);
      var e = p<0.5 ? 2*p*p : 1-Math.pow(-2*p+2,2)/2;
      packet.setAttribute("cx", f.x+(t.x-f.x)*e);
      packet.setAttribute("cy", f.y+(t.y-f.y)*e);
      if(p<1) requestAnimationFrame(frame);
      else { animating=false; if(cb) cb(); }
    }
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  }

  function autoRoute(){
    if(animating || levelDone) return;
    var path = shortestPath(current,dest);
    if(!path){
      if(LEVELS[levelIdx].unreachable){
        showOutage();
      } else {
        say("No path from here. A router or link on every route is broken  -  try restoring or restarting the level.","err");
      }
      return;
    }
    if(path.length===1){ onDelivered(); return; }
    say("Auto-routing along the shortest surviving path...","info");
    stepPath(path,0);
  }

  function stepPath(path,i){
    if(i>=path.length-1){
      current=path[path.length-1];
      onDelivered();
      return;
    }
    movePacket(path[i],path[i+1],function(){
      current=path[i+1]; hops++; updateBar(); render();
      stepPath(path,i+1);
    });
  }

  function onDelivered(){
    if(levelDone) return;
    levelDone=true;
    delivered++;
    var opt = optimal===null ? hops : optimal;
    var extra = hops - opt;
    var pts = Math.max(20, 100 - (extra<0?0:extra)*20);
    score += pts;
    updateBar();
    render();

    var hadFailure = countBroken() > 0;
    var effLine = (extra<=0) ? "Perfect  -  you used the fewest possible hops!" : ("You used " + hops + " hops; the shortest surviving route was " + opt + ".");
    var teach = hadFailure
      ? "You routed <b>around a failure</b>. Redundant paths are exactly why the Internet keeps working when a router or link goes down."
      : "Each hop moved the packet across one link. There is no single fixed wire  -  routers pass packets along until they reach the destination.";

    var isLastDeliverable = true;
    for(var i=levelIdx+1;i<LEVELS.length;i++){ if(!LEVELS[i].unreachable){ isLastDeliverable=false; break; } }
    var moreLevels = (levelIdx < LEVELS.length-1);

    var btn = moreLevels ? '<button class="btn btn-primary" id="irs-next" style="min-width:160px">Next Level →</button>'
                         : '<button class="btn btn-primary" id="irs-next" style="min-width:160px">See Results →</button>';

    showOverlay(
      '<h3 class="win">Packet Delivered!</h3>'+
      '<p><b>'+hops+' hops</b> • +'+pts+' points<br>'+effLine+'</p>'+
      '<p>'+teach+'</p>'+
      btn
    );
    document.getElementById("irs-next").addEventListener("click", function(){
      if(moreLevels) startLevel(levelIdx+1);
      else showResults();
    });
    say("Delivered in " + hops + " hops. +" + pts + " points.","ok");
  }

  function showOutage(){
    levelDone=true;
    render();
    showOverlay(
      '<h3 class="bad">Server Unreachable  -  Outage</h3>'+
      '<p>Every route to the Server passes through one gateway, and it is down. With <b>no redundant path</b>, the packet cannot be delivered at all.</p>'+
      '<p>This is what a real outage looks like: a single point of failure with no backup. The Internet avoids this by building <b>many</b> paths between points.</p>'+
      '<button class="btn btn-primary" id="irs-finish" style="min-width:160px">Finish →</button>'
    );
    document.getElementById("irs-finish").addEventListener("click", showResults);
    say("No path exists. One gateway, no redundancy = total outage.","err");
  }

  function showResults(){
    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsGameScore',{detail:{value:score}}));
    showOverlay(
      '<h3 class="win">Network Mastered!</h3>'+
      '<p>Packets delivered: <b>'+delivered+'</b><br>Final score: <b>'+score+'</b></p>'+
      '<p>You routed packets hop-by-hop, rerouted around broken routers and links, and saw why a single point of failure breaks everything. <b>The Internet is fault-tolerant because it offers many redundant paths, not one fixed route.</b></p>'+
      '<button class="btn btn-primary" id="irs-again" style="min-width:160px">Play Again</button>'
    );
    document.getElementById("irs-again").addEventListener("click", function(){
      score=0; delivered=0; updateBar(); startLevel(0);
    });
  }

  function showOverlay(html){
    overlay.innerHTML = '<div class="irs-card">'+html+'</div>';
    overlay.className = "irs-overlay show";
  }
  function hideOverlay(){ overlay.className="irs-overlay"; overlay.innerHTML=""; }

  function countBroken(){
    var c=0,k;
    for(k in brokenNodes){ if(brokenNodes[k]) c++; }
    for(k in brokenEdges){ if(brokenEdges[k]) c++; }
    return c;
  }

  function recomputeOptimal(){
    optimal = null;
    var p = shortestPath(source,dest);
    if(p) optimal = p.length-1;
  }

  // ---- Level setup ----
  function startLevel(i){
    levelIdx=i;
    var lvl=LEVELS[i];
    // deep-copy nodes so we can reuse defs
    nodes = lvl.nodes.map(function(n){ return {id:n.id,x:n.x,y:n.y,label:n.label,type:n.type}; });
    edges = lvl.edges.map(function(e){ return [e[0],e[1]]; });
    brokenNodes={}; brokenEdges={};
    lvl.brokenNodes.forEach(function(id){ brokenNodes[id]=true; });
    lvl.brokenEdges.forEach(function(e){ brokenEdges[keyOf(e[0],e[1])]=true; });
    source=null; dest=null;
    nodes.forEach(function(n){ if(n.type==="source") source=n.id; if(n.type==="dest") dest=n.id; });
    current=source;
    hops=0; levelDone=false; breakMode=false;
    setBreakBtn();
    recomputeOptimal();
    hideOverlay();
    noteEl.innerHTML = "<b>Level "+(i+1)+" • "+lvl.name+".</b> "+lvl.note;
    updateBar();
    render();
    if(lvl.unreachable){
      say("Try to reach the Server. Use Auto-Route to test if any path survives.","info");
    } else if(countBroken()>0){
      say("Something is broken. Find a working route to the Server, or tap Auto-Route.","info");
    } else {
      say("Tap a router linked to your computer to send the first hop.","info");
    }
  }

  function newPacket(){
    if(animating) return;
    current=source; hops=0; levelDone=false;
    hideOverlay();
    updateBar();
    render();
    say("Fresh packet at the source. Route it to the Server.","info");
  }

  function setBreakBtn(){
    var b=document.getElementById("irs-break");
    if(breakMode){ b.textContent="Break Mode: ON"; b.className="btn btn-break on"; }
    else { b.textContent="Break Mode: OFF"; b.className="btn btn-break"; }
  }

  // ---- Buttons ----
  document.getElementById("irs-send").addEventListener("click", newPacket);
  document.getElementById("irs-auto").addEventListener("click", autoRoute);
  document.getElementById("irs-restart").addEventListener("click", function(){ startLevel(levelIdx); });
  document.getElementById("irs-break").addEventListener("click", function(){
    if(animating) return;
    breakMode=!breakMode;
    setBreakBtn();
    render();
    if(breakMode) say("Break Mode ON: tap a router or a link to disable it (tap again to restore). Then route around it.","info");
    else say("Break Mode OFF: tap routers to move your packet again.","info");
  });

  // ---- Go ----
  startLevel(0);
})();
</script>

      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Is the World Wide Web the same as the Internet?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">No. The Internet is a network of networks, the global infrastructure that connects billions of devices. The World Wide Web is one service that runs over the Internet: a system of linked pages and resources accessed using HTTP. Email and video calls also use the Internet without being part of the Web.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is a protocol, and why do open protocols matter?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">A protocol is an agreed-upon set of rules for formatting and transmitting data. Open, standardized protocols are published and free to use, so devices from different manufacturers running different software can interoperate as long as they follow the same rules. That is what lets the whole Internet work together.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why are packets that take different paths and arrive out of order not a problem?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Because each packet carries a sequence number and a destination address. Packets are routed independently and may arrive out of order, but at the destination TCP uses the sequence numbers to reassemble them in the correct order and requests a resend for anything lost, so the original data is restored.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between bandwidth and latency?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Bandwidth is a rate: the maximum amount of data that can be sent per unit of time, such as bits per second. Latency is the delay, the time it takes data to travel from one point to another. A connection can have high bandwidth and still have noticeable latency, so the two are not the same measurement.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why was IPv6 created if IPv4 already existed?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses and can only provide about 4.3 billion unique IP addresses, which is not enough for all the phones, computers, and smart devices online today. IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses and offers a vastly larger pool, which is how the addressing system was designed to scale as the Internet keeps growing.</div>
