<script>
(function(){
  var G = {
    score:0, streak:0, best:0, sortIdx:0, phase:'intro',
    recruited:0, goal:1000, timeLeft:0, timer:null
  };

  var TASKS = [
    {t:'Map disaster damage after a hurricane using photos from thousands of residents', ico:'🌎', good:true, why:'Many people covering a wide area map far more damage than one team could.'},
    {t:'Fund a new indie video game with many small pledges from fans', ico:'💰', good:true, why:'Crowdfunding pools tiny contributions from a huge crowd into real money.'},
    {t:'Label 50,000 training images so an AI can learn to spot birds', ico:'🏷', good:true, why:'Splitting huge labeling work across many people gets it done fast.'},
    {t:'Build a free online encyclopedia anyone can add to and edit', ico:'📚', good:true, why:'Diverse contributors cover more topics than any single author could.'},
    {t:'Collect local temperature and wildlife readings for a climate study', ico:'🌿', good:true, why:'Citizen-science volunteers gather data at a scale researchers cannot alone.'},
    {t:'Translate a short article into 20 languages using volunteer speakers', ico:'🗣', good:true, why:'Reaching many bilingual volunteers scales work that needs diverse skills.'},
    {t:'Perform heart surgery on a patient in the operating room', ico:'🩺', good:false, why:'Life-critical work needs one trained expert, not a crowd of strangers.'},
    {t:'Write the classified security code for a private bank vault system', ico:'🔒', good:false, why:'Tasks that must stay secret cannot be opened up to the public crowd.'},
    {t:'Decide the exact medication dose for a specific hospital patient', ico:'💉', good:false, why:'This needs one qualified expert who knows the patient, not the crowd.'},
    {t:'Sign a legally binding contract on behalf of your company', ico:'📝', good:false, why:'Authority and accountability rest with one person, so a crowd cannot do it.'},
    {t:'Fly a passenger jet safely across the country', ico:'✈', good:false, why:'Safety-critical control belongs to one certified expert, not a crowd.'}
  ];

  var body = document.getElementById('cp-body');
  var elScore = document.getElementById('cp-score');
  var elStrk = document.getElementById('cp-strk');
  var elPart = document.getElementById('cp-part');

  function shuffle(a){ a=a.slice(); for(var i=a.length-1;i>0;i--){ var j=Math.floor(Math.random()*(i+1)); var t=a[i];a[i]=a[j];a[j]=t;} return a; }
  function sync(){ elScore.textContent=G.score; elStrk.textContent=G.streak; }

  var sortSet=[];
  var SORT_N=6;

  function intro(){
    G.phase='intro'; elPart.textContent='Intro';
    body.innerHTML =
      '<div class="cp-center">'+
      '<div class="cp-task"><div class="ico">👥</div><div class="txt">Ready to see when the crowd wins?</div></div>'+
      '<p class="cp-prompt">Round 1: sort real tasks. Round 2: recruit the crowd to reach a goal. One quick game, two ways crowdsourcing shows its power.</p>'+
      '<button class="cp-start" id="cp-startbtn">▶ Start</button>'+
      '</div>';
    document.getElementById('cp-startbtn').onclick=startGame;
  }

  function startGame(){
    G.score=0; G.streak=0; G.sortIdx=0; sync();
    sortSet = shuffle(TASKS).slice(0,SORT_N);
    G.phase='sort'; renderSort();
  }

  function renderSort(){
    elPart.textContent='1 / 2';
    var task = sortSet[G.sortIdx];
    body.innerHTML =
      '<div class="cp-phase">Round 1 • Sort the task ('+(G.sortIdx+1)+' of '+SORT_N+')</div>'+
      '<p class="cp-prompt">Predict first: would a big online crowd handle this well?</p>'+
      '<div class="cp-task"><div class="ico">'+task.ico+'</div><div class="txt">'+task.t+'</div></div>'+
      '<div class="cp-choices">'+
        '<button class="cp-btn good" id="cp-good">Crowdsource<span class="sm">Great for a crowd</span></button>'+
        '<button class="cp-btn bad" id="cp-bad">Not a good fit<span class="sm">Wrong for a crowd</span></button>'+
      '</div>'+
      '<div class="cp-fb hidden" id="cp-fb"></div>';
    document.getElementById('cp-good').onclick=function(){ answerSort(true); };
    document.getElementById('cp-bad').onclick=function(){ answerSort(false); };
  }

  function answerSort(chose){
    var task = sortSet[G.sortIdx];
    var correct = (chose===task.good);
    var good=document.getElementById('cp-good'), bad=document.getElementById('cp-bad');
    good.disabled=true; bad.disabled=true;
    good.style.opacity=chose||correct?'1':'.55'; bad.style.opacity=(!chose)||(!correct)?'1':'.55';
    var fb=document.getElementById('cp-fb');
    fb.classList.remove('hidden');
    if(correct){
      G.streak++;
      var pts=10 + Math.min(G.streak,5)*2;
      G.score+=pts;
      fb.className='cp-fb ok';
      fb.innerHTML='✅ Correct (+'+pts+'). '+task.why;
    } else {
      G.streak=0;
      fb.className='cp-fb no';
      fb.innerHTML='❌ Not quite. '+task.why;
    }
    sync();
    setTimeout(function(){
      G.sortIdx++;
      if(G.sortIdx<SORT_N) renderSort();
      else recruitIntro();
    }, 1350);
  }

  function recruitIntro(){
    G.phase='recruit'; elPart.textContent='2 / 2';
    G.recruited=0; G.goal=1000; G.timeLeft=10;
    body.innerHTML =
      '<div class="cp-phase">Round 2 • Recruit the crowd</div>'+
      '<p class="cp-prompt">Each tap invites more people. No single tap does much  -  but many small contributions add up fast. Reach <b>'+G.goal+'</b> contributors before time runs out!</p>'+
      '<div class="cp-meterwrap">'+
        '<div class="cp-meter"><div class="cp-fill" id="cp-fill"></div></div>'+
        '<div class="cp-metertxt" id="cp-metertxt">0 / '+G.goal+' contributors</div>'+
      '</div>'+
      '<button class="cp-recruit" id="cp-recruitbtn">📱 Recruit the crowd!<span class="sm">Tap as fast as you can</span></button>'+
      '<div class="cp-crowd" id="cp-crowd"></div>'+
      '<div class="cp-timer" id="cp-timer">Time: 10.0s</div>';
    document.getElementById('cp-recruitbtn').onclick=recruitTap;
    var start=Date.now();
    G.timer=setInterval(function(){
      var elapsed=(Date.now()-start)/1000;
      G.timeLeft=Math.max(0,10-elapsed);
      var te=document.getElementById('cp-timer');
      if(te) te.textContent='Time: '+G.timeLeft.toFixed(1)+'s';
      if(G.timeLeft<=0 || G.recruited>=G.goal) endRecruit();
    },100);
  }

  var faces=['👤','👩','👨','🤵','👧','👦'];
  function recruitTap(){
    if(G.phase!=='recruit') return;
    var add=8+Math.floor(Math.random()*10);
    G.recruited+=add;
    if(G.recruited>G.goal) G.recruited=G.goal;
    var pct=Math.min(100,(G.recruited/G.goal)*100);
    var fill=document.getElementById('cp-fill');
    var txt=document.getElementById('cp-metertxt');
    var crowd=document.getElementById('cp-crowd');
    if(fill) fill.style.width=pct+'%';
    if(txt) txt.textContent=G.recruited+' / '+G.goal+' contributors (+'+add+')';
    if(crowd){
      var n=Math.min(60,Math.round(G.recruited/16));
      var s=''; for(var i=0;i<n;i++) s+=faces[i%faces.length];
      crowd.innerHTML=s;
    }
    if(G.recruited>=G.goal) endRecruit();
  }

  function endRecruit(){
    if(G.timer){ clearInterval(G.timer); G.timer=null; }
    if(G.phase!=='recruit') return;
    G.phase='done';
    var reached=G.recruited>=G.goal;
    var bonus=Math.round(G.recruited/10) + (reached?40:0);
    G.score+=bonus;
    sync();
    endScreen(reached,bonus);
  }

  function endScreen(reached,bonus){
    elPart.textContent='Done';
    var tie = reached
      ? 'You hit the goal! One tap was tiny, but a big crowd made it easy  -  that scale is exactly why crowdsourcing works for mapping, funding, and labeling.'
      : 'Time! Even without the goal, notice how fast small contributions piled up. That is the power of the crowd  -  scale and diversity many hands provide.';
    body.innerHTML =
      '<div class="cp-end">'+
      '<div class="ico" style="font-size:40px">🎉</div>'+
      '<div class="big">Great work!</div>'+
      '<div class="flabel">Final score</div>'+
      '<div class="fscore" id="cp-fscore">'+G.score+'</div>'+
      '<div class="flabel">Recruited '+G.recruited+' contributors • +'+bonus+' bonus</div>'+
      '<p class="tie">'+tie+' But remember: it is <b>not</b> right for tasks needing one expert or that must stay secret, like surgery or private security code.</p>'+
      '<button class="cp-again" id="cp-againbtn">↻ Play again</button>'+
      '</div>';
    document.getElementById('cp-againbtn').onclick=startGame;
    try{ document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsGameScore',{detail:{value:G.score}})); }catch(e){}
  }

  intro();
})();
</script>

      <h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is crowdsourcing in one sentence?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Crowdsourcing is getting input, ideas, content, labor, or funding from a large group of people, often through the Internet, to accomplish a task or solve a problem.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">How is crowdsourcing different from ordinary collaboration?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Collaboration can be a small, closed team working together. Crowdsourcing specifically draws on a large, often open group, usually reached through the Internet, with each person contributing a small piece. Size and openness are what set it apart.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">Why is the Internet so important to crowdsourcing?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">The Internet gives a project reach, speed, and scale: a request can reach millions of people, thousands can contribute in parallel, and software gathers and combines every small contribution automatically. Without computing, the crowd shrinks to whoever you can reach in person.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What is the difference between citizen science and crowdfunding?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Both are forms of crowdsourcing, but they differ in what the crowd provides. In citizen science the crowd supplies data and labor, such as classifying images or reporting observations. In crowdfunding the crowd supplies money, many small contributions that together fund a project.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="faq-item">
        <button class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFAQ(this)">What are the main concerns with crowdsourced work?<i class="faq-icon">+</i></button>
        <div class="faq-a">Quality and accuracy, because contributions come from many unverified people; coordination, because thousands of loose contributors are hard to organize; and attribution, because it is unclear who gets credit or ownership when a crowd builds something together.</div>

function _activity(d){
  try{ var w=document.querySelector('.lesson-page');
    if(w){ d.course=w.getAttribute('data-course'); d.unit=w.getAttribute('data-unit'); d.lesson=w.getAttribute('data-lesson'); }
    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsActivity',{detail:d}));
  }catch(e){}
}
function checkMCQ(qid, chosen, correct, fbId){
  var opts=document.querySelectorAll('#'+qid+'-options .mcq-option');
  opts.forEach(function(b){b.disabled=true;b.onclick=null;});
  var letters=['A','B','C','D'];
  opts[letters.indexOf(chosen)].classList.add(chosen===correct?'correct':'incorrect');
  if(chosen!==correct)opts[letters.indexOf(correct)].classList.add('revealed-correct');
  document.getElementById(fbId).classList.add('show');
  _activity({activity:'quiz',item:qid,choice:chosen});
}
function miniMCQ(id, chosen, correct, fbId){
  var opts=document.querySelectorAll('#'+id+'-opts .mini-opt');
  opts.forEach(function(b){b.onclick=null;b.style.cursor='default';});
  var letters=['A','B','C','D'];
  opts[letters.indexOf(chosen)].classList.add(chosen===correct?'correct':'incorrect');
  if(chosen!==correct)opts[letters.indexOf(correct)].classList.add('reveal');
  var fb=document.getElementById(fbId);

  <div class="lesson-main">

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Define the digital divide as unequal access to computing devices and to the Internet</span></li>
        <li><span>Identify factors that drive the divide, including income, geography, and demographics</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain how the divide affects who can participate in and benefit from computing</span></li>
        <li><span>Distinguish the local, national, and global levels at which the divide exists</span></li>
        <li><span>Describe evenhanded efforts that can reduce the divide, such as infrastructure, cost, and training</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span>Big Idea 5 (Impact of Computing) is 21 to 26 percent of the AP CSP exam, the single largest slice, and the digital divide is a favorite target because it is easy to write clear, fair questions about it. Nail the definition and the causes and you bank reliable points.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>Two students are assigned the same online research project. One has a laptop at home and fast, reliable Internet; the other shares a single phone with three siblings and can only get online at the public library before it closes. Both are equally smart and equally hardworking, yet one will almost certainly turn in more. What is actually different between them, and what would it take to close that gap?</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What the Digital Divide Actually Is</h2>
      <p>The <strong>digital divide</strong> is the unequal <strong>access</strong> to computing devices and to the Internet across different groups of people. That word, access, is the whole idea. The divide is not about who is smart or who is good with computers. It is about who has a working device, a reliable connection, and the ability to use them, and who does not.</p>
      <p>Access is really two things at once. A person needs a <strong>device</strong> (a computer, tablet, or phone that can do the task) and a <strong>connection</strong> (Internet service that is fast and reliable enough to be useful). Having a phone but no home Internet, or having Internet so slow that a video call keeps dropping, still counts as being on the wrong side of the divide. The AP framework ties this directly to opportunity: access to computing shapes who can participate in and benefit from what computing offers.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>When a question describes the digital divide, the key idea graders want is <strong>unequal access to computing and the Internet, and the resulting difference in who can participate</strong>. Answers that focus on access and opportunity beat answers about personal talent or interest almost every time.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>What Drives the Divide</h2>
      <p>The framework lists the groups the divide falls along. You should be able to recognize each factor:</p>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Factor</th>
<th>How it affects access</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Socioeconomic status (income)</strong></td>
<td>Devices and monthly Internet service cost money. Lower-income households are less able to afford a good device or a fast plan.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Geography</strong></td>
<td>Rural and remote areas often lack the infrastructure (cables, towers) that cities have, so service may be slow, expensive, or unavailable. This also differs between wealthier and less wealthy countries.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Demographics</strong></td>
<td>Access can differ by age, education level, and disability. For example, a site that is unusable with a screen reader shuts out some users regardless of their connection.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Digital literacy</strong></td>
<td>Even with a device and a connection, a person needs the skills to use them. Lack of training is its own barrier.</td>
</tr>
      </table>
      <p>These factors overlap. A low-income household in a rural area faces both a cost barrier and an infrastructure barrier at the same time. The divide is also shaped by <strong>decisions</strong>, by governments, companies, and individuals, about where to build infrastructure, how to price service, and what to teach.</p>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A town's homes are spread far apart in a remote area, and no company has run high-speed cable out to them, so residents can only get slow service at high prices. Which factor of the digital divide does this best illustrate?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-divide-1-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-divide-1','A','C','mc-divide-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> The residents lack interest in the Internet</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-divide-1','B','C','mc-divide-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> The residents are not skilled enough to use computers</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-divide-1','C','C','mc-divide-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> Geography and infrastructure limit their access</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-divide-1','D','C','mc-divide-1-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> The Internet itself is running out of space</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-divide-1-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Why It Matters: Participation and Benefit</h2>
      <p>So much of daily life now runs through computing: applying for jobs, doing schoolwork, seeing a doctor over video, filing government forms, banking, and finding information. When access is unequal, so is the chance to <strong>participate in and benefit from</strong> all of that. The divide can widen existing gaps, because the people who most need affordable services online are sometimes the least able to reach them.</p>
      <p>The divide exists at three levels, and the exam expects you to tell them apart:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Local</strong>: differences between neighborhoods or households in the same town, such as which students have home Internet.</li>
        <li>
<strong>National</strong>: differences within one country, such as urban versus rural regions.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Global</strong>: differences between countries, where wealthier nations tend to have far higher access than lower-income ones.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>The digital divide is about <strong>access and opportunity, not natural ability</strong>. A wrong answer will suggest some groups are simply "not good with technology" or "not interested." The framework is clear that the divide is a difference in access to devices, connection, and training, not a difference in how capable people are. If someone gets a device, a connection, and instruction, they can participate.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Narrowing the Divide</h2>
      <p>Because the divide comes from access barriers, efforts to reduce it target those barriers. The framework wants you to recognize the general categories, not to endorse any one plan:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>
<strong>Expanding infrastructure</strong>: building cable, fiber, or wireless coverage into areas that lack it.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Lowering cost</strong>: making devices and service more affordable, for example through subsidized plans or low-cost hardware.</li>
        <li>
<strong>Providing training</strong>: teaching digital literacy so people can actually use the access they gain.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>These can come from governments, companies, nonprofits, schools, or individuals, and real solutions usually combine several. A program that ships free laptops but never provides Internet or instruction has only solved one piece of the problem. Keep your reasoning <strong>evenhanded</strong>: the exam asks which actions reduce access barriers, not which political approach is best.</p>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A district gives every student a laptop but discovers many still cannot complete online homework because their homes have no Internet service. Which additional action would most directly reduce the remaining divide?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-divide-2-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-divide-2','A','B','mc-divide-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> Giving each student a second laptop</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-divide-2','B','B','mc-divide-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> Providing affordable home Internet access to those households</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-divide-2','C','B','mc-divide-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> Assigning only homework that requires no computer</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-divide-2','D','B','mc-divide-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> Making the laptops run faster</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-divide-2-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How 5.2 Is Tested on the Multiple-Choice Exam</h2>
      <p>Digital divide questions on the AP CSP exam cluster around three things, and knowing the shape of them makes the points easy. First, the <strong>definition</strong>: expect a question that asks what the digital divide is, where the correct answer names unequal access to computing devices and the Internet across groups. Second, the <strong>causes</strong>: a scenario will describe a person or community, and you identify which factor (income, geography, demographics, or digital literacy) explains their limited access, or which action would reduce that barrier. Third, the <strong>effects</strong>: questions connect access to who can participate in and benefit from computing, such as school, jobs, or services.</p>
      <p>Two habits keep you out of the traps. Keep your framing <strong>evenhanded</strong>: the exam treats the divide as a matter of access and opportunity, never as a claim that some group is naturally worse with technology, and it does not favor one political solution over another. And read for <strong>level</strong>: notice whether a question is describing a local, national, or global gap, because the correct answer often hinges on that scope.</p>
    </div>

<div id="q1-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The divide is about access and opportunity, not personal preference or enjoyment.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. The digital divide is the unequal access to computing devices and the Internet among different groups, which affects who can participate and benefit.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Typing speed is a personal skill, not the access gap the framework describes.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. That describes technology adoption over time, not unequal access across groups.</div>

        <div class="mcq-options" id="q2-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','A','C','q2-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Digital literacy, at the global level</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','B','C','q2-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> Disability, at the national level</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','C','C','q2-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Socioeconomic status, at the local level</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','D','C','q2-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> Infrastructure age, at the global level</button>
</div>
<div id="q2-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The scenario is about affording service, not about skills, and it compares neighborhoods in one city, not countries.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Nothing here points to disability, and comparing neighborhoods in one city is local, not national.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. The gap tracks income (socioeconomic status), and because it is between neighborhoods in the same city it is a local-level divide.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. The described cause is affordability by income, and one city is a local scope, not global.</div>

        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A student writes four claims about the digital divide. Which claim is <strong>incorrect</strong>?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q3-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','A','D','q3-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> The divide can exist at local, national, and global levels</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','B','D','q3-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> The divide is influenced by the cost of devices and Internet service</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','C','D','q3-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Access to training in digital literacy can affect the divide</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','D','D','q3-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> The divide exists because some groups are naturally less capable with technology</button>
</div>
<div id="q3-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. This claim is true. The divide does occur across local, national, and global scopes.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. This claim is true. Cost of devices and service is a real driver of the divide.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. This claim is true. Digital literacy and training influence who can use the access they have.</div>
<div id="q3-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. This is the false claim. The divide is about unequal access and opportunity, not any natural difference in ability between groups.</div>

        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>Consider these statements about efforts to reduce the digital divide:</p></div>

          <li>
<strong>I.</strong> Expanding Internet infrastructure into areas that currently lack service can increase access.</li>
          <li>
<strong>II.</strong> Lowering the cost of devices and service can increase access for lower-income households.</li>
          <li>
<strong>III.</strong> Access alone always guarantees a person can use computing effectively, so training is unnecessary.</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q4-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','A','A','q4-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> I and II only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','B','A','q4-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> I only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','C','A','q4-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> II and III only</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','D','A','q4-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> I, II, and III</button>
</div>
<div id="q4-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. I and II both reduce access barriers. III is false: without digital literacy, access alone does not guarantee effective use, which is why training matters.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement II is also a valid way to reduce the divide, so I only is too narrow.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement III is false, and statement I is true, so this pairing cannot be right.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Statement III is false, so not all three can be correct.</div>

</div>

        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A country moves nearly all job applications, school enrollment, and government services online. According to the framework, what is the most direct consequence of the digital divide in this setting?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q5-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','A','B','q5-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Everyone gains equal access to these services because they are now online</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','B','B','q5-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> People without reliable devices and Internet access are less able to participate in and benefit from these services</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','C','B','q5-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> The digital divide disappears once services move to the Internet</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q5','D','B','q5-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> The main effect is that servers must be upgraded to handle more traffic</button>
</div>
<div id="q5-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Moving services online does not give everyone access; it can shut out those who lack devices or a connection.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. When essential services require computing, the people on the wrong side of the divide are least able to participate in and benefit from them.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Putting services online does not remove the underlying access gaps; it can make them matter more.</div>
<div id="q5-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Server capacity is a technical detail, not the framework's point about unequal participation.</div>
      </div>

</div>

        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A nonprofit wants to reduce the global digital divide between a wealthy nation and a lower-income nation where few communities have any Internet infrastructure at all. Which action would most directly address the barrier described?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q6-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','A','B','q6-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> Publishing its website in more languages</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','B','B','q6-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> Building network infrastructure so communities that currently have no service can connect</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','C','B','q6-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Speeding up the servers in the wealthy nation</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q6','D','B','q6-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> Encouraging residents to buy newer phones on their own</button>
</div>
<div id="q6-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Translation helps usability but does nothing for communities that have no connection at all.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. The stated barrier is a lack of infrastructure, so building network coverage is the action that most directly creates access.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Faster servers elsewhere do not help communities that cannot connect in the first place.</div>
<div id="q6-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Telling people to buy devices ignores that there is no service to connect them, and it assumes they can afford it.</div>

  var state = { round:0, total:0, choices:[] };

  function optKeyForDriver(driver){
    for(var k in OPTS){ if(OPTS[k].driver===driver) return k; }
    return null;
  }

  function renderPlay(){
    var R = ROUNDS[state.round];
    state.choices = R.comms.map(function(){ return null; });
    elRound.textContent = state.round+1;
    elTotal.textContent = state.total;
    updateBudget();

    var html = '';
    html += '<p class="btd-round-h">Round '+(state.round+1)+' of 4</p>';
    html += '<p class="btd-round-t">'+R.note+'</p>';

    R.comms.forEach(function(c, ci){
      html += '<div class="btd-comm">';
      html += '<div class="btd-comm-top"><span class="btd-comm-name">'+c.name+'</span>'+
              '<span class="btd-comm-pop">'+c.pop+' unconnected</span></div>';
      html += '<p class="btd-need">Gap: '+c.gap+'</p>';
      html += '<div class="btd-opts">';
      for(var k in OPTS){
        var o = OPTS[k];
        html += '<button class="btd-opt" data-ci="'+ci+'" data-k="'+k+'">'+
                '<span class="btd-opt-n">'+o.name+'</span>'+
                '<span class="btd-opt-c">Cost '+o.cost+'</span>'+
                '<span class="btd-opt-d">'+o.d+'</span></button>';
      }
      html += '</div></div>';
    });
    html += '<p class="btd-warn" id="btd-warn"></p>';
    html += '<div class="btd-actions">'+
            '<button class="btd-btn" id="btd-resolve">Resolve round ▶</button>'+
            '<button class="btd-btn ghost" id="btd-clear">Clear picks</button>'+
            '</div>';
    body.innerHTML = html;

    Array.prototype.forEach.call(body.querySelectorAll('.btd-opt'), function(btn){
      btn.addEventListener('click', function(){ togglePick(parseInt(btn.getAttribute('data-ci'),10), btn.getAttribute('data-k')); });
    });
    body.querySelector('#btd-resolve').addEventListener('click', resolveRound);
    body.querySelector('#btd-clear').addEventListener('click', function(){ renderPlay(); });
  }

  function spent(){
    var s = 0;
    state.choices.forEach(function(k){ if(k) s += OPTS[k].cost; });
    return s;
  }
  function updateBudget(){
    var R = ROUNDS[state.round];
    var left = R.budget - spent();
    elBudget.textContent = 'Budget: '+left+' / '+R.budget;
    elBudget.classList.toggle('low', left<=2);
    return left;
  }

  function togglePick(ci, k){
    var R = ROUNDS[state.round];
    var warn = body.querySelector('#btd-warn');
    warn.textContent = '';
    var prev = state.choices[ci];
    // toggle off if same
    if(prev===k){ state.choices[ci]=null; }
    else {
      var wouldSpend = spent() - (prev?OPTS[prev].cost:0) + OPTS[k].cost;
      if(wouldSpend > R.budget){ warn.textContent = 'Not enough budget for that pick. Free up points or choose a cheaper fix.'; refreshSel(); return; }
      state.choices[ci]=k;
    }
    refreshSel();
  }

  function refreshSel(){
    var R = ROUNDS[state.round];
    var left = updateBudget();
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(body.querySelectorAll('.btd-opt'), function(btn){
      var ci = parseInt(btn.getAttribute('data-ci'),10);
      var k = btn.getAttribute('data-k');
      var sel = state.choices[ci]===k;
      btn.classList.toggle('sel', sel);
      // disable options that cost more than remaining (unless already selected in this community)
      var curCost = state.choices[ci]?OPTS[state.choices[ci]].cost:0;
      var affordable = (OPTS[k].cost - curCost) <= left || sel;
      btn.classList.toggle('dis', !affordable);
    });
  }

  function resolveRound(){
    var R = ROUNDS[state.round];
    var roundConnected = 0;
    var results = R.comms.map(function(c, ci){
      var k = state.choices[ci];
      var connected = 0, cls='bad', explain='';
      if(!k){
        connected = 0; cls='bad';
        explain = 'No investment  -  0 connected. ' + c.why;
      } else if(OPTS[k].driver === c.driver){
        connected = c.pop; cls='good';
        explain = 'Right fix for the cause  -  all '+c.pop+' connected. ' + c.why;
      } else {
        connected = Math.round(c.pop*0.25); cls='mid';
        explain = 'Partial: this helps a little but does not address the real cause. ' + c.why;
      }
      roundConnected += connected;
      return { c:c, connected:connected, cls:cls, explain:explain };
    });
    state.total += roundConnected;

    var html = '';
    html += '<p class="btd-round-h">Round '+(state.round+1)+' results</p>';
    html += '<p class="btd-note">You connected <b>'+roundConnected+'</b> people this round. The digital divide is about <b>unequal access and its causes</b>  -  matching each fix to what actually drives the gap connects the most people.</p>';
    results.forEach(function(r){
      var pct = Math.round(r.connected / r.c.pop * 100);
      html += '<div class="btd-res-comm">';
      html += '<div class="btd-res-name">'+r.c.name+'</div>';
      html += '<div class="btd-res-conn '+r.cls+'">'+r.connected+' / '+r.c.pop+' connected ('+pct+'%)</div>';
      html += '<div class="btd-meter"><i style="width:'+pct+'%"></i></div>';
      html += '<div class="btd-res-why">'+r.explain+'</div>';
      html += '</div>';
    });
    var last = state.round >= ROUNDS.length-1;
    html += '<div class="btd-actions">'+
            '<button class="btd-btn" id="btd-next">'+(last?'See final results ▶':'Next round ▶')+'</button>'+
            '</div>';
    body.innerHTML = html;
    elTotal.textContent = state.total;

    body.querySelector('#btd-next').addEventListener('click', function(){
      if(last){ renderEnd(); }
      else { state.round++; renderPlay(); }
    });
  }

  function renderEnd(){
    elRound.textContent = 4;
    var maxPeople = 0;
    ROUNDS.forEach(function(R){ R.comms.forEach(function(c){ maxPeople += c.pop; }); });
    var pct = Math.round(state.total / maxPeople * 100);
    var msg;
    if(pct>=90) msg = 'Outstanding. You matched investments to the true drivers  -  geography, income, skills, and cost  -  and closed nearly every gap.';
    else if(pct>=65) msg = 'Solid work. You connected most people. The biggest wins came from matching each fix to what actually caused the gap.';
    else msg = 'The gaps stayed wide. Remember: the divide is not just "no internet"  -  infrastructure fixes geography, devices fix income, training fixes skills, and shared access fixes cost.';

    var html = '';
    html += '<h3 class="btd-end-h">🌐 Every fix has a cause</h3>';
    html += '<div class="btd-end-lbl">Total people connected</div>';
    html += '<div class="btd-end-big">'+state.total+'</div>';
    html += '<div class="btd-end-lbl">out of '+maxPeople+' possible ('+pct+'%)</div>';
    html += '<p class="btd-end-msg">'+msg+' The <b>digital divide</b> describes unequal access to computing driven by socioeconomic status, geography, and other factors  -  and closing it means addressing the specific cause each community faces.</p>';
    html += '<div class="btd-actions">'+
            '<button class="btd-btn" id="btd-again">↻ Play again</button>'+
            '</div>';
    body.innerHTML = html;

    body.querySelector('#btd-again').addEventListener('click', function(){
      state = { round:0, total:0, choices:[] };
      renderPlay();
    });

    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('apcsGameScore', { detail:{ value: state.total } }));
  }

  renderPlay();
})();
</script>

  .prog-step-link:hover .prog-dot{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-dot{width:26px!important;height:26px!important;border-radius:50%!important;display:flex!important;align-items:center!important;justify-content:center!important;font-size:9px!important;font-weight:700!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}
  .prog-dot.active{background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;}
  .prog-dot.upcoming{background:#f1f5f9!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;}
  .prog-dot.done{background:#dbeafe!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;border:2px solid var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-label{font-size:8px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;line-height:1.2!important;white-space:nowrap!important;}
  .prog-label.active-label{color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;}
  .prog-arrow{flex:1 0 4px!important;height:2px!important;background:#e2e8f0!important;margin-bottom:18px!important;min-width:4px!important;max-width:16px!important;flex-shrink:0!important;}

  /* MAIN */
  .lesson-main{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;padding:40px 24px 80px;}
  .lesson-objectives{background:var(--bi3-bg);border-left:4px solid var(--bi3);border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin-bottom:28px;}
  .lesson-objectives h2{font-size:14px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;text-transform:uppercase!important;letter-spacing:.06em!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .lesson-objectives ul{list-style:none;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .lesson-objectives li{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#1e3a8a;line-height:1.5;}
  .lesson-objectives li::before{content:"\2713";color:var(--bi3);font-weight:700;flex-shrink:0;margin-top:1px;}
  .score-impact{background:#f0fdf4;border:1px solid #bbf7d0;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 18px;margin-bottom:28px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;font-size:14px;color:#14532d;}
  .score-impact strong{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}

  /* HOOK */
  .hook-box{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:32px;}
  .hook-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .hook-box p{font-size:15px!important;color:#bfdbfe!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#bfdbfe!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:0!important;}

  /* LESSON SECTIONS */
  .lesson-section{margin-bottom:40px;}
  .lesson-section h2{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px!important;padding-bottom:10px!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .lesson-section h3{font-size:17px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-top:24px!important;margin-bottom:10px!important;}
  .lesson-section p{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section ul,.lesson-section ol{padding-left:20px;margin-bottom:14px;}
  .lesson-section li{font-size:15px;color:#374151;line-height:1.7;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .lesson-section code{background:#eef2ff;color:#1e3a8a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e3a8a!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}

  /* DUAL CODE PANEL */
  .code-panel-wrap{margin:20px 0;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;}
  .code-panel-tabs{display:flex;background:#1e293b;}
  .code-tab{padding:8px 16px;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;border:none;background:transparent;letter-spacing:.04em;transition:background .15s;font-family:inherit;}
  .code-tab.py{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.pseudo{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;}
  .code-tab.active{background:rgba(255,255,255,.15)!important;}
  .code-tab-label{font-size:10px;opacity:.6;margin-left:4px;font-weight:400;}
  .code-pane{background:#0f172a;padding:18px 20px;overflow-x:auto;height:0;overflow:hidden;padding:0;}
  .code-pane.active{height:auto;overflow-x:auto;padding:18px 20px;}
  .code-pane pre{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:0;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word;max-width:100%;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-kw{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .py-fn{color:#6ee7b7!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#6ee7b7!important;}
  .py-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .py-str{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .py-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .py-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .py-op{color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;}
  .ps-kw{color:#c4b5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#c4b5fd!important;font-weight:700;}
  .ps-op{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .ps-num{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .ps-str{color:#86efac!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#86efac!important;}
  .ps-comment{color:#475569!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#475569!important;font-style:italic;}
  .ps-var{color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* CALLOUTS */
  .callout-exam{background:#fffbeb;border:1px solid #fcd34d;border-left:4px solid var(--amber);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-exam-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--amber)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--amber)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-exam p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}
  .callout-trap{background:#fef2f2;border:1px solid #fca5a5;border-left:4px solid var(--red);border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;padding:16px 20px;margin:20px 0;}
  .callout-trap-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;margin-bottom:6px;}
  .callout-trap p{font-size:14px!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.6!important;}

  /* MINI EXERCISES */
  .mini-ex{background:#fff;border:1px solid #bfdbfe;border-radius:12px;padding:20px 24px;margin:24px 0;}
  .mini-ex-label{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mini-ex-q{font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;margin-bottom:14px;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-ex-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin-bottom:14px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;}
  .mini-opts{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:7px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-opt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;padding:10px 14px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;font-family:monospace;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;background:#f8fafc;text-align:left;width:100%;transition:border-color .15s;}
  .mini-opt:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mini-opt.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-opt.reveal{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mini-opt-letter{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;min-width:18px;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-opt.correct .mini-opt-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mini-opt.incorrect .mini-opt-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mini-fib-row{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .mini-fib-input{padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;width:130px;outline:none;color:var(--navy)!important;background:#f8fafc;}
  .mini-fib-input:focus{border-color:var(--bi3-lt);}
  .mini-fib-input.correct{border-color:var(--green);background:#f0fdf4;}
  .mini-fib-input.incorrect{border-color:var(--red);background:#fef2f2;}
  .mini-fib-btn{padding:8px 18px;background:var(--bi3);border:none;border-radius:8px;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-family:inherit;}
  .mini-fb{font-size:13px;font-weight:500;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:7px;margin-top:6px;display:none;line-height:1.5;}
  .mini-fb.c{background:#f0fdf4;color:var(--green)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--green)!important;display:block;}
  .mini-fb.w{background:#fef2f2;color:var(--red)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--red)!important;display:block;}

  /* VOCAB */
  .vocab-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;margin-bottom:24px;font-size:14px;}
  .vocab-table thead tr{background:var(--bi3);}
  .vocab-table thead th{padding:10px 16px;text-align:left;font-weight:600;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;font-size:13px;}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bi3-bg);}
  .vocab-table tbody tr:nth-child(odd){background:#fff;}
  .vocab-table tbody td{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid #bfdbfe;color:#374151;vertical-align:top;line-height:1.5;}
  .vocab-table tbody td:first-child{font-weight:700;color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;white-space:nowrap;}

  /* CPT CONNECTION */
  .cpt-connection{background:#fefce8;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-left:4px solid #f59e0b;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;padding:20px 24px;margin:28px 0;}
  .cpt-connection-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#92400e!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#92400e!important;margin-bottom:8px;}
  .cpt-connection h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;margin:16px 0 8px!important;}
  .cpt-connection p{font-size:14px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.7!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .cpt-connection a{color:#b45309!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b45309!important;font-weight:600;text-decoration:underline;}
  .cpt-connection code{background:#fef3c7;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:13px;}
  .cpt-stems{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 0 8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;}
  .cpt-stems li{background:#fffef5;border:1px solid #fde68a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 14px;font-size:13px!important;color:#78350f!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#78350f!important;line-height:1.6;}
  .cpt-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:14px 16px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.8;margin:6px 0 12px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;display:block;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}

  /* EMAIL */
  .email-capture{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:12px;padding:24px 28px;margin-bottom:36px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .email-capture-text{flex:1;min-width:200px;}
  .email-capture-eyebrow{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:4px;}
  .email-capture h3{font-size:16px!important;font-weight:700!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .email-capture p{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:0!important;line-height:1.5!important;}
  .email-capture-form{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;flex-shrink:0;}
  .email-capture-input{padding:10px 14px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);background:rgba(255,255,255,.1);color:#fff!important;font-size:14px;font-family:inherit;min-width:180px;outline:none;}
  .email-capture-btn{padding:10px 20px!important;background:var(--bi3)!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;border:none!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;font-weight:600!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .email-capture-success{display:none;font-size:14px;color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;font-weight:600;padding:10px 0;}

  /* MCQ */
  .mcq-section{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .mcq-section-header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;margin-bottom:24px;padding-bottom:16px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--bi3-bg);}
  .mcq-section-icon{width:40px;height:40px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--bi3-bg);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:18px;flex-shrink:0;}
  .mcq-section-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif;font-size:20px;color:var(--navy)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--navy)!important;}
  .mcq-section-sub{font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);}
  .mcq-item{margin-bottom:28px;padding-bottom:28px;border-bottom:1px solid #f1f5f9;}
  .mcq-item:last-child{border-bottom:none;margin-bottom:0;padding-bottom:0;}
  .mcq-q-num{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);margin-bottom:8px;}
  .diff-tag{display:inline-block;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:100px;margin-left:8px;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#b91c1c!important;border:1px solid #fca5a5;}
  .mcq-q-text{font-size:15px!important;font-weight:600!important;color:#0f1f3d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0f1f3d!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-bottom:12px!important;}
  .predict-note{font-size:12px;font-style:italic;color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-code{background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;margin:10px 0 14px;font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;line-height:1.75;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;white-space:pre;overflow-x:auto;display:block;}
  .mcq-code .k{color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}
  .mcq-code .s{color:#f9a8d4!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#f9a8d4!important;}
  .mcq-code .n{color:#fde68a!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fde68a!important;}
  .mcq-code .c{color:#64748b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#64748b!important;font-style:italic;}
  .mcq-roman{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0 14px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;}
  .mcq-roman li{font-family:monospace;font-size:13px;color:#1e293b!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#1e293b!important;background:#f1f5f9;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 12px;}
  .mcq-roman li strong{color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-dk)!important;font-family:"DM Sans",sans-serif;margin-right:8px;}
  .mcq-options{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;margin-bottom:12px;}
  .mcq-option{display:flex!important;align-items:flex-start!important;gap:12px!important;padding:11px 14px!important;border:2px solid #e2e8f0!important;border-radius:8px!important;cursor:pointer!important;background:#f8fafc!important;font-size:14px!important;color:#374151!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#374151!important;line-height:1.5!important;text-align:left!important;width:100%!important;font-family:inherit!important;}
  .mcq-option:hover{border-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;background:var(--bi3-bg)!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect{border-color:var(--red)!important;background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-option.revealed-correct{border-color:var(--green)!important;background:#f0fdf4!important;}
  .mcq-option-letter{font-weight:700!important;color:var(--bi3)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3)!important;flex-shrink:0!important;min-width:18px!important;}
  .mcq-option.correct .mcq-option-letter{color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;}
  .mcq-option.incorrect .mcq-option-letter{color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;}
  .mcq-feedback{display:none!important;padding:12px 16px!important;border-radius:8px!important;font-size:14px!important;line-height:1.6!important;margin-top:8px!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.show{display:block!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.correct-fb{background:#f0fdf4!important;color:#14532d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#14532d!important;border:1px solid #bbf7d0!important;}
  .mcq-feedback.incorrect-fb{background:#fef2f2!important;color:#7f1d1d!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#7f1d1d!important;border:1px solid #fecaca!important;}

  /* GAME */
  .game-section{background:linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a 0%,#1e40af 100%);border-radius:14px;padding:28px;margin-bottom:40px;}
  .game-badge{display:inline-block;background:rgba(147,197,253,.15);border:1px solid rgba(147,197,253,.35);color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:100px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .game-title{font-family:"DM Serif Display",serif!important;font-size:24px!important;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;margin-bottom:4px!important;}
  .game-sub{font-size:13px!important;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-bottom:20px!important;}
  .vt-score-bar{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;margin-bottom:20px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;}
  .vt-stat{text-align:center;}
  .vt-stat-val{font-size:20px;font-weight:800;color:#fff!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important;line-height:1;}
  .vt-stat-lbl{font-size:10px;color:#94a3b8!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#94a3b8!important;margin-top:2px;}
  .vt-code-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);border-radius:12px;padding:18px 20px;margin-bottom:16px;}
  .vt-code-label{font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--bi3-lt)!important;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .vt-code-lines{font-family:monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:2;color:#e2e8f0!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#e2e8f0!important;}
  .vt-line{display:block;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:4px;white-space:pre;}
  .vt-line.hl{background:rgba(147,197,253,.2);color:#93c5fd!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#93c5fd!important;}

    <div class="lesson-objectives">
      <h2>After this lesson, you will be able to:</h2>
      <ul>
        <li><span>Explain that material created on a computer is the intellectual property of its creator and is protected by copyright</span></li>
        <li><span>Describe how creators use licenses, including Creative Commons and open source, to grant others permission to use their work under stated conditions</span></li>
        <li><span>Explain why using another person's work requires following its license and giving attribution, and why taking credit for it is plagiarism</span></li>
        <li><span>Identify material in the public domain and explain why downloading or distributing copyrighted work without permission can be illegal</span></li>
        <li><span>Apply legal and ethical reasoning to decide when a use needs permission, attribution, or neither</span></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div class="score-impact">📈 <span>Big Idea 5 (Impact of Computing) is 21 to 26 percent of the AP CSP exam, and legal and ethical questions about copyright, licensing, and attribution show up on nearly every practice test. The same rules govern the Create Performance Task, where you must cite any code or media you did not create, so this lesson protects both your score and your submission.</span>
</div>
    <div class="hook-box">
      <div class="hook-label">💡 Think about this first</div>
      <p>You find a perfect photo for your app with a quick image search, and you find a chunk of code on a public forum that does exactly what you need. Both are sitting right there on the open Internet, free to view. Does the fact that you can see and download something mean you are allowed to use it in your own project, and how would you even know?</p>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>You Made It, You Own It: Intellectual Property</h2>
      <p>When you create something original on a computer, a drawing, a song, a photo, a paragraph, or a program, that material is your <strong>intellectual property</strong>. It belongs to you as its creator. The moment an original creative work is fixed in a usable form, <strong>copyright</strong> automatically protects it. You do not have to register it or add a symbol for copyright to apply. Copyright gives the owner control over how the work is used, including who may copy it, share it, or build on it.</p>
      <p>The flip side is the part students forget: <strong>other people's work is also their intellectual property</strong>. A photo you find online, a song clip, a block of code on a forum, all of it was created by someone who owns the copyright by default. Being able to see or download a work does not transfer any rights to you. Using it in your own project without permission can violate the owner's rights and can be illegal.</p>
      <div class="callout-exam">
        <div class="callout-exam-label">🎯 What the exam rewards</div>
        <p>When a question involves reusing someone else's photo, music, or code, the exam wants you to check the <strong>license and give attribution</strong>, not to assume the work is free. The strongest answers respect the creator's ownership and follow the stated conditions for use.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Licenses: Permission With Conditions</h2>
      <p>Copyright would make sharing impossible if there were no way to grant permission, so creators use <strong>licenses</strong>. A license is the creator saying, in advance, "you may use my work if you follow these conditions." Two license systems appear constantly on the exam:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>A <strong>Creative Commons</strong> license lets a creator keep copyright while allowing others to use the work under stated conditions, such as giving <strong>attribution</strong>, using it only for <strong>non-commercial</strong> purposes, or releasing any changes under the same <strong>share-alike</strong> terms.</li>
        <li>An <strong>open source</strong> license applies to software and lets others use, <strong>modify</strong>, and share the <strong>source code</strong> under its conditions. Open source is about the freedom to read and change the code, not simply that the program is free of cost.</li>
      </ul>
      <p>A license does not mean "anything goes." If a Creative Commons image requires attribution, you must credit the creator; if it is non-commercial, you cannot use it to make money. Ignoring a condition means you are using the work outside its license, which puts you back to using it without permission.</p>
      <table class="vocab-table">
        <tr>
<th>Term</th>
<th>What it allows</th>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Copyright</strong></td>
<td>Automatic protection for an original work; only the owner may copy, share, or build on it unless they grant permission.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Creative Commons</strong></td>
<td>Reuse of a copyrighted work under conditions the creator chooses, such as attribution, non-commercial, or share-alike.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Open source</strong></td>
<td>Freedom to use, modify, and share software source code under the license's stated conditions.</td>
</tr>
        <tr>
<td><strong>Public domain</strong></td>
<td>No copyright applies, so the work is free for anyone to use for any purpose without permission.</td>
</tr>
      </table>

        </div>

      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>Attribution, Plagiarism, and the Public Domain</h2>
      <p>Nearly every license that lets you reuse a work asks for one thing in return: <strong>attribution</strong>, meaning you credit the original creator. Attribution is both a legal condition and an ethical duty. When you present someone else's work as your own, whether it is a paragraph, an image, or a block of code, that is <strong>plagiarism</strong>. Plagiarism is an ethical violation even when you technically had permission to use the work, because the wrong is claiming credit you did not earn.</p>
      <p>Some material carries no copyright at all and sits in the <strong>public domain</strong>. This includes works whose copyright has expired and works released to the public deliberately. Public domain material is genuinely free to use for any purpose without permission, though crediting the source is still good practice and honest. Knowing whether something is public domain, licensed, or fully copyrighted is the difference between a legal reuse and an illegal one.</p>
      <div class="callout-trap">
        <div class="callout-trap-label">⚠ Common trap</div>
        <p>"It is on the Internet, so it is free to use." This is <strong>false</strong>. Most content online is copyrighted the instant it is created, and being publicly visible grants you no rights at all. Downloading or distributing a copyrighted work without permission can be illegal. You must find the license, follow its conditions, and give attribution, or confirm the work is in the public domain, before you reuse it.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="mini-ex">
        <div class="mini-ex-label">Quick check</div>
        <div class="mini-ex-q">A student copies three paragraphs from a website into their report and presents them as their own writing, adding no credit. The website's content is copyrighted. What best describes this?</div>
        <div class="mini-opts" id="mc-legal-2-opts">
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-legal-2','A','B','mc-legal-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">A</span> Acceptable, because the paragraphs were publicly available online</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-legal-2','B','B','mc-legal-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">B</span> Plagiarism, and a possible copyright violation, because the work was used without credit or permission</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-legal-2','C','B','mc-legal-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">C</span> Public domain use, because copying makes the text the student's property</button>
          <button class="mini-opt" onclick="miniMCQ('mc-legal-2','D','B','mc-legal-2-fb')"><span class="mini-opt-letter">D</span> Fully legal open source reuse of the paragraphs</button>
        </div>
        <div class="mini-fb" id="mc-legal-2-fb"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="lesson-section">
      <h2>How This Shows Up on the Create Performance Task and the Exam</h2>
      <p>The Create Performance Task requires you to <strong>acknowledge and cite any code or media you did not create yourself</strong>. If you borrow a code segment from a library, a tutorial, or a classmate, or use an image, sound, or font made by someone else, you must credit the source in your program or written responses. Submitting borrowed work as your own is plagiarism and violates the AP CSP policy, and it can cost you a score on the task. The safe habit is to prefer material that is in the public domain or carries a clear license, follow that license, and write down where every outside piece came from as you build.</p>
      <p>The same rules earn points on the multiple-choice section, where scenarios ask whether a use needs permission, needs attribution, or is allowed because the work is public domain. Master copyright, Creative Commons, open source, public domain, and plagiarism here, and you are protected in both places the AP exam grades you.</p>
    </div>

</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Decide which license fits the described freedoms before reading the options.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A programmer finds a code library online whose license lets anyone read the source code, change it, and redistribute the modified version, as long as the same license terms are kept. Which type of license does this describe?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q1-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','A','C','q1-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> A trademark that protects the library's name</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','B','C','q1-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> A license that places the code in the public domain and removes all conditions</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','C','C','q1-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> An open source license</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q1','D','C','q1-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> Standard copyright with no permissions granted</button>
</div>
<div id="q1-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. A trademark protects a brand identifier, not the right to read, modify, and redistribute source code.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Public domain means no conditions at all, but this license keeps a condition (the same terms must be kept), so it is not public domain.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. An open source license grants the freedom to use, modify, and share source code under stated conditions, such as keeping the same license terms.</div>
<div id="q1-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Standard copyright with no permissions would forbid modifying and redistributing the code without asking the owner.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="mcq-item" data-activity="quiz" data-item="q2">
        <div class="mcq-q-num">Question 2 of 6<span class="diff-tag">Attribution and plagiarism</span>
</div>
        <div class="predict-note">Predict what the student did wrong before you look.</div>
        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>A student uses an image released under a Creative Commons license that requires attribution. The student includes the image in a project but removes the creator's name and claims to have made the image. Which statement best describes the situation?</p></div>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q2-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','A','D','q2-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> The use is fine because Creative Commons images are always free to use however you want</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','B','D','q2-fb-B')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">B</span> The use is fine because the image was downloaded rather than sold</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','C','D','q2-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> The student only broke the law but did nothing unethical</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q2','D','D','q2-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> The student violated the license by not attributing the creator and also committed plagiarism by claiming the work</button>
</div>
<div id="q2-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Creative Commons licenses come with conditions, and this one required attribution, which was not given.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Whether the image was sold is irrelevant; the license required attribution, which the student removed.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. It is both a license violation and an ethical problem, since claiming another's work as your own is plagiarism.</div>
<div id="q2-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Removing the required attribution breaks the license, and claiming the image as one's own is plagiarism, an ethical violation.</div>
      </div>

        <div class="mcq-q-text"><p>Consider these statements about material found on the Internet:</p></div>
        <ul class="mcq-roman">
          <li>
<strong>I.</strong> An original photo posted online is automatically protected by copyright, even without a copyright symbol.</li>
          <li>
<strong>II.</strong> A work in the public domain may be used by anyone for any purpose without seeking permission.</li>
          <li>
<strong>III.</strong> Because a work is publicly visible online, it is free for anyone to copy and reuse.</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="mcq-options" id="q3-options">
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q3','A','A','q3-fb-A')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">A</span> I and II only</button>

<div id="q3-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. I and II are true. III is false: public visibility grants no rights, since most online content is copyrighted.</div>

<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','C','C','q4-fb-C')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">C</span> Being able to find and download a work does not grant any right to reuse it, because it is likely still copyrighted</button>
<button class="mcq-option" onclick="checkMCQ('q4','D','C','q4-fb-D')"><span class="mcq-option-letter">D</span> The developer should have used a faster download tool</button>
</div>
<div id="q4-fb-A" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. File size is a technical detail and is not the legal or ethical flaw in the reasoning.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-B" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Indexing by search engines has nothing to do with whether the developer may reuse the song.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-C" class="mcq-feedback correct-fb">Correct. Access is not permission. Most works online are copyrighted, so the developer must check the license or confirm public domain before reusing the song.</div>
<div id="q4-fb-D" class="mcq-feedback incorrect-fb">Incorrect. Download speed is irrelevant to the question of permission to reuse the work.</div>
